title: fix: evaluate ImageValidatingPolicies concurrently
author: pyd-07
head: pyd-07:fix/17275-ivpol-webhook-timeout
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a timeout issue affecting multiple `ImageValidatingPolicy` objects that match the same admission request.

Basic `ImageValidatingPolicy` objects can be aggregated into the same validating webhook. The IVPOL engine previously evaluated the matching policies sequentially, meaning a slow image verification operation in one policy could delay all subsequent policies and cause the aggregate webhook request to exceed its timeout.

This fix evaluates successfully compiled `ImageValidatingPolicy` objects concurrently while preserving existing cross-policy verification, `required` verification, error handling, and deterministic result processing.

## Related issue

Closes #17275

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.20.0`. -->

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno.

- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update the documentation.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

The relevant evaluation flow is:

```text
ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
        ↓
IVPOL webhook
        ↓
ValidateClustered()
        ↓
HandleValidating()
        ↓
evaluatePolicies()
        ↓
matching IVPOLs
        ↓
policy evaluation
````

`ImageValidatingPolicy` objects without `matchConditions`, `MatchPolicy: Exact`, or an explicit `timeoutSeconds` can be classified as basic policies and aggregated into a single validating webhook.

Previously, the IVPOL engine evaluated matching policies sequentially:

```text
IVPOL A ──┐
          │
IVPOL B ──┼──> one webhook invocation
          │
IVPOL C ──┘
                ↓
        sequential evaluation
                ↓
       aggregate latency > timeout
                ↓
       context deadline exceeded
```

This is particularly problematic for `ImageValidatingPolicy` because evaluation can perform image-related operations involving external registry and verification work.

The evaluation flow is now split into three phases:

1. **Sequential compilation**

   All matching policies are compiled before evaluation begins. CEL compilation remains sequential because an initial attempt to parallelize the complete compile-and-evaluate loop exposed concurrent access to shared CEL compiler/parser state.

2. **Concurrent policy evaluation**

   Successfully compiled policies are evaluated concurrently. This allows a policy waiting on image verification to make progress independently of other matching policies.

3. **Sequential result processing**

   Evaluation results are stored by their original policy index and processed sequentially. This preserves deterministic result handling and avoids concurrent writes to the response map.

The existing shared `ImageVerificationResults` is retained so that verification evidence can continue to be shared across policies.

`required` verification is also enforced only after all policies have completed evaluation. A policy evaluated later may provide verification evidence required by another policy, so enforcing `required` independently inside each concurrent evaluation would change the existing behavior.

### Regression Test

A regression test was added which creates multiple matching `ImageValidatingPolicy` objects and uses a blocking image context.

The test verifies that when one policy is blocked during image evaluation, another matching policy can still begin image evaluation before the first policy is released.

The test therefore fails with the previous sequential implementation and passes with the concurrent implementation.

The engine test also passes with the Go race detector:

```text
go test -race ./pkg/cel/policies/ivpol/engine -count=1
```

## Proof Manifests

<!--
No proof manifests are included. The regression is covered by a unit test
at the IVPOL engine level because the change concerns internal evaluation
scheduling rather than a new policy syntax or configuration option.
-->

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).
- [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.
- [ ] This is a feature and I have added CLI tests that are applicable.
- [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is <replace>.
- [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and
  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

## Further Comments

Adding a `matchConditions` entry such as:

```yaml
matchConditions:
  - name: force-unique-webhook
    expression: "true"
```

can appear to resolve the timeout because it changes the policy's webhook classification and therefore the webhook topology. However, this does not address the underlying sequential evaluation behavior.

The fix instead retains the existing webhook aggregation behavior and makes the expensive policy evaluation phase concurrent.

This change is also aligned with the motivation described in #15229, which identified sequential policy evaluation as a scalability and latency concern for both `ValidatingPolicy` and `ImageValidatingPolicy`.

The implementation intentionally does not make CEL compilation concurrent. An initial attempt to parallelize the complete compile-and-evaluate loop exposed a race in CEL compilation. Compilation was therefore separated from evaluation so that only the evaluation phase is parallelized.

This approach preserves the existing cross-policy `required` verification behavior and deterministic result processing.



<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Policy checks are now evaluated concurrently, improving processing efficiency when multiple image-validation policies are configured.
  * Results are processed consistently and deterministically, regardless of evaluation timing.
  * Errors are reported individually for the affected policy checks, making validation issues easier to identify.
  * Pending required checks now preserve the relevant policy context through evaluation.

title: fix(policy): resolve subresource triggers in mutating policy matchConstraints
author: anushkagupta200615-jpg
head: anushkagupta200615-jpg:fix-subresource-trigger-resolution
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug where `MutatingPolicy` failed to trigger when declaring subresources (such as `pods/status`) under `matchConstraints.resourceRules[].resources`. When evaluating trigger resources, `PolicyController` attempted to map the raw subresource string to a Kind via `RESTMapper.KindFor()`, which failed with `no matches for /v1, Resource=pods/status` because subresources do not have independent Kinds in discovery. 

This change strips the subresource suffix before the GVR→GVK mapping so the parent resource Kind (`Pod`) is properly resolved, while keeping the full declared subresource path in the GVR for trigger matching.

## Related issue

Closes #17392

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.14.0

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. 
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

- In `pkg/policy/gpol.go` (`getGpolTriggers`), derive `baseResource` by stripping any subresource suffix (e.g. `pods/status` -> `pods`) prior to calling `pc.restMapper.KindFor()`.
- Retain the full `gvr` containing the subresource name so that trigger evaluation matches against declared subresource rules.
- Add regression test `TestGetGpolTriggers_SubresourceTrigger` in `pkg/policy/gpol_test.go`.

title: feat(helm): protect legacy policy CRDs from Helm prune with resource-policy keep
author: thisis-manan
head: thisis-manan:feat/issue-17489-helm-resource-policy-keep
action: Keep on main — requires human confirmation (migration-grace, see §1.5)
body:
## Explanation

This PR addresses a data-loss risk during the Kyverno 1.20 legacy-policy migration. The legacy `kyverno.io` policy CRDs (`ClusterPolicy`, `Policy`, `CleanupPolicy`, `ClusterCleanupPolicy`, and the legacy `PolicyException`) now carry the `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` annotation, so a Helm uninstall or chart removal will **not** implicitly delete these live CRDs and garbage-collect users' existing policy resources during the migration grace window. This is a **change** to existing Helm chart behavior.

## Related issue

Closes #17489

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.20.0

## Documentation (required for features)

User-facing behavior (Helm uninstall no longer removes legacy CRDs) is documented in the chart README (`charts/kyverno/README.md`), including how to delete the CRDs manually after migration is verified. Happy to raise a website docs PR if maintainers prefer.

## What type of PR is this

/kind feature

title: fix(helm): allow OpenShift to assign container UID and GID
author: ANAMASGARD
head: ANAMASGARD:fix-16160-openshift-security-context
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

  Kyverno’s Helm chart currently assigns UID and GID `65534` to its containers. OpenShift namespaces use cluster-assigned UID ranges, so the `restricted-v2` Security Context Constraint rejects Kyverno pods when `65534` is outside the namespace’s permitted range.

  This bug fix removes the fixed UID and GID defaults, allowing OpenShift and other platforms to assign an appropriate non-root identity.
  Existing security hardening, including `runAsNonRoot`, dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystems, disabled privilege escalation,  and `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, remains unchanged.

  ## Related issue

  Closes #16160

  ## Milestone of this PR

  To be assigned by maintainers.

  ## Documentation (required for features)

  Not applicable as this is a Helm chart bug fix rather than a new feature. The generated chart README and ArtifactHub release note are updated in this PR.

  ## What type of PR is this

  /kind bug

  ## Proposed Changes

  - Remove the default `runAsUser: 65534` and `runAsGroup: 65534` values from:
    - CRD migration hooks
    - Helm test pods
    - webhook cleanup hooks
    - admission controller init and main containers
    - background controller
    - cleanup controller
    - reports controller
  - Remove the fixed UID/GID from the `wait-for-reports-server` readiness init container.
  - Preserve all existing container security hardening.
  - Preserve support for explicitly configured `runAsUser` and `runAsGroup` values.
  - Regenerate the Helm chart README and installation manifest.
  - Add an ArtifactHub release-note entry.

  This deliberately avoids OpenShift-specific detection or conditional template logic. When no UID is specified, OpenShift can assign one
  from the namespace’s permitted SCC range. Other Kubernetes platforms continue to enforce non-root execution through `runAsNonRoot: true`
  and the container image’s non-root default user.

  ### Proof Manifests

  The default rendered security context no longer specifies a fixed UID or GID:

  ```yaml
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    privileged: false
    allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
    readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
    capabilities:
      drop:
        - ALL
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  ```

  Explicit UID/GID configuration remains supported. The following test-only values were used to approximate an OpenShift-assigned high UID:

  ```yaml
  crds:
    migration:
      securityContext: &highUid
        runAsUser: 1000770000
        runAsGroup: 1000770000

  test:
    securityContext: *highUid

  webhooksCleanup:
    securityContext: *highUid

  admissionController:
    initContainer:
      securityContext: *highUid
    container:
      securityContext: *highUid

  backgroundController:
    securityContext: *highUid

  cleanupController:
    securityContext: *highUid

  reportsController:
    securityContext: *highUid
  ```

  Local verification performed:

  - Default Helm render:
    - 13 Kyverno-owned container contexts omitted `runAsUser` and `runAsGroup`.
    - All existing security-hardening fields remained present.
  - Reports-server-enabled render:
    - 17 Kyverno-owned contexts passed.
    - All four `wait-for-reports-server` init containers omitted fixed UID/GID values.
  - Explicit override render:
    - All 13 configurable contexts rendered UID/GID `1000770000`.
  - All 17 chart CI values files passed `helm lint`.
  - Relevant Helm documentation and installation-manifest generation was run twice and produced an identical diff.
  - Kubernetes v1.33.7 Kind cluster with Restricted Pod Security:
    - All four Kyverno controller deployments became Available at UID/GID `1000770000`.
    - All five Helm tests passed.
    - The CRD migration Job was observed and completed successfully at UID/GID `1000770000`.
    - Both pre-delete cleanup Jobs completed successfully at UID/GID `1000770000`.
    - Helm uninstall completed successfully.

  An actual OpenShift cluster was not available for local testing. Kind Restricted Pod Security and the arbitrary high-UID test validate runtime compatibility, but do not emulate OpenShift SCC identity injection.


  The full repository-wide `make codegen-all` target was not completed locally because the installed `client-wrapper` tool was stale and  refreshing it required unavailable network downloads. The generators relevant to this Helm change completed successfully and were verified as idempotent.

When the `--exceptionNamespace` flag is set on the admission controller to restrict where `PolicyException` resources can be defined, creating CEL `PolicyException` resources (`policies.kyverno.io`) outside the designated namespace silently bypassed this restriction. title: fix(exceptions): honour expiresAt in the CEL policy providers
author: itsvishalyadav
head: itsvishalyadav:fix/expired-polex-providers
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

While looking at how the CEL policy engines pick up PolicyExceptions, I noticed that `spec.expiresAt` is only honoured on the admission path.

`PolicyException.spec.expiresAt` is documented as retiring an exception, and the API type ships an `IsExpired()` helper for exactly that. #16299 wired that helper into `ListExceptions` in `pkg/cel/engine/exception.go` and into the admission policy generator, but the CEL policy providers never call `ListExceptions`. Each of them carries its own copy of the `spec.policyRefs` matching loop, and none of those copies looks at `expiresAt`.

Those providers are what the background scanner and the CLI use. In `pkg/controllers/report/background/controller.go` the exception list comes from `utils.FetchCELPolicyExceptions`, which lists every exception with no expiry filter and hands the whole slice to `ScanResource`, and that builds the vpol, mpol and ivpol providers from it. The `kyverno apply` and `kyverno test` commands build the same providers the same way.

The result is that admission and reporting disagree about the same object. Once an exception expires the webhook correctly stops honouring it and starts denying the resource again, but the background scan keeps attaching it, so the PolicyReport still reports skip and `kyverno apply` in CI still passes. Anyone using `expiresAt` to hand out a time boxed exception ends up with reports and CI that keep trusting it forever.

This PR fixes the issue by extracting the exception selection into a single `engine.MatchExceptions` helper that skips expired exceptions, and using it from all five providers so every path agrees on which exceptions are still live.

## Related issue

Fixes #17473

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone TBD

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- `pkg/cel/engine/exception.go`: add `MatchExceptions`, which selects the exceptions matching a policy kind and name and skips expired and nil entries. `ListExceptions` now delegates to it, so its behaviour is unchanged.
- `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/provider.go`, `mpol/engine/provider.go`, `ivpol/engine/provider.go`, `dpol/engine/provider.go` and `gpol/engine/fetch.go`: replace the duplicated `spec.policyRefs` loop with `engine.MatchExceptions`, which is what brings the expiry check to the background scan and CLI paths.
- Tests covering the helper directly, plus provider level tests for ivpol and gpol showing an expired exception is no longer attached.

### Proof Manifests

Not applicable, this is covered by unit tests.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).
- [ ] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.
- [ ] This is a feature and I have added CLI tests that are applicable.
- [x] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is release-1.19.
- [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and
  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

## Further Comments

I went with one shared helper rather than adding the same `IsExpired()` line five times, because the duplicated matching loop is what let the expiry check drift out of sync in the first place. Keeping the selection in one place means the next change to it lands everywhere at once.

Every new test fails on main without the change. 1.19 has the same gap and I have ticked the cherry pick box for it. 1.18 and earlier are not affected because `expiresAt` does not exist there.

title: fix(webhook): fix concurrent map race in expressionCache.GetOrCompile
author: tendinginfinity24
head: tendinginfinity24:fix/expression-cache-race
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

expressionCache.GetOrCompile passed the live preexistingExpressions map directly into CompileMatchConditionsWithKubernetesEnv with no lock held. Concurrently, policy-informer callbacks (AddExpression) write to the same map under c.mu.Lock(). The Go race detector — and in production, the Go runtime — detects this as a concurrent map read and write, causing a fatal error: concurrent map read and map write panic on the elected leader replica (the only replica that runs the reconcile-driven read path).
This is a bug fix. No user-facing behavior is changed.

## Related issue

Closes #17463

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.19.1

## Documentation (required for features)

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

GetOrCompile had a lock gap: it released c.mu.RLock() after checking isPreexisting, then called CompileMatchConditionsWithKubernetesEnv passing the live c.preexistingExpressions map with no lock held. validateMatchConditionsExpression reads that map at matchconditions.go:68 to determine the CEL environment type — a plain map read with no synchronization.

The fix takes a defensive copy (snapshot) of preexistingExpressions while the read lock is still held, then passes the snapshot (thread-local, unshared) to the compiler. No lock is needed during compilation itself.

A secondary improvement: after acquiring the write lock to store the result, GetOrCompile now re-checks whether another goroutine already stored the same entry during compilation and returns the existing one if so, avoiding a redundant overwrite.

Race confirmed on main before fix:

WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0006b6d80 by goroutine 55:
  github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/controllers/webhook.(*expressionCache).AddExpression()
      pkg/controllers/webhook/expression_cache.go:119

Previous read at 0x00c0006b6d80 by goroutine 58:
  github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/cel/compiler.validateMatchConditionsExpression()
      pkg/cel/compiler/matchconditions.go:68
  github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/controllers/webhook.(*expressionCache).GetOrCompile()
      pkg/controllers/webhook/expression_cache.go:50

After fix:

ok      github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/controllers/webhook      1.539s

To reproduce:

bash
go test -race -count=1 -run TestGetOrCompile_Race ./pkg/controllers/webhook/...

### Proof Manifests

N/A — the race is exercised entirely by the unit test; it does not require a running cluster or policy manifests. The added test (expression_cache_race_test.go) is a reliable reproducer.

The two non-leader replicas run AddExpression via informer callbacks but never hit the read path, so they never crash. title: fix(exceptions): honour the operations field when matching PolicyExceptions
author: itsvishalyadav
head: itsvishalyadav:fix/polex-operations-matching
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

`PolicyException` match blocks accept an `operations` field. The CRD exposes it and describes it as *"used to match a specific action"*, and `kyverno create exception --resource operation=CREATE` generates it. The engine never read it.

`checkResourceDescription` in `pkg/engine/utils/exceptions.go` evaluated `kinds`, `name`, `names`, `namespaces`, `annotations`, `selector` and `namespaceSelector`, but had no branch for `operations`, so the field was silently discarded. An exception scoped to a single operation applied to every operation instead.

The practical effect is that exceptions are broader than the user declared. Someone who scopes an exception to `CREATE` in order to keep enforcing a policy on `UPDATE` and `DELETE` silently gets no enforcement on those operations at all.

This is a fix of existing behavior. It only narrows exceptions that already set `operations`; exceptions that leave the field unset are unaffected.

## Related issue

Fixes #17461

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone TBD

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- Thread `policyContext.Operation()` through `checkMatchesResources` → `checkResourceFilter` → `checkResourceDescription` in `pkg/engine/utils/exceptions.go`.
- Skip an exception whose match block sets `operations` when the admission operation is not in that list.

The check mirrors rule matching in `doesResourceMatchConditionBlock` (`pkg/engine/utils/match.go`), and uses the same operation value: `pkg/engine/background.go` already passes `policyContext.Operation()` to `MatchesResourceDescription` for rules, so exception matching and rule matching now agree in every path.

An empty `operations` list keeps its current "matches any operation" meaning, so this is not a behavior change for exceptions that do not use the field.

### Proof Manifests

Given this policy and exception, `disallow-capabilities` should still be enforced on `UPDATE` and `DELETE`, and only be waived on `CREATE`:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2
kind: PolicyException
metadata:
  name: exempt-on-create-only
  namespace: default
spec:
  exceptions:
    - policyName: disallow-capabilities
      ruleNames:
        - "*"
  match:
    any:
      - resources:
          namespaces:
            - default
          operations:
            - CREATE
```

Before this change the exception applied to `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `CONNECT` alike. After it, only `CREATE` is exempted.

title: fix(webhook): guard nil Scope dereference in sortedRules to prevent controller panic
author: 7se7en72025
head: 7se7en72025:fix/webhook-nil-scope-panic
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it

The webhook controller panics with a nil pointer dereference when sorting `RuleWithOperations` entries whose `Scope` field is nil.

### Root cause

`sortedRules()` in `pkg/controllers/webhook/utils.go` unconditionally dereferences the `Scope` pointer during comparison:

```go
strings.Compare(string(*a.Scope), string(*b.Scope))
```

But [`admissionregistrationv1.Rule.Scope`](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/admissionregistration/v1#Rule) is defined as `*ScopeType` and is optional. When omitted, it defaults to nil.

### How nil Scope enters the pipeline

`CreateMatchConstraints()` in `pkg/cel/autogen/match.go` builds `RuleWithOperations` without setting `Scope`:

```go
rules = append(rules, admissionregistrationv1.NamedRuleWithOperations{
    RuleWithOperations: admissionregistrationv1.RuleWithOperations{
        Rule: admissionregistrationv1.Rule{
            APIGroups:   []string{gv.Group},
            APIVersions: []string{gv.Version},
            Resources:   sets.List(resources),
            // Scope is not set — remains nil
        },
        Operations: operations,
    },
})
```

These rules flow through the webhook generation pipeline:

```
CreateMatchConstraints()
  → buildWebhookRules()
    → buildForJSONPoliciesValidation()
      → sortedRules()
        → strings.Compare(string(*a.Scope), ...) // panic
```

### The fix

Introduces a `scopeString()` helper that safely dereferences `Scope`, treating nil as `AllScopes` (`"*"`), consistent with Kubernetes semantics where an omitted scope matches all resource scopes.

Notably, `generateRuleKey()` in the same file already handles nil Scope correctly (line 279), but `sortedRules()` did not.

**Before:**
```go
if x := strings.Compare(string(*a.Scope), string(*b.Scope)); x != 0 {
```

**After:**
```go
func scopeString(s *admissionregistrationv1.ScopeType) string {
    if s == nil {
        return string(admissionregistrationv1.AllScopes)
    }
    return string(*s)
}

// in sortedRules():
if x := strings.Compare(scopeString(a.Scope), scopeString(b.Scope)); x != 0 {
```

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/17131

## How has this been tested?

Added 7 new test cases across 2 test functions:

**`TestSortedRules_NilScope`** (3 subtests):
- `nil scope does not panic` — verifies the crash no longer occurs when sorting a nil-Scope rule against a non-nil-Scope rule
- `both nil scopes do not panic` — verifies sorting two nil-Scope rules is safe
- `nil scope treated as AllScopes sorts before Cluster and Namespaced` — verifies sort-order semantics: nil (= `"*"`) < `Cluster` < `Namespaced`

**`TestScopeString`** (4 subtests):
- nil input returns `AllScopes`
- `Namespaced`, `Cluster`, and `AllScopes` pass through correctly

All existing `TestSortedRules` tests continue to pass, confirming no change in behavior for non-nil Scope values.

```
$ go test ./pkg/controllers/webhook/... -v -count=1
PASS
ok  github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/controllers/webhook  0.207s
```

- [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.

title: fix: correct Object.metadata type in MPOL autogen
author: pyd-07
head: pyd-07:fix/mpol-autogen-object-metadata-17438
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes an issue where `MutatingPolicy` pod-controller autogen could generate invalid CEL `Object` type names for metadata fields. Policies using `Object.metadata` in an `ApplyConfiguration` mutation could therefore be rejected when applied to workload controllers such as Deployments and CronJobs, even though the same mutation worked for Pods.

The fix rewrites the capitalized `Object.metadata` type name to the appropriate pod-template metadata path during autogen, while preserving normal `object.metadata` and `oldObject.metadata` field accesses.

## Related issue

Closes #17438

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.2.3`. -->

## Documentation (required for features)

This is a bug fix and does not introduce a new feature or require documentation changes.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

The MutatingPolicy CEL autogen logic already rewrites `Object.spec`, `Object.metadata.labels`, and `Object.metadata.annotations` when generating mutations for pod controllers. However, the bare `Object.metadata` type name was not rewritten.

For example, a Deployment mutation was generated as:

```cel
Object{
  spec: Object.spec{
    template: Object.spec.template{
      metadata: Object.metadata{
        labels: Object.spec.template.metadata.labels{
          foo: "bar"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `Object.metadata` type name is invalid at that location because it does not match the generated field path. It must be:

```cel
Object.spec.template.metadata
```

This PR adds a targeted rewrite for the capitalized `Object.metadata` type name using a dedicated regular expression. The replacement uses the existing controller-specific metadata path, so nested controllers such as CronJobs correctly generate:

```cel
Object.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.metadata
```

The replacement intentionally matches only `Object.metadata`, avoiding changes to lowercase `object.metadata.*` and `oldObject.metadata.*` accesses.

### Proof Manifests

The issue was reproduced against Kyverno v1.19.0 on Kubernetes v1.35.1 using the following `MutatingPolicy`:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-label
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["pods"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  mutations:
    - patchType: ApplyConfiguration
      applyConfiguration:
        expression: |
          Object{
            metadata: Object.metadata{
              labels: Object.metadata.labels{
                foo: "bar"
              }
            }
          }
```

With Kyverno v1.19.0, the generated Deployment mutation contained `Object.metadata` and the Deployment was rejected with:

```text
type mismatch: unexpected type name "Object.metadata",
expected "Object.spec.template.metadata",
which matches field name path from root Object type
```

After applying this fix, the generated expression contains:

```cel
metadata: Object.spec.template.metadata{
  labels: Object.spec.template.metadata.labels{
    foo: "bar"
  }
}
```

The same Deployment was then successfully admitted and the mutation was applied to the Pod template:

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: repro
        foo: bar
```

Regression tests cover:

* `Object.metadata` rewriting for Deployments.
* `Object.metadata` rewriting for nested CronJobs.
* Preservation of `object.metadata.namespace`.
* Preservation of `oldObject.metadata.namespace`.

## Further Comments

The fix is intentionally limited to the MutatingPolicy CEL autogen path. It does not broaden the existing metadata replacements, avoiding unintended rewriting of lowercase CEL object field accesses.

title: fix(mpol): evaluate matchConditions during background mutateExisting evaluation
author: pujitha24
head: pujitha24:auto/issue-17411
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug: a `MutatingPolicy`/`NamespacedMutatingPolicy` that has `spec.matchConditions` set, and has background scanning / mutate-existing enabled but does **not** define an explicit `spec.targetMatchConstraints`, correctly respected `matchConditions` when mutating a resource at admission time, but ignored `matchConditions` entirely during background/mutate-existing reconciliation. This meant resources that should have been excluded by the policy's match conditions were mutated anyway once the background scan/mutate-existing controller processed them. After this fix, background/mutate-existing evaluation respects `matchConditions` exactly like admission-time evaluation does, for policies that don't define an explicit target.

## Related issue

Closes #17411

## Milestone of this PR

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno.
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`pkg/cel/policies/mpol/engine/engine.go`'s `handlePolicy` decided whether to evaluate `spec.matchConditions` or `spec.targetMatchConditions` purely based on whether the caller was the admission webhook (`Handle`, always `matchConditions`) or the background/mutate-existing controller (`Evaluate`, always `targetMatchConditions`). `targetMatchConditions` is a newer, distinct field that's only meaningful when a policy defines an explicit separate target via `spec.targetMatchConstraints` (added in #16614 to support mutating a resource other than the trigger, e.g. mutating a ConfigMap when a Deployment is created). When `targetMatchConstraints` is not set, the resource being processed during a background scan *is* the trigger itself (per the API's own doc comment: "When spec.targetMatchConstraints is not defined, Kyverno mutates existing resources matched in spec.matchConstraints"). In that case `targetMatchConditions` is always an empty slice, and an empty CEL match-condition list trivially evaluates to "match", so `matchConditions` was silently skipped during background evaluation.

The fix computes `hasExplicitTarget` from the policy's `GetTargetMatchConstraints()` (true when `ResourceRules` or `Expression` is set), and only takes the `EvaluateTarget`/`targetMatchConditions` path during background evaluation when the policy actually defines an explicit target. Otherwise it falls back to `Evaluate`/`matchConditions`, mirroring the existing fallback pattern the matcher-constraints check already uses one block above for `matchConstraints` vs. `targetMatchConstraints`. Policies that do define an explicit target (the cross-resource-target feature from #16614) are unaffected — verified by the existing `matches target constraints with trigger variables` test, which still passes.

A new regression test drives `engine.Evaluate` (the background/mutate-existing entry point) directly with a policy that has `matchConditions` but no `targetMatchConstraints`: it fails before this fix (a non-matching resource still gets mutated) and passes after (the non-matching resource is skipped, a matching one is mutated).

Note: this repo's own CI (`Unit tests`, `Go`/golangci-lint on `main`) is currently green, so no unrelated inherited failures are expected on this PR.

### Proof Manifests

The reporter's original policy is a good reproduction (from #17411): a `MutatingPolicy` with `spec.evaluation.background.enabled: true`, `spec.evaluation.mutateExisting.enabled: true`, and `spec.matchConditions` gating on an annotation, but no `spec.targetMatchConstraints`.

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: annotate-if-enabled
spec:
  evaluation:
    background:
      enabled: true
    mutateExisting:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["configmaps"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  matchConditions:
    - name: require-enabled-annotation
      expression: |-
        object.metadata.?annotations[?'example.com/enabled'].orValue('false') == 'true'
  mutations:
    - patchType: ApplyConfiguration
      applyConfiguration:
        expression: |
          Object{
            metadata: Object.metadata{
              labels: {"mutated": "true"}
            }
          }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: unmarked-cm
  namespace: default
data: {}
```

Before this fix, the background/mutate-existing controller would still add the `mutated: "true"` label to `unmarked-cm` even though it lacks the `example.com/enabled: "true"` annotation required by `matchConditions`. After this fix, it is correctly left untouched (only ConfigMaps with the annotation get mutated by the background controller), matching admission-time behavior. This exact scenario is covered by the new unit test `TestEvaluate/respects_matchConditions_during_background_mutateExisting_evaluation_when_no_explicit_target_is_defined` in `pkg/cel/policies/mpol/engine/engine_test.go`.

title: fix: correct contextSize accounting in ReplaceContextEntry
author: AftAb-25
head: AftAb-25:fix/replace-context-entry-size-leak
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
### Description

This PR fixes a bug in how Kyverno tracks context size when updating existing variables, which was causing spurious `ContextSizeLimitExceededError` failures (especially in `foreach` rules that refresh context variables per iteration).

**The issue:**
When `ReplaceContextEntry` is called, it was always adding the size of the incoming data (`len(dataRaw)`) to `ctx.contextSize`. However, it never subtracted the size of the *existing* entry that was being replaced. 
Because of this, `contextSize` only ever grew. If a `foreach` loop repeatedly refreshed a variable (like an `apiCall` result), the internal size counter would keep accumulating until it hit the 2MB default limit, even if the actual live context data was very small.

**The fix:**
- Before checking the size limit and updating the counter, we now marshal the existing entry (if one exists under that key) to determine its serialized size.
- The size limit check is now correctly performed against the net delta: `new size - old size`.
- `ctx.contextSize` is updated accurately: `(current size - old size + new size)`.

I've also added a regression test (`Test_ReplaceContextEntryDoesNotLeakSize`) that simulates replacing a context entry in a tight loop to ensure the size limit isn't falsely triggered.

### Related Issue
Fixes #17408

### Checklist
- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have added/updated tests to cover these changes.

title: fix: prevent pivot mutation in FindAndShiftReferences loop
author: AftAb-25
head: AftAb-25:fix/find-and-shift-references-pivot-mutation
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
### Description

This PR fixes a subtle bug in the variable substitution engine where multiple `anyPattern` references inside the same string would fail to shift correctly. 

**The issue:**
In `FindAndShiftReferences` (inside `vars.go`), when dealing with `anyPattern`, the code was mutating the `pivot` argument directly inside the loop:
`pivot = pivot + "/" + ruleIndex`

Because this mutated the outer loop variable, the first iteration worked fine (e.g., changing it to `"anyPattern/0"`), but any subsequent references in that same string would fail because the code would search for `"anyPattern/0"` instead of `"anyPattern"`. This resulted in the second and later paths failing to shift.

**The fix:**
I introduced a local `effectivePivot` variable scoped to the loop iteration. This ensures we don't permanently corrupt the `pivot` string for the rest of the loop.

I also added a regression test (`TestFindAndShiftReferences_AnyPatternMultipleReferences`) that checks a string with two distinct `anyPattern` references to ensure they both shift independently and correctly.

### Related Issue
Fixes #17396

title: fix(apicall): allow Service APICalls in namespaced policies
author: itsvishalyadav
head: itsvishalyadav:fix-namespaced-service-apicall
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug where Namespaced Policies fail to execute Service APICalls due to incorrect namespace path validation.

Service APICalls natively have an empty `URLPath`. In `apiCall.Fetch()`, Kyverno performs path verification for Namespaced Policies. Because `URLPath` is empty, `path.Clean("")` evaluates to `.`. The namespace validation regex fails, and Kyverno blocks the call with:
`path . does not contain a namespace segment, which is required for namespaced policies`

This PR fixes the bug by skipping the namespace check if `URLPath` is empty, allowing Service APICalls to proceed to `executeServiceCall`, which handles egress filtering separately.

Fixes #17393

- Modified `pkg/engine/apicall/apiCall.go` to skip K8s API path namespace validation when `call.APICall.URLPath == ""`.

title: fix: use dynamic APIVersion in event ObjectReferences instead of hardcoded values
author: yashrajshuklaaa
head: yashrajshuklaaa:fix/event-api-version-todo
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

Several `Info` events created by Kyverno (for background rules, cleanup policies, and policy exceptions) had their `APIVersion` hardcoded as a string literal in the event's `ObjectReference`, even though the underlying policy object already exposed a method to get its real API version. This meant that for any policy type where the actual version could legitimately differ (e.g. `kyverno.io/v2` vs `v2beta1`), the emitted Kubernetes Event could carry an inaccurate `apiVersion` field, which could confuse tooling or users inspecting `kubectl get events` output. This PR makes those fields reflect the real value dynamically instead of assuming it.

## What type of PR is this

/kind cleanup

## Proposed Changes

- In `pkg/event/events.go`, replaced hardcoded `APIVersion: "kyverno.io/v1"` / `"kyverno.io/v2"` string literals with dynamic `policy.GetAPIVersion()` / `exception.GetAPIVersion()` calls in:
  - `NewBackgroundFailedEvent`
  - `NewBackgroundSuccessEvent`
  - `NewPolicyExceptionEvents` (exception event)
  - `NewCleanupPolicyEvent`
- One occurrence in `NewPolicyExceptionEvents` (the policy level event, using `kyvernov1.PolicyInterface`) was left hardcoded, since that interface has no `GetAPIVersion()` method and is only implemented by `Policy`/`ClusterPolicy`, which are always `kyverno.io/v1`. Replaced the stale `TODO` there with a comment explaining why it's intentionally hardcoded.
- Resolves 5 instances of the same `// TODO: iirc it's not safe to assume api version is set` comment in this file.


## Further Comments

This was investigated by reading through the type definitions for `engineapi.GenericPolicy`, `engineapi.GenericException`, `kyvernov2.CleanupPolicyInterface`, and `kyvernov1.PolicyInterface` to confirm which had a working `GetAPIVersion()` method before making changes. One case (`kyvernov1.PolicyInterface`) genuinely can't be fixed the same way, so it was left as is with an explanatory comment rather than force fitting a change.

title: fix: nil pointer dereference in validation engine on UPDATE requests
author: AftAb-25
head: AftAb-25:fix/nil-dereference-validate-old-object
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
Fixes: #17354


## Description
This PR fixes a bug where the Kyverno admission controller can crash and restart due to a nil pointer dereference in the validation engine. 

## What's happening?
When processing an `UPDATE` request for an `Enforce` policy that has `allowExistingViolations: true`, the engine calls `validateOldObject`. If that errors out, the code attempts to return a skip response and calls `ruleResponse.Properties()`. 

The problem is that `ruleResponse` can easily be `nil` here (for instance, if the validation rule was empty/invalid and didn't hit the deny, pattern, or forEach blocks, or if `validateResourceWithRule` returned nil). Calling `.Properties()` on it triggers a panic.

## The Fix
Instead of calling `ruleResponse.Properties()`, I changed it to just use `v.rule.ReportProperties`. This avoids the nil dereference entirely and brings it in line with the sibling `RuleSkip` call just a few lines down (which already uses `v.rule.ReportProperties`), making things much more consistent.

Fixes #17354

title: fix(cli): propagate messageExpression errors to fail cli tests
author: smkspurti
head: smkspurti:fix/issue-15350-message-expression-error
action: Keep on main
body:
## Description

This fixes a bug in the Kyverno CLI where a runtime error during `messageExpression` CEL evaluation would silently pass a test case that expected a `fail` outcome. 

The CLI now distinguishes a `messageExpression` evaluation error from an ordinary policy rule failure, preventing the test runner from incorrectly passing a test when the expected `fail` result masks an underlying evaluation error.

### Root Cause & Architecture

Previously, when `validation.MessageExpression.ContextEval()` failed, the runtime error was immediately converted into a human-readable fallback string (e.g. `"failed to evaluate message expression: no such key..."`) and the actual `error` object was dropped. 

Because `EvaluationResult.Error` was `nil`, the engine treated this as a standard `RuleFail`. When a user's CLI test expected `result: fail`, the CLI test runner matched it and returned `PASS`, hiding the policy authoring error.

### Solution

This PR:
1. Adds a typed `MessageExpressionError` field to `EvaluationResult`.
2. Preserves the existing string fallback behavior in `EvaluationResult.Message` so the change does not alter the existing webhook-facing message behavior.
3. Propagates the structured error via `engineapi.MessageExpressionErrorKey` in the `RuleResponse` properties.
4. Updates the CLI `checkResult` logic to detect this property and fail the test, regardless of the expected rule result.

**Related to #15881.** This PR takes a structured error-propagation approach, preserving the existing human-readable message while exposing the underlying `messageExpression` evaluation error to the CLI through `RuleResponse` properties.

Fixes #15350

title: fix: prevent command injection via PR title in cherry-pick action
author: 1PoPTRoN
head: 1PoPTRoN:fix/cherry-pick-command-injection-17337
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

This is a security fix. The cherry-pick composite action was taking the PR title, target branch and merge commit and pasting them straight into a `shell: bash` block. A PR title is attacker-controlled and can be edited after merge, so a payload like `x" ; curl ... | sh ; echo "` would break out of the quoted `--title` and run arbitrary code in a job that already has a GitHub App token with `contents: write` and git credentials from `gh auth setup-git`.

No runtime behavior changes — just makes the action handle those inputs as data instead of code.

## Related issue

Closes #17337

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- maintainers will set milestone -->

## Documentation (required for features)

No docs needed — GitHub Actions fix only.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

* Move `source-pr`, `source-pr-title`, `target-branches` and `merge-commit` from `${{ inputs... }}` interpolation inside `run:` to `env:` and reference as `"$SOURCE_PR_TITLE"` etc. (quoted). This is the documented safe pattern for untrusted data in Actions.
* Quote every use: `"$TARGET_BRANCHES"`, `"$MERGE_COMMIT"`, `"$pr_branch_name"`, `"$target_branch"` — no more unquoted expansions.
* Add small defense-in-depth checks: `SOURCE_PR` must be numeric, `MERGE_COMMIT` must be 40-char hex, each branch must pass `git check-ref-format --branch`. Trim whitespace for comma-separated branches. Keeps `set -uo pipefail` without breaking `continue-on-error`.

Only file touched: `.github/actions/git/cherry-pick/action.yaml`. Callers `comment-cherry-pick.yaml` and `cherry-pick-on-merge.yaml` stay the same — they now feed safe inputs.

### Proof Manifests

No Kyverno manifests — this is a workflow fix. Local reproduction for the report:

**Before (buggy interpolation):**

```bash
TITLE='x" ; touch /tmp/pwned ; echo "'
# GitHub would template to: gh pr create --title "x" ; touch /tmp/pwned ; echo " ..."
bash -c 'echo "TITLE: x" ; touch /tmp/pwned ; echo " rest"'
ls /tmp/pwned  # exists => vulnerable
```

**After (this PR, via env):**

```bash
export SOURCE_PR_TITLE='x" ; touch /tmp/pwned ; echo "'
export SOURCE_PR=123
bash -c 'echo "$SOURCE_PR_TITLE (Cherry-pick #$SOURCE_PR)"'  # literal
ls /tmp/pwned  # no file => blocked
# same for merge-commit: "abc123; echo pwned" now rejected by ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ check
# branch "main; echo pwned" rejected by git check-ref-format
```

Verified with `bash -n` on the `run:` snippet and static check that `run:` no longer contains `${{ }}`.

- [x] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).

- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective. (shell reproduction above; no Go code change)

- [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is <replace>.
- [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and
  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

## Further Comments

I kept the fix minimal on purpose — one file, same `env:` pattern already used elsewhere in the repo (`comment-cherry-pick.yaml:113` does `COMMENT_BODY` via `env:`). Validation is intentionally strict but matches real GitHub data (numeric PR, 40-hex SHA, valid branch name per git rules). If maintainers prefer looser validation I can drop it and keep just the `env:` + quoting, which alone fixes the injection.

Suggested follow-up: add `actionlint` with the command-injection check to CI so `${{ }}` in `run:` gets caught automatically.

## Description

This PR resolves #17158 by adding full support for `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` (`nvpol`) resources in the `admissionpolicy-generator` controller (`pkg/controllers/admissionpolicygenerator`).

### Root Cause
When `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` (`nvpol`) was added under `policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1`, `nvpolInformer` was passed to `NewController` and stored in `c.nvpolLister`, but informer event handler registration (`controllerutils.AddEventHandlersT`), reconcile key dispatching, and status updates for `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` were omitted in `admissionpolicygenerator`.

### Key Changes
1. **Informer Event Handler Registration (`controller.go`):** Added `AddEventHandlersT` for `nvpolInformer` in `NewController` to enqueue `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` events.
2. **Event Handling & Enqueuing (`vpol.go`):** Updated `addVP`, `updateVP`, `deleteVP`, and `enqueueVP` to accept `policiesv1beta1.ValidatingPolicyLike`. Enqueues keys with prefix `"NamespacedValidatingPolicy/"` when `GetNamespace()` is non-empty.
3. **Reconciler Dispatch & Status Updates (`controller.go`, `utils.go`, `generate-vap.go`):**
   - Added `getNamespacedValidatingPolicy` lister helper in `utils.go`.
   - Added `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` branch in `reconcile()` to fetch the resource, wrap it with `engineapi.NewNamespacedValidatingPolicy`, and invoke `handleVAPGeneration`.
   - Added `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` status update branch in `updatePolicyStatus()`.
   - Updated VAP name construction for namespaced validating policies (`nvpol-<namespace>-<name>`).
4. **VAP Builder (`pkg/admissionpolicy/builder.go`):** Updated `BuildValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and `BuildValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` to use `policy.AsValidatingPolicyLike()` so spec constraints, validations, and binding actions are extracted for both cluster-scoped and namespaced validating policies.
5. **Unit Tests (`vpol_test.go`):** Added unit tests covering event handler functions and key enqueuing logic for `NamespacedValidatingPolicy`.

title: fix: preserve MutatingPolicy reinvocation policy
author: pyd-07
head: pyd-07:fix/mpol-reinvocation-policy
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug where `MutatingPolicy` webhooks are registered with `reinvocationPolicy: Never`.

As a result, when another mutating webhook modifies a resource after the `MutatingPolicy` webhook has already executed, the `MutatingPolicy` is not reinvoked and therefore does not see or process those later changes.

The generated `MutatingPolicy` webhooks are now registered with `reinvocationPolicy: IfNeeded`, allowing Kubernetes to reinvoke them when subsequent mutations require it.

## Related issue

Closes #17282

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.19.1` -->

## Documentation (required for features)

This is a bug fix and does not introduce a new feature or require documentation changes.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`MutatingPolicy` webhooks generated by Kyverno were not setting `ReinvocationPolicy`.

When the field is omitted, Kubernetes uses `Never`, which prevents the `MutatingPolicy` webhook from being called again after another mutating webhook changes the resource.

This PR explicitly sets:

```go
ReinvocationPolicy: &ifNeeded,
```

on generated `MutatingPolicy` webhooks.

A regression test was added to verify that the generated `MutatingPolicy` webhook configuration contains:

```yaml
reinvocationPolicy: IfNeeded
```

The behavior was also verified against a live Kubernetes cluster using a second mutating webhook which adds a container after the initial Kyverno mutation. The newly added container was subsequently processed by the `MutatingPolicy`, confirming that reinvocation occurs as expected.

### Proof Manifests

The live reproduction used:

* A `MutatingPolicy` which rewrites container image registries.
* A separate mutating webhook which adds a new container.
* The generated Kyverno `MutatingPolicy` webhook configured with `reinvocationPolicy: IfNeeded`.

The resulting resource demonstrated that the container added by the later webhook was also processed by the `MutatingPolicy`:

```text
main            registry.example.com/library/nginx:1.25
later-webhook   registry.example.com/library/busybox:1.36
```

The generated webhook configuration was verified to contain:

```text
mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail    IfNeeded    /mpol/rewrite-image-registry
```

title: fix: recompute and retry mutate existing on target conflict
author: ranyhb
head: ranyhb:fix/mutate-existing-retry-on-conflict
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

When several trigger resources point at the same target resource, `mutate` rules with `targets` lose most of their mutations. The background controller issued a single update using the resourceVersion from its own read, so every writer but one hit a conflict, and once the UpdateRequest exhausted its three requeues the mutation was dropped — no policy report, no event, only a `failed to update target resource` line in the controller log.

This is a fix to existing behaviour. Conflicts are now recomputed and retried, so concurrent triggers against one target converge instead of silently dropping writes.

## Related issue

Closes #17284

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- maintainers -->

## Documentation (required for features)

Not a user-facing behaviour or API change — it removes silent write loss. Happy to raise a website PR if maintainers would like this called out in the mutate-existing docs.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`k8s.io/client-go/util/retry` is already used elsewhere in the repo (`pkg/controllers/policystatus`, `pkg/controllers/webhook`, `pkg/globalcontext/externalapi`), so this follows the existing pattern.

- The engine call and the target update are wrapped in `retry.RetryOnConflict`. **The engine call has to be inside the retry**: a patch may be derived from the target's current content, so replaying the previously computed patch against a newer resourceVersion would overwrite the other writer rather than merge with it. Recomputing re-loads the target and re-evaluates any `target.*` context.
- Applying rule responses moves into `applyMutations`, which returns a conflict to the caller and collects every other outcome. That keeps a retried attempt from duplicating errors or events, and reports are emitted once the retry settles rather than per attempt.
- No API change, no new flag, no behaviour change other than writes no longer being lost.

Two alternatives I considered and did not take, in case maintainers prefer one — happy to switch:

1. Serialize by target identity inside the controller. Deterministic rather than probabilistic, but only covers writers in this process.
2. Key the UpdateRequest workqueue by target instead of by UpdateRequest name, so client-go's existing per-key serialization does the work. Cleanest, but a much larger change.

## Proof Manifests

Conformance test added at `test/conformance/chainsaw/mutate/clusterpolicy/standard/existing/concurrent-triggers-shared-target/` — twenty triggers, one shared target, each patch derived from the target's own content:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: register-triggers-on-shared-target
spec:
  rules:
  - name: register-trigger
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - ConfigMap
          namespaces:
          - shared-target-ns
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              register: "true"
    context:
    - name: registered
      variable:
        jmesPath: "join(',', sort([ split(target.data.registered, ',')[?@ != '' && @ != '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}'], ['{{ request.object.metadata.name }}'] ] | []))"
    mutate:
      mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
      targets:
      - apiVersion: v1
        kind: ConfigMap
```

title: fix(pkg/policy): use RetryOnConflict for unlabelDownstream
author: vishalmore90
head: vishalmore90:fix-issue-17278
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
### Context
Fixes #17278

During policy evaluation, `unlabelDownstream` removes tracking labels from generated resources when the parent policy/rule is updated or deleted. Previously, this used a direct `UpdateResource` on the object originally fetched by `ListResource`. If the generated resource was modified concurrently (e.g., by another controller updating its status), the Kubernetes API Server would reject the label update with a `409 Conflict`. Because this error was not retried, the generated resource was permanently orphaned and retained its Kyverno tracking labels.

### Changes Made
*   Wrapped the read-modify-write operation inside `unlabelDownstream` in `pkg/policy/generate.go` with `retry.RetryOnConflict`.
*   Added an explicit `GetResource` step inside the retry loop to always fetch the latest `ResourceVersion`.
*   Added nil-safety guards for `GetLabels()` and `apierrors.IsNotFound` to cleanly exit if the resource was deleted concurrently.

title: fix(gpol): re-register downstream UID in metadataCache after recreation
author: tendinginfinity24
head: tendinginfinity24:bug/generatingPolicy
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

When a GeneratingPolicy with synchronize: enabled: true generates a downstream resource, Kyverno watches that resource and recreates it if a user deletes it. However, this only worked for the first deletion. Any subsequent deletion left the resource permanently absent until the next background scan.

The root cause: when Kyverno recreates a deleted resource, Kubernetes assigns it a new UID. The handleAdd event handler — which receives the watch.Added event for the recreated resource — was a no-op. It never registered the new UID in metadataCache. On the next deletion, handleDelete looked up the new UID, found nothing in the cache, and silently skipped recreation.

This PR fixes handleAdd to detect recreated Kyverno-managed resources by their labels, remove the stale dead-UID entry, and register the new UID so subsequent deletions are handled correctly.

## Related issue

Closes #17265

## Milestone of this PR

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

handleAdd in pkg/background/gpol/dynamic_watcher.go previously contained only a log statement. It now:

Returns early for resources not managed by Kyverno (no-op for unrelated events)
Returns early if the UID is already in the cache (first-time creation already registered by SyncWatchers)
For a recreated resource — same name, namespace, and policy label but new UID — removes the stale cache entry keyed by the old dead UID and inserts a fresh entry keyed by the new UID

### Proof Manifests

# Kubernetes resource

```yaml

kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: sync-test
spec:
  evaluation:
    synchronize:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['']
        apiVersions: ['v1']
        operations: ['CREATE', 'UPDATE']
        resources: ['namespaces']
  variables:
    - name: nsName
      expression: 'object.metadata.name'
  generate:
    - template:
        interpolate: cel
        value: |
          apiVersion: v1
          kind: ConfigMap
          metadata:
            name: sync-test-cm
            namespace: (( variables.nsName ))
          data:
            key: value
```

# Trigger namespace:

```yaml
metadata:
  name: sync-test-ns
```

kubectl delete cm sync-test-cm -n sync-test-ns
kubectl get cm sync-test-cm -n sync-test-ns   # must exist

# Second deletion — failed before this fix, succeeds after
kubectl delete cm sync-test-cm -n sync-test-ns
kubectl get cm sync-test-cm -n sync-test-ns   # must exist

title: fix: fallback to direct client lookup for secrets in namespaces not covered by informers
author: waterWang
head: waterWang:fix-imagepullsecrets-pod-namespace-fallback
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

After the image verification credential refactoring in #16439, Kyverno migrated from direct `SecretInterface` access to informer-backed listers for looking up registry credentials. The `multiLister` only creates informers for:

1. Kyverno's own namespace
2. Namespaces parsed from the controller's `--imagePullSecrets` flag

When a Pod specifies `spec.imagePullSecrets` pointing to a Secret in a namespace that is not covered by either of the above, the lister returns an empty `secretNamespaceLister` that always returns `NotFound`. The Secret is silently skipped, and the registry responds with `UNAUTHORIZED`.

This is a regression from the pre-#16439 behavior where `SecretInterface` could access Secrets in any namespace (Kyverno's default RBAC grants `get/list/watch secrets` cluster-wide).

## Fix

Two changes in `cmd/internal/`:

1. **`lister.go`** — `multiLister.Secrets(ns)` now falls back to a `directSecretNamespaceLister` that uses the Kubernetes API directly when no informer exists for the requested namespace. This is safe because:
   - Kyverno's default RBAC (shown in the issue) already grants cluster-wide Secret access
   - The fallback is per-request, not a global informer (which would be a bigger permission ask)
   - A 10s timeout prevents hanging on unavailable namespaces

2. **`registry.go`** — passes the `kubernetes.Interface` client to `multiLister` so it can perform the fallback lookup.

## Related issues

Fixes #17257

## Release notes

```release-note
fix: restore imagePullSecrets lookup for Pod-specified secrets in namespaces not covered by the controller's informers
```

title: fix(report): prevent nil pointer panic in IsPolicyReportable for typed nil policies
author: vishalmore90
head: vishalmore90:fix/report-typed-nil-is-policy-reportable
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`IsPolicyReportable` in `pkg/utils/report/create_ephemeral.go` guards
against nil inputs with `pol == nil`. In Go, this check only catches a
**bare nil interface**. When a concrete typed nil (e.g.
`(*kyvernov1.ClusterPolicy)(nil)`) is assigned to a `metav1.Object`
interface, the interface value is **not nil** - it carries type metadata
but a nil data pointer. The existing guard passes through silently, and
the immediately following `pol.GetLabels()` call panics with a nil
pointer dereference at runtime.

This function is called from 10 production sites across webhook
handlers, background controllers, and the mutation pipeline - all of
which pass policy interfaces that could be typed nils.

**Fix:** use `reflect.ValueOf(pol).IsNil()` guarded by a
`Kind() == reflect.Ptr` check. This is the canonical Go pattern for
catching typed nils and is already established in this codebase at
`pkg/background/common/labels.go:42` (`MutateLabelsSet`).

Fixes #17256

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #17256

## Changes

### pkg/utils/report/create_ephemeral.go

Added `"reflect"` import and updated the nil guard:

    -    if pol == nil { // invalid behavior
    +    if pol == nil || (reflect.ValueOf(pol).Kind() == reflect.Ptr && reflect.ValueOf(pol).IsNil()) {

### pkg/utils/report/create_ephemeral_test.go (new file)

Six unit tests covering:
- bare nil interface -> false
- typed nil *ClusterPolicy -> false  (the panic case)
- typed nil *Policy -> false
- valid policy, no exclude label -> true
- valid policy with reports.kyverno.io/disabled label -> false
- valid policy with empty labels map -> true

- [x] No API types, CRDs, or generated code were modified

title: [Bug] Fix CEL policy reconcilers to correctly handle cache invalidation on compilation failure
author: itsvishalyadav
head: itsvishalyadav:fix-cel-reconciler-cache
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

In the CEL engine, the `vpol` (ValidatingPolicy) and `mpol` (MutatingPolicy) reconcilers failed to properly handle compilation errors during reconciliation. If a policy or its autogenerated variants failed to compile, the reconcilers aborted early and returned without updating the in-memory cache (`r.policies`).

For `vpol`, the error was swallowed entirely, leading to a silent failure where the old version of the policy continued to be enforced by the engine without any indication to the user. For `mpol`, returning the error caused an infinite requeue loop without fixing the cache state.

This PR fixes the behavior by:
1. **Base policy compilation failure**: Explicitly deleting the policy from the cache, logging the error, and returning `nil` to prevent an infinite requeue for a deterministic compilation failure.
2. **Autogenerated policy compilation failure**: Logging the error and continuing the loop instead of aborting the entire reconciliation, allowing the valid base policy to still be cached and enforced.

## Related issue

Fixes #17254

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone TBD

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- Modified `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/reconciler.go` to delete from cache on base policy compilation failure and `continue` on autogenerated policy failure.
- Modified `pkg/cel/policies/mpol/engine/reconciler.go` to delete from cache and return `nil` on base policy compilation failure, and `continue` on autogenerated policy failure. Added the `logging` package import.

title: fix: evaluate validate.deny on image-verify cache hit (#17173)
author: waterWang
head: waterWang:fix-17173-cache-hit-skip-validate-deny
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #17173: when the image-verify cache is hot, `validate.deny` conditions are silently skipped because the cache-hit path returns `RulePass("verified from cache")` without ever calling `verifyImage()` → `verifyAttestations()` → `validate()`.

### Root cause

The cache key (`generateKey()`) captures only policy identity (UID + ResourceVersion), rule name, and image reference. It does **not** capture live context data (ConfigMaps, API calls) or `request.object` fields that `validate.deny.conditions` may reference. On a cache hit, the engine returned `RulePass` without evaluating the deny block, so a rule like

```yaml
validate:
  deny:
    conditions:
      all:
        - key: "{{ toggle.data.deny }}"
          operator: Equals
          value: "true"
```

silently degraded to "always pass" for the entire cache TTL (default 1h) once the image was cached.

### Fix

In the cache-hit branch of `Verify()`: if the rule has `HasValidateImageVerification()` (i.e. it carries a `validate.deny` block), still run `iv.validate(imageVerify, ctx)` before returning a response. Cryptographic re-verification is correctly skipped (image content is immutable per digest), but deny evaluation is now performed on every admission, exactly as it would be on a cache miss.

### What is NOT changed

- The cache-hit path for rules without `validate.deny` is unaffected (same `RulePass` as before).
- The cache-miss path is unchanged.
- The cryptographic re-verification on cache hit is still correctly skipped (the `verifyImage()` → `verifyAttestors()` / `verifyAttestations()` chain is not duplicated).

This PR restores that behavior for negative resource-diff tests specifically, without reintroducing the bug that the 1.18 change fixed (rule-status mismatches, e.g. an expected-fail validation that actually passed, must still fail the suite).

## What type of PR is this

## Proposed Changes

`checkResult` in `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/command.go` returns one of three failure reasons: a resource-content mismatch (`"Resource diff"`), a file load/parse error (`"Resource error"`), or a rule-status mismatch (`"Want X, got Y"`). #15361 removed a blanket rescue (`success := ok || (!ok && test.Result == "fail")`) that had been masking real status-mismatch failures, but that removal also dropped the legitimate case: a `patchedResources`/`generatedResources` diff mismatch where the test author expects `fail`.

This PR:
- Names the resource-diff reason as a constant, `reasonResourceDiff`, and returns it from the three diff branches in `checkResult`.
- Adds `isExpectedFailure(ok, reason, test)`, which rescues a failure to a pass only when it is a resource-diff mismatch (`reason == reasonResourceDiff`) **and** the test declares `result: fail`. A rule-status mismatch or a resource load/parse error is never rescued, so the #15361 fix for status mismatches is preserved.
- Applies the rescue at the three `printTestResult` call sites in `output.go` that call `checkResult` (mutation/validation, generated resources, and target resources). The `checkRuleResultOnly` path (Generation rules with no generated resources) is intentionally left untouched, since it never returns `reasonResourceDiff`.

title: fix(ivpol): honor insecureIgnoreTlog/insecureIgnoreSCT in attestation verification
author: pujitha24
head: pujitha24:auto/issue-17109
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This is a bug fix. `ImageValidatingPolicy` cosign attestors expose an `insecureIgnoreTlog`/`insecureIgnoreSCT` escape hatch on `ctlog` so that keyed/KMS-signed material can be verified in air-gapped setups with no public Rekor transparency log. That escape hatch worked for image *signatures* (`VerifyImageSignature`) but was missing from the attestation path (`VerifyAttestationSignature`), so offline keyed attestation verification (e.g. verifying a signed SBOM) always failed with `cosign bundle verification failed`, even when the attestation was cryptographically valid and its signature had already been checked.

## Related issue

Closes #17109

## Milestone of this PR

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. 
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`VerifyAttestationSignature` in `pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/verifier.go` unconditionally returned an error when `cosign.VerifyImageAttestations` reported `verified=false` (i.e. the attestation could not be tied to a Rekor/tlog bundle). `VerifyImageSignature` already tolerated this exact condition when the attestor's `CTLog.InsecureIgnoreTlog` or `CTLog.InsecureIgnoreSCT` was set, since `verified` here means "verified via a transparency-log bundle", not "the signature is cryptographically valid" — for keyed/KMS signing without a public tlog, `verified=false` is expected, and the returned attestations slice only ever contains attestations whose signatures already passed cryptographic verification.

This change extracts the existing inline check from `VerifyImageSignature` into a small shared helper, `ignoreTlog(cosignAttestor *v1beta1.Cosign) bool`, and applies it to the same branch in `VerifyAttestationSignature`, so both verification paths now behave consistently: an attestation whose signature verified but whose tlog inclusion could not be confirmed is accepted when the attestor explicitly opted out of tlog/SCT verification, and rejected otherwise. Downstream, the per-attestation predicate-type/annotation matching loop (`found`/`checkedTypes`) is unchanged, so this cannot cause a bogus or absent attestation to be accepted — it only skips the transparency-log-inclusion check for attestations that already passed cryptographic signature verification, exactly mirroring the pre-existing image-signature behavior.

### Proof Manifests

```go
// pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/verifier.go (VerifyAttestationSignature, excerpt)
sigs, verified, err := cosign.VerifyImageAttestations(ctx, image.NameRef(), cOpts)
if err != nil {
    ...
} else if !verified {
    if !ignoreTlog(attestor.Cosign) {
        err := fmt.Errorf("cosign bundle verification failed")
        logger.Error(err, "image verification failed")
        return err
    }
}
```

```yaml
# Example ImageValidatingPolicy attestor/attestation matching the issue's repro:
attestors:
  - name: k
    cosign:
      key: { data: <public PEM> }        # or kms:
      ctlog: { insecureIgnoreTlog: true, insecureIgnoreSCT: true }
attestations:
  - name: sbom
    intoto: { type: https://cyclonedx.org/bom }
validations:
  - expression: "variables.allImages.map(i, verifyAttestationSignatures(i, attestations.sbom, [attestors.k]) > 0).all(e, e)"
```

- [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is <replace>.
- [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and
  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

## Further Comments

Validation performed:
- `go build ./pkg/image/...` — passed.
- `go vet ./pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/...` — passed.
- `gofmt -l` on both changed files — no output (already formatted).
- `golangci-lint run ./pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/... -c .golangci.yml` — 0 issues.
- `go test ./pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/... -v` — all tests passed (77s), including the pre-existing network-dependent integration tests against `ghcr.io/kyverno/test-images/cosign` (registry was reachable in this environment), and the new `TestIgnoreTlog` unit test.

Disclosure / limitation: I added a pure unit test (`TestIgnoreTlog`, no network) that proves the extracted helper is logically identical to the pre-existing `VerifyImageSignature` check it mirrors. I also attempted to add a live, positive integration test for `VerifyAttestationSignature` with a keyed attestor + `InsecureIgnoreTlog` (analogous to the existing `Test_ImageSignatureVerificationKeyed`), but none of the available `ghcr.io/kyverno/test-images/cosign` fixtures reproduce the `verified=false` condition on the attestation path — their key-based attestations verify with `verified=true` regardless of `CTLog` config, so such a test would pass identically with or without this fix and wouldn't provide real coverage. I did not have a way to sign a new offline/air-gapped test fixture without a live cluster/registry write access, so I'm disclosing this rather than adding a misleading test. Concretely: the new `if !ignoreTlog(...)` conditional at the `VerifyAttestationSignature` call site is not exercised (true or false branch) by any existing fixture; its correctness is established by code-path tracing into cosign's `VerifyImageAttestations`/`verifyOCIAttestation` (an attestation only ever lands in the returned `sigs` slice after its signature is cryptographically verified, independent of `bundleVerified`, and an empty `sigs` implies a non-nil `err` returned before this branch is reached), not by an integration test. A small offline-signed, key-based, no-Rekor-entry test fixture would let this be covered by a live test in the future; not required for this fix.

title: fix: cache KMS-based verifiers by key to prevent goroutine leak in image verification
author: waterWang
head: waterWang:fix-kms-goroutine-leak
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Fix: KMS verifier goroutine leak

**Issue:** kyverno/kyverno#17190

## Problem

KMS-based verifiers (e.g. `gcpkms://`) are rebuilt on every image verification via `PublicKeyFromKeyRefWithHashAlgo`, which creates a new KMS client (gRPC connection) each time. These clients are never closed, causing goroutine and memory growth with the number of distinct image references verified until the admission controller is OOMKilled.

## Fix

Cache the KMS-based verifier by key reference using a `sync.Map`. When the same KMS key reference is encountered again, the cached verifier is reused instead of creating a new one, preventing the goroutine leak.

## Changes

- `pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/cosign.go`: Added `kmsVerifierCache` sync.Map, check cache before creating a new KMS verifier, and store on first creation.

title: fix: correct GetResourceGVR boundary length calculation for 64-65 char GVRs
author: waterWang
head: waterWang:fix-getresourcegvr-boundary-64-65
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

`SetResourceGVR()` stores long GVR values in split-label format when the dotted representation (`resource.version.group`) exceeds Kubernetes' 63-character label limit. However, `GetResourceGVR()` determines whether reconstruction is required by calculating the length of a concatenated string **without the `.` separators** (`group + version + resource`).

This creates a boundary condition for GVRs whose dotted length is 64 or 65 characters. For example:

- `openstackmachinecreators.v1beta1.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io`
  - Dotted length: 65 → stored as split labels ✓
  - Without-dot length: 63 → read path skips reconstruction ✗
  - Result: `GetResourceGVR()` returns an empty GVR, report adoption fails

## Related issue

Closes #17191
