title: fix(cosign): resolve bundle artifactType on fallback tag registries
author: bhuvan-somisetty
head: bhuvan-somisetty:fix/sigstore-fallback-tag-bundle-resolution
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

On container registries that do not support the OCI 1.1 referrers API (e.g. GHCR, which returns HTTP 404 for `/referrers/<digest>`), `go-containerregistry` falls back to fetching referrer manifests via the fallback tag scheme (`sha256-<digest>`).

Descriptors in fallback tag indices generated by Cosign 3.x have `manifestDesc.ArtifactType` set to `application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json` or `""`, with the actual bundle `artifactType` or `mediaType` residing on the referenced image manifest or layer level. In `pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go`, filtering strictly on `manifestDesc.ArtifactType` caused all fallback tag bundle descriptors to be discarded, resulting in a false "no signatures found" error.

This PR updates `fetchBundles` in `sigstore.go` so that when `manifestDesc.ArtifactType` is empty or `application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json`, it inspects the referenced manifest's `ArtifactType`, layer `MediaType`, or bundle structure to resolve valid Cosign bundles.

## Related issue

Closes #16664

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- In `fetchBundles` (`pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go`), when `manifestDesc.ArtifactType` is empty or `application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json`, fetch the referenced manifest and check its `ArtifactType` and layer `MediaType`.
- Fall back to verifying Sigstore bundle JSON structure if descriptor-level metadata is typed `oci.empty`.
- Preserve existing fast-path prefix filter for standard referrers index descriptors.

### Proof Manifests

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: check-image-signatures
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signature
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    verifyImages:
    - imageReferences:
      - "ghcr.io/my-org/*"
      attestors:
      - entries:
        - keyless:
            issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
            subjectRegExp: https://github.com/my-org/.*
            rekor:
              url: https://rekor.sigstore.dev
```

title: fix: panic in RedactSecret on empty annotations and unreachable error check
author: jojinkb
head: jojinkb:fix-unreachable-code
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

`RedactSecret` (used to mask Secret data and annotations before admission request payloads are dumped to logs when `--dumpPayload` is enabled) contained an unreachable error check, a silently discarded error, and bare type assertions — one of which is a reachable panic: a valid Secret with an explicitly empty `metadata.annotations: {}` makes `RedactSecret` panic with `interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not map[string]interface {}` inside the admission handler chain. This PR fixes the panic (empty annotations now redact as a graceful no-op), removes the unreachable check that SVACE flagged, and makes the remaining error handling correct and self-consistent.

## Related issue

Closes #15401

The unreachable check was reported by the Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) using SVACE. Related discussion: #15091 ("potential panic").

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- To be set by maintainers, e.g. via `/milestone` -->

## Documentation (required for features)

Not applicable — bug fix in internal error handling, no new or altered user-facing behavior.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

In `pkg/utils/kube/secret.go` `RedactSecret`:

- **Fix a reachable panic on empty annotations.** A Secret with `metadata.annotations: {}` unmarshals into `corev1.Secret` as a non-nil empty map (so the `secret.Annotations != nil` branch is taken), but the empty map is then dropped by `omitempty` during the internal marshal/unmarshal round trip, so `updatedMeta["annotations"]` is nil and the bare type assertion panics. Since an empty annotations map has nothing to redact, this case is now a no-op: when the round trip dropped the annotations key, redaction skips `SetNestedMap` instead of panicking (or erroring, which would make `redactPayload` in `pkg/webhooks/handlers/dump.go` drop the entire admission dump for a valid Secret).
- **Remove the unreachable `if err != nil` block** after `updateSecret["metadata"].(map[string]interface{})` — a type assertion never sets `err`, and the previous statement that did (`datautils.ToMap`) already returned on error, so `err` is always nil there (the exact SVACE finding in #15401).
- **Replace the three bare type assertions** (`updateSecret["string_data"]`, `updateSecret["metadata"]`, `updatedMeta["annotations"]`) with checked `, ok` assertions that return descriptive errors instead of panicking. This appears to be what the dead check originally intended.
- **Return the wrapped error from `json.Marshal(stringSecret)`** instead of `return *resource, nil`, which swallowed the error and would have reported an unredacted Secret as successfully redacted.

Added tests:

- `TestRedactSecret_EmptyAnnotations` — regression test for the panic; it fails (panics) on the unfixed code and verifies the no-op behavior on the fixed code.
- `TestRedactSecret_AnnotationsWithoutData` — covers the annotations-only branch (Secret with annotations but no `data`), which had no dedicated test.

### Proof Manifests

Not applicable — the affected code path is the debug admission-dump handler (`--dumpPayload`), not policy behavior. Verified via unit tests:

```
$ go test ./pkg/utils/kube/... -run TestRedactSecret -v
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_WithData
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_WithAnnotations
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_AnnotationsWithoutData
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_EmptyAnnotations
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_EmptyData
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_MultipleDataKeys
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_PreservesMetadata
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_TLSSecret
--- PASS: TestRedactSecret_DockerConfigSecret
PASS
ok      github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/utils/kube
```

On the unfixed code, `TestRedactSecret_EmptyAnnotations` panics:

```
--- FAIL: TestRedactSecret_EmptyAnnotations (0.00s)
panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not map[string]interface {} [recovered, repanicked]
```

`go vet`, `golangci-lint run`, and `golangci-lint fmt --diff` are clean for the package.

## Checklist

- [X] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).

- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.

- [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is <replace>.

  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

## Further Comments

The scope is slightly wider than deleting the single dead `if` block: the checked type assertions, the empty-annotations no-op, and the un-swallowed marshal error are the same class of defect in the same function, and fixing them together implements what the dead check was evidently meant to do. title: fix(generate): fix GeneratingPolicy synchronization for custom resources and multiple triggers
author: rx18-eng
head: rx18-eng:fix/gpol-sync-customresource-revert
action: Keep on main
body:
# Explanation

`GeneratingPolicy` synchronization has two bugs that a user hit together: after restarting the background controller, a policy generating a `ResourceQuota`, a `NetworkPolicy`, and a Kai Scheduler `Queue` per tenant namespace only kept the `NetworkPolicy` in sync.

First, custom resources never synchronized at all. The update that reverts a modified downstream cleared `resourceVersion`, which Kubernetes accepts for built-in resources but rejects for custom resources, so the `Queue` silently stayed modified.

Second, a policy with several triggers deleted its own resources. `SyncWatchers` runs once per trigger but stores its result per policy, so each namespace overwrote the policy's set of kinds and anything missing from the last one had its watcher stopped and its downstreams deleted in every other namespace.

Both fixes restore the intended synchronization behavior.


## Related issue

Closes #16747 

## Milestone of this PR

`/milestone 1.19.0`

## What type of PR is this

`/kind bug`

## Proposed Changes

- Revert and source-change propagation now reuse the live `resourceVersion` instead of clearing it. This matches what the traditional generate engine already does in `clone.go`. The delete-and-recreate path still clears it, since `Create` rejects one.
- The watcher prune step now keeps a kind as long as any downstream of it still belongs to the policy, and no longer deletes anything. Deleting generated resources is already owned by the policy update and delete paths (`DeleteDownstreams` and `RemoveWatchersForPolicy`), and both clear the cache before regenerating, so the prune loop only ever found resources to delete when another trigger still owned them.
- Added unit coverage for both update paths and for the multi-trigger prune logic, plus the counterpart case where a kind the policy genuinely stopped generating still has its watcher removed.
- Added two integration tests running the reported policy against a real API server. Both fail on `main`.

## Proof Manifests

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: queues.scheduling.run.ai
spec:
  group: scheduling.run.ai
  names:
    kind: Queue
    listKind: QueueList
    plural: queues
    singular: queue
  scope: Cluster
  versions:
    - name: v2
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
---
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: generate-tenant-resources
spec:
  evaluation:
    synchronize:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["namespaces"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  matchConditions:
    - name: is-tenant-namespace
      expression: "'tenant' in object.metadata.labels"
  variables:
    - name: nsName
      expression: "object.metadata.name"
    - name: queue
      expression: >
        [{"kind": dyn("Queue"), "apiVersion": dyn("scheduling.run.ai/v2"),
          "metadata": dyn({"name": string(variables.nsName)}),
          "spec": dyn({"displayName": dyn("Free Tier"), "parentQueue": dyn("normal-root")})}]
    - name: networkPolicy
      expression: >
        [{"kind": dyn("NetworkPolicy"), "apiVersion": dyn("networking.k8s.io/v1"),
          "metadata": dyn({"name": "namespace-isolation", "namespace": string(variables.nsName)}),
          "spec": dyn({"podSelector": dyn({}), "policyTypes": dyn(["Ingress", "Egress"])})}]
  generate:
    - expression: generator.Apply("", variables.queue)
    - expression: generator.Apply(variables.nsName, variables.networkPolicy)
```

To reproduce on `main`: create two namespaces labelled `tenant`, wait for both `Queue`s, then edit one `Queue` (it never reverts). Delete the `Queue` in one namespace and restart the background controller, and the other namespace's `Queue` gets deleted too.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the contributing guidelines.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.

## Further Comments

I kept the prune step and only made it cache-aware rather than reworking how `SyncWatchers` is called, so the "policy stopped generating this kind" cleanup still happens, just once the kind genuinely has nothing left. I left the goroutine in `generate_controller.go` alone: with cache-based pruning the ordering no longer loses anything, and the worst case is brief watcher churn that self-heals on the next sync.

Fixed `GeneratingPolicy` synchronization for generated custom resources, and stopped a policy with multiple triggers from deleting downstream resources and losing watchers.

title: fix(engine): set default Content-Type header to application/json for APICall POST requests
author: bhuvan-somisetty
head: bhuvan-somisetty:fix/apicall-post-content-type
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

`context.apiCall` service requests with `method: POST` build the request body from `data` key/value pairs (encoded as JSON) but do not automatically add a `Content-Type` header unless explicitly listed under `service.headers`. Strict HTTP servers and frameworks (such as FastAPI 0.135+) reject these requests with HTTP 422 because the missing `Content-Type` header causes payload parsing to fail.

This PR updates the HTTP header construction logic for APICall service calls so that `POST` requests default to `Content-Type: application/json` if no `Content-Type` header is explicitly provided in `service.headers`.

## Related issue

Closes #16745

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- Update `addHTTPHeaders` in `pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go` to set `Content-Type: application/json` for `POST` requests when `Content-Type` is not already present in the request headers.
- Preserve any user-supplied `Content-Type` header (such as `text/plain` or custom types) configured under `service.headers`.
- Add unit tests in `pkg/engine/apicall/executor_test.go` verifying default `Content-Type` header behavior on `POST` requests and custom header preservation.

### Proof Manifests

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-apicall-post-header
spec:
  rules:
  - name: call-service
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:

      apiCall:
        method: POST

    validate:

title: fix: drop empty patch arrays in JoinPatches
author: n0liu
head: n0liu:fix/joinpatches-empty-array
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

`JoinPatches` in `pkg/utils/json/utils.go` combines serialized JSON patches into a single JSON Patch array. When one of the inputs is an empty array (`[]`), it was stripped down to an empty string but still appended to the list, so joining it with a real patch produced malformed JSON with a stray comma — e.g. `[, {"op":"add",...}]` — which then fails to decode. This is a fix of existing behavior.

The empty check was done before the surrounding brackets were removed, so `[]` (length 2) slipped past it. This adds a second check after the brackets are trimmed, skipping the token once it is empty — consistent with how empty-string inputs are already dropped.

## Related issue

Closes #16710

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- `pkg/utils/json/utils.go`: skip a patch token that becomes empty after its surrounding `[` / `]` are removed, so an empty array no longer joins in as a stray, comma-producing operation.
- `pkg/utils/json/utils_test.go`: add `Test_JoinPatches_EmptyArray` covering an empty array in the leading and trailing positions (result must decode and equal the single real patch) and two empty arrays collapsing to `nil`. The test fails on `main` (`[, {...}]` fails to decode) and passes with the fix.

Verified locally: `go test -race ./pkg/utils/json/` passes, `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean.

title: fix(autogen): preserve controller metadata paths in VPol and IVPol
author: ANAMASGARD
head: ANAMASGARD:fix/12484-autogen-metadata-fields-v2
action: Keep on main
body:
## Replacement PR

This draft supersedes #16475, which was automatically closed by the repository pull-request limit. The replacement was rebuilt from the current `main` branch and replaces the earlier metadata deny-list with a narrow allow-list.

## What this fixes

Addresses #12484.

VPol and IVPol autogen previously rewrote all `object.metadata` and `oldObject.metadata` paths to Pod-template metadata. That is incorrect for controller-scoped metadata such as `name`, `namespace`, `uid`, resource versions, owner references, and lifecycle fields.

Autogen now applies deterministic metadata semantics:

- `spec` rewrites to the configured Pod-template spec path.
- `metadata.labels` and `metadata.annotations`, including CEL optional selectors such as `metadata.?labels`, rewrite to the configured Pod-template metadata path.
- All other metadata paths remain scoped to the admitted controller.

This is a corrective behavior change for the controller-metadata rewrite defect. It intentionally does not implement OR-expansion across controller and Pod-template metadata levels.

## Scope boundaries

- #16524 remains the narrower `object.metadata.name` fix for #15591. This PR includes the broader shared semantics and remains a draft pending maintainer guidance on consolidation.
- #16477 is out of scope. This PR does not add custom-controller definitions, CRD template paths, or support for multiple Pod templates.

## Verification

Passed locally:

```text
go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/cel/autogen/... ./pkg/cel/policies/vpol/autogen/... ./pkg/cel/policies/ivpol/autogen/... ./pkg/cel/policies/mpol/autogen/...
go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/cel/...
make imports
make fmt
make imports-check
make fmt-check
git diff --check
cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/kubectl-kyverno test /tmp/kyverno-policies
```

The external policy suite completed with `4963 tests passed and 0 tests failed`. The two previously failing focused suites are also green: `metadata-match-regex` is 10/10 and `require-annotations` is 8/8, including the Deployment and CronJob good cases.

The regression coverage includes Deployment and CronJob paths, `object` and `oldObject`, dot, bracket, and CEL optional-selector notation after JSON round-trip, metadata boundaries, repeated occurrences, already-generated paths, and idempotence.

`chainsaw test --test-dir test/conformance/chainsaw/autogen` was not runnable locally because no Docker daemon or KinD cluster is available in this environment.

Maintainer guidance is requested on whether this scoped correction is sufficient to change `Addresses #12484` to `Closes #12484` and whether #16524 should be consolidated into this PR.

title: fix: deduplicate redundant SubjectAccessReview checks during policy validation
author: 7se7en72025
head: 7se7en72025:fix/dedupe-policy-validation-auth-checks
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

Validating a Kyverno policy checks, for every rule with a `validate`, `mutate`, or `generate` action, whether the relevant Kyverno service account (reports/background/admission controller) has the necessary `get`/`list`/`watch` permissions on the resource kinds the rule matches. This is implemented as one `SubjectAccessReview` API call per verb, per rule — even when several rules in the same policy match the same kind. For a policy with 22 rules all matching `Pods`, this means 66 sequential `SubjectAccessReview` round trips during a single policy-validation webhook call. On clusters with higher API server latency this pushes the webhook past its timeout, and the policy fails to apply or update entirely.

This PR adds a small cache that memoizes the outcome of a `SubjectAccessReview` check (keyed by user, verb, resource kind, namespace, name, subresource) and shares it across every rule while validating a single policy, so identical checks are only sent to the API server once. This is a fix to existing behavior; it does not change what gets validated or the resulting permission decisions, only how many times the same check is executed.

## Related issue

Closes #12099

## Milestone of this PR

## Documentation (required for features)

N/A — internal performance fix, no user-facing behavior changes.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- Added `auth.Cache` (`pkg/policy/auth/auth.go`), a mutex-protected map from `(user, verb, gvk, namespace, name, subresource)` to the allowed/denied result. Errors are intentionally **not** cached, since they are often transient (e.g. a slow API server) and should be retried rather than replayed for the rest of the validation pass.
- `auth.NewAuth` now takes a `*Cache` (nil disables memoization, preserving old behavior for any other caller).
- `validate.NewValidateFactory`, `mutate.NewMutateFactory`, and `generate.NewGenerateFactory` now accept and forward the same cache to the `Auth` instances they create.
- `validation/policy.Validate` creates a single `auth.Cache` per policy-validation call and passes it into `validateActions` for every rule in the policy, so rules sharing a resource kind reuse each other's `SubjectAccessReview` results. The exported signature of `Validate` is unchanged, so no caller (webhook handler, CLI) needed updating.

### Proof Manifests

Reproduction from the issue — a policy where every rule matches `Pods`, so a large number of rules previously meant that many repeated, sequential `SubjectAccessReview` calls for the same kind:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: many-rules-same-kind
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: rule-1
    match:
      any:
      - resources: { kinds: [Pod] }
    validate:
      message: "rule 1"
      pattern: { spec: { containers: [{ name: "*" }] } }
  - name: rule-2
    match:
      any:
      - resources: { kinds: [Pod] }
    validate:
      message: "rule 2"
      pattern: { spec: { containers: [{ name: "*" }] } }
  # ... repeated N times, one rule per required check
```

Before this change, applying a policy shaped like this with 22 rules issued 66 sequential `SubjectAccessReview` calls (3 verbs × 22 rules) against the API server during the validating webhook call, exactly as reported in #12099. After this change, the 3 verbs are checked once for `Pod` and reused for the remaining 21 rules, cutting the call count from 66 to 3 for this example.

This is exercised directly by the new unit tests in `pkg/policy/auth/auth_test.go`, which use a fake `SubjectAccessReview` reactor to count actual API calls:

- `TestAuth_CanI_NoCacheRepeatsAccessReviews`: 5 identical checks with no cache issue 15 (5×3) calls, matching pre-fix behavior.
- `TestAuth_CanI_CacheDedupesAccessReviews`: the same 5 checks sharing a `Cache` issue only 3 calls — one per verb.

I confirmed the new test fails against the pre-fix code (temporarily inlining the old, uncached `check` implementation reproduces the 15-calls failure) and passes once the cache is restored.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).
- [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.
- [ ] This is a feature and I have added CLI tests that are applicable.
- [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is <replace>.
- [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and
  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

## Further Comments

I used Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant) to help implement this fix and write/verify the accompanying tests; the change was reviewed and tested by me before submitting.

An alternative considered was parallelizing the `SubjectAccessReview` calls with goroutines, as also suggested in the issue. I went with deduplication instead: it directly targets the reported waste (repeated identical checks across rules matching the same kind), requires no new concurrency/error-aggregation handling, and composes with a future parallelization change if that's still wanted for the remaining non-duplicate checks.

  - Reduces repeated authorization requests and can improve validation speed, especially for policies with overlapping rules.

- **Compatibility**
  - Validation behavior remains unchanged when result reuse is unavailable or not configured.

title: feat: stable autogen rule names via optional validation identifier
author: aditip149209
head: aditip149209:autogen-identifier
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

<!--
In a couple sentences, explain why this PR is needed and what it addresses. This should be an explanation a non-developer user can understand and covers the "why" question. It should also clearly indicate whether this PR represents an addition, a change, or a fix of existing behavior. This explanation will be used to assist in the release note drafting process.

THIS IS MANDATORY.
-->
Fixes kyverno/kyverno#16000. 
Autogen-generated rule names for ValidatingPolicy currently fall back to positional naming i.e. autogen-validate-0, autogen-validate-1, etc,  based on a validation's index in spec.validations. If the list gets reordered (e.g. inserting a new check in the middle), every name after that point shifts, silently breaking anything that referenced a specific rule by name (e.g. PolicyReport consumers, dashboards, external tooling).

Adds an optional way to assign a stable identifier to each validation, so its rule name becomes autogen-{identifier} and stops depending on position. Identifiers are supplied via a policy annotation rather than an inline identifier: field on each validation:

```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: check-pod-security
  annotations:
    validate.policies.kyverno.io/identifiers: |
      {
        "!has(object.spec.securityContext) || object.spec.securityContext.privileged != true": "check-privileged",
        "!has(object.spec.hostNetwork) || object.spec.hostNetwork == false": "check-host-network"
      }
spec:
  validations:
    - expression: "!has(object.spec.securityContext) || object.spec.securityContext.privileged != true"
      message: "Privileged containers are not allowed"
    - expression: "!has(object.spec.hostNetwork) || object.spec.hostNetwork == false"
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed" 
```

The annotation is a JSON object keyed by the validation's exact CEL expression text, not its index, which allows the validation to survive reordering. A policy with no annotation behaves exactly as it does today: fully backward compatible.

PS: Known limitation
The identifier lives in a separate annotation instead of inline next to the validation it names, so there's nothing stopping the expression text and the annotation key from drifting apart if someone edits the expression later (whitespace, rewording) without updating the annotation. validate.go's stray-key check catches this at apply time rather than letting it fail silently, but it is a real ergonomic tradeoff against the inline-field design from the original issue.

title: fix(cli): derive OCI apiVersion annotation from policy object
author: vmsilvamolina
head: vmsilvamolina:fix/16569-oci-annotation-apiversion
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

When packaging a Kyverno policy into an OCI image, the CLI generates an `io.kyverno.image.apiVersion` annotation describing the policy. This annotation was always hardcoded to `kyverno.io/v1`, regardless of the actual `apiVersion` of the policy object being packaged (e.g. `kyverno.io/v2beta1`). This fix derives the annotation from the policy object's own API version instead of hardcoding it.

## Related issue

Closes #16569

## Milestone of this PR

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`internal.Annotations()` now type-asserts the policy to `runtime.Object` and reads `GetObjectKind().GroupVersionKind()` to derive the `apiVersion` annotation, falling back to `kyverno.io/v1` only if the object's `TypeMeta` has no version set (e.g. constructed programmatically without it). Both `*kyvernov1.Policy` and `*kyvernov1.ClusterPolicy` — the only concrete types behind `kyvernov1.PolicyInterface` produced by the CLI's policy loader — implement `runtime.Object` and carry their original `apiVersion` in `TypeMeta` after being parsed from YAML (verified locally, see below).

### Proof Manifests

Policy YAML used to reproduce the bug:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2beta1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-policy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    validate:
      message: "test"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: "?*"
```

Loaded this policy through the CLI's actual loader (`policy.Load`) and called `internal.Annotations()` on the result:

**Before the fix:**
```
annotations: map[string]string{"io.kyverno.image.apiVersion":"kyverno.io/v1", "io.kyverno.image.kind":"ClusterPolicy", "io.kyverno.image.name":"test-policy"}
```

**After the fix:**
```
annotations: map[string]string{"io.kyverno.image.apiVersion":"kyverno.io/v2beta1", "io.kyverno.image.kind":"ClusterPolicy", "io.kyverno.image.name":"test-policy"}
```

title: fix: propagate namespaceSelector from NamespacedMutatingPolicy to webhook configuration
author: Tommolo
head: Tommolo:fix/namespacedmutatingpolicy-namespaceselector-webhook
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug in `NamespacedMutatingPolicy` where the `namespaceSelector` defined in `matchConstraints` was not being propagated to the generated `MutatingWebhookConfiguration`. As a result, the admission webhook intercepted requests from **all namespaces** (except `kube-system` and `kyverno`), causing mutations to be applied universally instead of only within the namespace declared in the policy. This is a **fix** of existing behavior: after this change, a `NamespacedMutatingPolicy` scoped to namespace `foo` will no longer mutate resources in namespace `bar`.

## Related issue

Closes #16580

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- /milestone 1.18.x -->

## Documentation (required for features)

N/A — this is a bug fix with no new user-facing behavior or configuration surface.

- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:
  <!-- https://github.com/kyverno/website/pull/123 -->

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

The internal `webhook` struct had no `namespaceSelector` field. `buildResourceMutatingWebhookRules` therefore always set `NamespaceSelector: webhookCfg.NamespaceSelector` (the global config selector), ignoring each policy's `matchConstraints.namespaceSelector`.

The fix adds `namespaceSelector *metav1.LabelSelector` to the `webhook` struct and populates it per-policy via `mergeLabelSelectors(p.GetMatchConstraints().NamespaceSelector, cfg.GetWebhook().NamespaceSelector)`, mirroring the existing `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` behavior.

**Files changed:**
- `pkg/controllers/webhook/utils_webhook.go` — add `namespaceSelector` field + `metav1` import
- `pkg/controllers/webhook/controller.go` — populate `namespaceSelector` per-policy; add `webhookNamespaceSelector` helper; use it in `buildResourceMutatingWebhookRules`

### Proof Manifests

```yaml
# NamespacedMutatingPolicy scoped to plsr-namespace
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: NamespacedMutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: keda-scaledobject-min-pollinginterval-30
  namespace: plsr-namespace
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        kubernetes.io/metadata.name: "plsr-namespace"
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["keda.sh"]
        apiVersions: ["v1alpha1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["scaledobjects"]
  mutations:
    - patchType: ApplyConfiguration
      applyConfiguration:
        expression: |
          !has(object.spec.pollingInterval) || object.spec.pollingInterval < 30 ?
          Object{ spec: Object.spec{ pollingInterval: 30 } } : Object{}
# ScaledObject in OUT-OF-SCOPE namespace — pollingInterval must remain 5
# (was wrongly mutated to 30 before this fix)
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: test-out-of-scope
  namespace: kyverno-test
spec:
  pollingInterval: 5
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: my-deployment
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 5
  triggers:
    - type: cpu
      metricType: Utilization
      metadata:
        value: "70"

title: feat: warn on wildcard policy creation/update
author: ShubhamArora073
head: ShubhamArora073:feat/15488-warn-wildcard-policies
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

Policies matching all resource kinds (`kinds: ["*"]`) cause the webhook to intercept all API calls, adding significant load to the API server. Kyverno should warn users when they create/update such policies.

## Related issue

Closes #15488

## What type of PR is this

/kind enhancement

## Proposed Changes

1. **Detection function** (`pkg/validation/policy/validate.go`): `checkWildcardMatchResources` scans policy rules for wildcard kinds in `match.any`, `match.all`, and direct `match.kinds`.

2. **Admission warning** (`pkg/validation/policy/validate.go`): Added warning to the `Validate` function — returns as part of the admission response warnings slice.

3. **Event emission** (`pkg/webhooks/policy/handlers.go`): When a wildcard policy is admitted successfully, emits a Warning event on the policy object.

4. **Unit tests** (`pkg/validation/policy/wildcard_test.go`): Tests for wildcard detection covering:
   - `kinds: ["*"]` in direct match → warns
   - `kinds: ["Pod"]` → no warn
   - `kinds: ["Pod", "*"]` → warns
   - Wildcard in `match.any` filters → warns
   - Empty kinds (no wildcard) → no warn

### Proof

## Explanation

At `--v=1`, Kyverno logs verbose "Event occurred" / "PolicyApplied" / "Resource Mutated" messages for every policy application. These come from the Kubernetes event broadcaster's internal structured logging set at verbosity 0. Users expect `--v=1` to show only errors/warnings.

## Related issue

Closes #9581

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

Single-line change in `pkg/policy/policy_controller.go`: changed `StartStructuredLogging(0)` to `StartStructuredLogging(3)`.

This raises the threshold for event broadcaster log output to `--v=3`, so these messages only appear when users explicitly request higher verbosity. Events are still recorded to the Kubernetes API (visible via `kubectl get events`) — only console log output is suppressed.

### Proof

```bash
# Before: --v=1 shows event noise
{"level":"info","ts":...,"msg":"Event occurred","object":{"name":"my-policy"},...}

# After: --v=1 is quiet, --v=3 shows events
# (no output at v=1, events appear at v=3+)
```

title: fix(cli): report failure when test expects fail but resource excluded
author: ShubhamArora073
head: ShubhamArora073:fix/11519-test-expected-fail-passes
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

The `kyverno test` command incorrectly reports a test as passing when the test expects `result: fail` but the policy engine does not process the resource (resource excluded from policy match). The test should report this as a failure since the expected fail condition was never triggered.

## Related issue

Closes #11519

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

In `output.go`, when a resource is not found in the engine responses (excluded), the code now checks the expected result:
- If the test expects `fail` or `error`, it reports the test as **failed** (the policy should have caught it but didn't)
- If the test expects `pass`, `skip`, or `warn`, it reports as skipped (existing behavior)

### Proof

When a test expects `result: fail` for resource "bad-pod" but the policy excludes it:

```
# Before: test passes (incorrect)
PASS  disallow-privilege-escalation/privilege-escalation  bad-pod

# After: test fails (correct)
FAIL  disallow-privilege-escalation/privilege-escalation  bad-pod
      (expected fail but resource was not processed by the policy)
```

title: fix(policy): evaluate CEL matchConditions before creating UpdateRequests for generateExisting GeneratingPolicies
author: AYUSH-P-SINGH
head: AYUSH-P-SINGH:GeneratingPolicy_CEL
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug where the policy controller creates `UpdateRequests` (URs) for all trigger resource candidates during `GeneratingPolicy` reconciliation when `generateExisting: true` is enabled, without first evaluating the policy's CEL `matchConditions`.

As a result, URs may be created for resources that do not satisfy the policy's CEL constraints, leading to unnecessary reconciliation work and increased API server load, particularly in large clusters.

This change applies the existing GeneratingPolicy CEL evaluation during trigger discovery so that only resources satisfying the CEL match conditions are used to create `UpdateRequests`.

## Related issue

Closes #16556 

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone v1.13.0

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains a bug fix with no user-facing API or configuration changes.

- [x] Documentation update is not required.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- Updated `getGpolTriggers` to accept the complete `GeneratingPolicy` instead of only `MatchResources`.
- Reused the existing `gpolEngine` and `gpolProvider` to evaluate CEL `matchConditions` for each discovered trigger resource.
- Filtered out resources that fail CEL evaluation before creating `UpdateRequests`.
- Updated all callers of `getGpolTriggers` to pass the full `GeneratingPolicy`.
- Preserved the existing behavior when no CEL `matchConditions` are defined.

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: Feat/globalcontext name lookup
author: tendinginfinity24
head: tendinginfinity24:feat/globalcontext-name-lookup
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

Closes #15623. When spec.kubernetesResource.name is specified in a GlobalContextEntry, the data was always returned as a list, forcing policy authors to write complex CEL filter expressions to extract the single resource they wanted.

## Related issue

Closes #15623

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.19.0

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. 
I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:
https://github.com/kyverno/website/pull/2087

## What type of PR is this

/kind feature

## Proposed Changes

What was Kyverno's behavior before your PR?
spec.kubernetesResource always returned a list even when name was set, requiring CEL like context.myEntry.items.filter(x, x.metadata.name == "foo")[0].data.key.

What does this PR do?
Adds a name field to KubernetesResource. When set, getObject() uses lister.ByNamespace(ns).Get(name) or lister.Get(name) (cluster-scoped) to return the single named object directly.

What is the resulting behavior after your PR?
Policy authors can now access a specific resource with context.myEntry.data.key instead of unwrapping a list.

### Proof Manifests

**ClusterPolicy** — uses `globalReference` to look up a GlobalContextEntry that fetches a single specific resource by name:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: check-service-registry
spec:
  rules:
    - name: validate-allowed-registries
      match:
        all:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
      context:
        - name: allowedRegistries
          globalReference:
            name: service-registry.allowedRegistries
      validate:
        failureAction: Audit
        message: "Validation failed! The engine saw these allowed registries: {{ allowedRegistries }}"
        deny:
          conditions:
            all:
              - key: "{{ images.containers.*.registry }}"
                operator: AnyNotIn
                value: "{{ allowedRegistries }}"
Result — The Kyverno CLI correctly maps the single mocked context entry and successfully evaluates both passing and failing pods based on the fetched data:

title: fix: prevent panic in `kyverno test` on a git URL without a path
author: mailnike
head: mailnike:fix-cli-test-git-url-panic
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
### Problem

`loadTest` slices `gitURL.Path[1:]` for any path detected as a git source (`IsGit` = any `http(s)` URL). When the URL has a host but **no path**, e.g.

```
kyverno test http://github.com
```

`url.Parse` sets `Path` to `""` and the slice panics:

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [1:0]
```

### Fix

Return the existing `invalid URL path ...` error when the path is empty, instead of slicing it. Adds a regression test.

### Testing

`go test ./cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/` passes; the new test panics on `main` without the fix and passes with it.

title: fix: prevent panic in lookupImageExtractor for empty imageExtractor path
author: mailnike
head: mailnike:fix-image-extractor-empty-path-panic
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
### Problem

A `verifyImages` rule can define custom `imageExtractors`. When an extractor entry has an **empty** (or slash-only / whitespace) `path` and **no** explicit `value`, the path splits into zero components and `lookupImageExtractor` runs `fields[len(fields)-1]` with `len(fields) == 0`, panicking:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1]
    pkg/utils/api/image.go:178 lookupImageExtractor
```

Both are user-controllable through the policy spec: the CRD marks `path` required but sets no `minLength` (so `""` is accepted), and `value` is optional. The panic occurs while building extractors, before the resource is inspected.

### Fix

Skip an extractor that has neither usable path components nor an explicit value, instead of indexing `fields[-1]`. Adds a regression test covering `path` = `""`, `/`, `//`, and whitespace.

### Testing

`go test ./pkg/utils/api/` passes; the new test panics on `main` without the fix and passes with it.

title: fix(cel/autogen): preserve object.metadata.name in autogen messageExpression
author: ANAMASGARD
head: ANAMASGARD:fix/15591-autogen-preserve-object-name
action: Keep on main
body: ## Explanation When a ValidatingPolicy targets Pods and autogen expands rules to pod controllers (Deployments, StatefulSets, etc.), CEL autogen was rewriting `object.metadata.name` to `object.spec.template.metadata.name`. Pod templates typically do not set `metadata.name`, so `messageExpression` failed at runtime with `no such key` when building custom violation messages. This PR fixes that behavior by preserving `object.metadata.name` (and `oldObject.metadata.name`) during autogen rewriting, using the same protection pattern already used for `object.metadata.namespace`. If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer). - [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR. - [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective. ## Further Comments Maintainer context from #15591: autogen maps metadata to `spec.template.metadata`, where pod template `name` is usually unset. title: fix: make unused-package-check detect go.mod/go.sum changes
author: ShubhamArora073
head: ShubhamArora073:fix/unused-package-check
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

The `make unused-package-check` target is intended to fail CI when `go mod tidy` would modify `go.mod` or `go.sum`. However, the current implementation captures stdout from `go mod tidy` — but `go mod tidy` writes changes directly to files without printing to stdout. This means the check always passes, even when module files are out of sync.

This PR fixes the check to use the same `git diff --quiet --exit-code` pattern already established by the `fmt-check` and `imports-check` targets in the same Makefile.

## Related issue

Closes #16091

## Milestone of this PR

N/A — build tooling fix, applicable to any release.

## Documentation (required for features)

Not applicable — this is a CI/build fix with no user-facing behavior change.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

Replace the broken stdout-capture approach with a working-tree diff check:

1. Run `go mod tidy`
2. Show any diff in `go.mod` / `go.sum` (for developer visibility)
3. Fail if the diff is non-empty

This matches the pattern at lines 190-204 of the same Makefile (`fmt-check`, `imports-check`).

### Proof Manifests

Not applicable — this is a Makefile target, not a Kyverno policy change. Verification:

```bash

$ make unused-package-check
Checking unused packages...
# exits 0

If this test fails, it is because the git diff is non-empty after running "go mod tidy".
To correct this, locally run "go mod tidy" and commit the changes.

title: fix(cli): honor --audit-warn for ValidatingPolicy audit failures
author: Tavisha10
head: Tavisha10:fix-cli-audit-warn-vpol
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

`kyverno apply --audit-warn` already treats legacy `Policy`/`ClusterPolicy` audit violations as warnings (counted under `warn`, exit code `0`). This PR extends the same behavior to CEL `ValidatingPolicy` resources with `spec.validationActions: Audit` — previously, an audit-only violation was printed as an audit warning but still counted under `fail`, causing `kyverno apply` to exit non-zero. This is a bug fix; no new user-facing flags or behavior are introduced, existing audit-warn semantics are simply made consistent across policy types.

## Related issue

Fixes #16485

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

Root cause: `AddValidatingPolicyResponse` in `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/result.go` never received the `--audit-warn` flag and never inspected the policy's `spec.validationActions`, unlike the legacy `addEngineResponse` path which already handles this correctly for `Policy`/`ClusterPolicy`.

Fix: threads `auditWarn` through `AddValidatingPolicyResponse` and downgrades a `RuleStatusFail` to `warn` only when `--audit-warn` is set *and* `Deny` is absent from the policy's `spec.validationActions` (i.e. the policy is Audit-only), mirroring the legacy behavior exactly. All call sites updated accordingly; non-`ValidatingPolicy` call sites (`kyverno test`, envoy/http authz policies) pass `false` to preserve their existing behavior unchanged.

kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit
spec:
  validationActions:
    - Audit
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
    - expression: "false"
      message: audit failure
\`\`\`

\`\`\`yaml

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: demo
spec:

    - name: app
      image: nginx

Before: `kyverno apply policy.yaml --resource pod.yaml --audit-warn` → `pass: 0, fail: 1, warn: 0` → exit `1`
After: same command → `pass: 0, fail: 0, warn: 1` → exit `0`

title: Add status conditions to DeletingPolicy
author: atharrva01
head: atharrva01:feat/deleting-policy-status-conditions
action: Keep on main
body:
DeletingPolicy and NamespacedDeletingPolicy were the only CEL policy types without status reporting. Every other policy type exposes a `conditionStatus` with a `Ready` condition, but these only updated `lastExecutionTime`, leaving the CRD's `READY` column empty and giving no visibility into whether a policy was healthy before it executed.

This PR adds status reporting for both policy types. Since they run on a schedule and don't have a webhook, I added a small dedicated status helper that reuses the existing `resolveGVRs` and `permissionsCheck` logic to report an RBAC condition along with an overall `Ready` summary. No other policy types are affected.

The RBAC check runs using the reports ServiceAccount and currently verifies only `get`, `list`, and `watch` permissions. The status messages reflect that accurately, they indicate Kyverno can discover the target resources, not that it can delete them.

I also switched both status updates to field-scoped patches so the deleting controller (`lastExecutionTime`) and the status controller (`conditionStatus`) no longer overwrite each other's changes.

**Tests:** Added unit tests for both cluster- and namespace-scoped policies, plus Chainsaw tests verifying `Ready=True`.

**Follow-ups:**

* Validate the `delete` permission using the cleanup controller's ServiceAccount.
* Re-evaluate status when RBAC changes, since it currently only refreshes on informer resync.

title: fix(webhook): bound admission report creation goroutines with a timeout
author: viktor42b
head: viktor42b:fix-unbounded-admission-report-goroutines
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
# fix(webhook): bound admission report creation goroutines with a timeout

## Explanation

The classic-policy validate and mutate admission handlers create admission reports in fire-and-forget goroutines using `context.TODO()`:

- `pkg/webhooks/resource/validation/validation.go` (`HandleValidationEnforce`)
- `pkg/webhooks/resource/mutation/mutation.go` (`HandleMutation`)

The Kyverno client is built without a REST timeout (`pkg/config/client.go` only sets QPS/burst), so these goroutines have **no upper bound on their lifetime**. If the reports API *hangs* instead of failing fast — e.g. an overloaded reports-server behind an aggregated APIService that is still routable but no longer answering — each goroutine blocks until the kube-apiserver eventually times out the proxied call (~60s), holding the serialized report payload the whole time.

The reports circuit breaker does not protect against this failure mode: its health signal is a watch on `ephemeralreports`, which detects a *disconnected* reports API (watch errors, `IsRunning() == false` → breaker opens, reports dropped — works well), but not a *hanging* one — an established watch that silently stops delivering events keeps `IsRunning() == true` and the breaker closed while report creations pile up.

## Real-world incident

We hit this in a production-scale cluster (Kyverno v1.15.2, kind-`*` policy, ~250 admission req/s, reports-server-backed APIService):

1. reports-server became overloaded and started hanging (requests queued past their deadlines) while its APIService was still marked `Available` for a few more minutes.
2. During that window, every admission request leaked one hung report-creation goroutine. Goroutine counts went from a ~300 baseline to **50k–244k per pod within 1–3 minutes**.
3. Every admission-controller replica blew through its memory limit and was OOMKilled, nearly simultaneously — and kept OOM-crash-looping on restart for ~70 minutes.
4. With all webhook backends dead and `failurePolicy: Fail`, the kube-apiserver's in-flight mutating requests saturated waiting on webhook timeouts, and all writes cluster-wide failed until the reports API recovered.

## Fix

Two complementary bounds:

1. **Time bound** — the report-creation goroutines get a 10s `context.WithTimeout` (shared `reportutils.CreationTimeout`), mirroring the existing `backgroundTimeout` pattern in `handleBackgroundApplies` (`pkg/webhooks/resource/updaterequest.go`) and the audit worker context in `handlers.go`.

2. **Count bound** — a concurrency-limiting decorator (`breaker.WithConcurrencyLimit`) wraps the shared reports breaker, capping concurrent in-flight report creations (default 1000, configurable via `--maxReportsInFlight`). When saturated, additional creations are dropped like an open breaker and recorded through the existing breaker metrics under `circuit_name="admission reports in-flight"` — so `kyverno_breaker_drops` can be alerted on for saturation, with no new metric needed. Because it wraps the shared breaker, it covers every admission report write path: the async classic-policy goroutines and the synchronous ValidatingPolicy / MutatingPolicy / ImageValidatingPolicy handlers.

With both bounds, the incident scenario tops out at `min(admission_rate × 10s, 1000)` in-flight creations per pod instead of growing without bound, the pods survive, and the APIService availability controller flips the group to 503-fast-fail (at which point the existing count-based breaker takes over as designed).

## Related information

- Slack discussion or issue link (optional)

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone TBD

- [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR.

## Further comments

Proof of behavior: existing unit tests pass (`go test ./pkg/webhooks/resource/...`, 86 tests). The change only narrows the context passed to `createReports`; the error path (log-and-continue) is unchanged.

## Explanation

This PR fixes a reports-controller bug where stale `PolicyReport` resources could remain without `metadata.ownerReferences`, which could cause duplicate or outdated report entries to appear for the same workload. It sets ownership metadata earlier for admission-created reports and adds repair and periodic reconciliation paths so stale orphaned reports can be corrected or cleaned up.

## Related issue

Closes #16433

## Proposed Changes

This PR addresses an issue where admission-created ephemeral reports could exist without ownership metadata, which could leave behind stale aggregated `PolicyReport` or `ClusterPolicyReport` resources after a resource is deleted and recreated with a new UID.

The changes in this PR are:

- set `ownerReferences` at creation time for admission-created ephemeral reports;

title: fix: truncate ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding names that exceed the 63-char label limit
author: jsabalete
head: jsabalete:fix/vapbinding-label-length-limit
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

When a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` name exceeds 63 characters (which happens with operators that derive binding names from CRD group names), Kyverno's `background-scan-controller` fails to persist `EphemeralReport` objects. Kubernetes rejects the label key because its name portion (after the `/`) exceeds the 63-character limit. Policy Reporter loses visibility of those resources, though policy evaluation itself is unaffected.

`ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBindingLabel` and `MutatingAdmissionPolicyBindingLabel` in `pkg/utils/report/metadata.go` were passing `binding.GetName()` directly as the label key name portion without length validation.

The fix adds a `truncateLabelName` helper that replaces names longer than 63 chars with their MD5 hex hash (32 chars). MD5 is used instead of simple truncation (as done in `autogen` for rule names) because label keys require uniqueness. Two bindings with different names but a shared 63-char prefix would otherwise collide to the same key. Both the SET and GET paths go through the same function, so the lookup remains consistent.

## Related issue

Closes #16436

Similar issue was fixed for GVR names in #11547 / #11620.

## Milestone of this PR

<!--
Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.2.3`.
-->

- Add `truncateLabelName(name string) string` helper in `pkg/utils/report/metadata.go`

title: fix(jmespath): treat link-local IPs as internal in is_external_url
author: sage-mode-hunter
head: sage-mode-hunter:is-external-url-link-local
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

`is_external_url` is meant to tell a policy whether a URL points at an external host or an internal/non-routable one, so it can be used to reject requests aimed at internal infrastructure. Today it only treats loopback and RFC 1918 private ranges as internal, so link-local addresses and the unspecified address are reported as external. That includes `169.254.169.254`, the cloud metadata endpoint (AWS/GCP/Azure IMDS), which a policy relying on this helper would wrongly accept as a safe external target. This is a fix.

## Related issue

None.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`is_external_url` returned true for addresses that are not routable off-host:
- link-local unicast (`169.254.0.0/16` and `fe80::/10`), which covers the `169.254.169.254` cloud metadata endpoint
- the unspecified address (`0.0.0.0` / `::`)

Both the literal-IP branch and the resolved-DNS branch had the same gap, so the check is now shared in one `isInternalIP` helper and both branches use it. Added regression cases for the metadata IP, an IPv6 link-local address, and `0.0.0.0`.

title: test(integration): add VAP generation testing with vpol/native enforcement equivalence
author: rx18-eng
head: rx18-eng:test/framework-vap-generation
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

Adds test coverage for Kyverno's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP) generation, which previously had no validating-side tests. This is the path that converts a Kyverno policy (`ClusterPolicy` or the newer CEL `ValidatingPolicy`) into a native Kubernetes `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` so the API server enforces it directly. As traditional `ClusterPolicy` is deprecated and CEL/native enforcement becomes the norm, this conversion carries enforcement across the migration, so it should be tested.

This PR adds two layers of coverage:

- A framework helper (`GenerateVAP` / `ApplyVAP`) that drives the real generation builders and applies the generated `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and binding to envtest.
- A flagship integration test proving migration parity: one `ValidatingPolicy` is enforced both by Kyverno's engine and by the native `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` generated from it, and the two decisions must match. A production Pod is denied and a staging Pod is admitted in both paths. If VAP generation ever diverges from Kyverno's engine, migrating a policy to native enforcement would silently change enforcement behavior; this test fails in exactly that case.
- Unit tests for `BuildValidatingAdmissionPolicy` (previously none): `ValidatingPolicy` → `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` conversion, CEL `PolicyException` negation, binding action mapping, and the `CanGenerateVAP` rule-count eligibility boundary.

This also adds a new Tier-3 axis to the integration framework: verifying that Kyverno's *output* is enforced correctly by Kubernetes itself, not just that Kyverno's own engine reaches the correct decision.

## What type of PR is this

/kind test

## Proof / Verification

- `go test ./pkg/admissionpolicy/...` (unit, MAP + new VAP tests, no regressions)
- `go test -tags=integration -race ./test/integration/vap/...` (flagship integration test, passes under `-race`)
- `gofmt`
- `go vet`

## Out of scope

- A pre-existing `-race` flake in `test/integration/vpol` (`TestValidate_MultiplePolicies_DenyAndWarnCombined`), unrelated to this change.

title: fix: bypass empty digest check on unmutated verified images
author: om7057
head: om7057:fix-verify-image-missing-digest
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
Fixes #16344

### Description
In `pkg/engine/handlers/validation/validate_image.go`, the `validateImage` function unconditionally failed if `imageVerify.VerifyDigest` is true but `imageInfo.Digest == ""`. However, because policies can be configured with `mutateDigest: false` (which is required for Audit policies), the preceding verify pass correctly resolves and verifies the remote digest, but intentionally does not patch the resource with it. 

When the validate pass ran, it extracted the unmutated image (which still only has a tag), hit the `imageInfo.Digest == ""` check, and threw a false positive missing digest error.

This PR updates `validateImage` to respect `imageVerify.MutateDigest == false`. If `MutateDigest` is false, it logs and bypasses the missing digest error. The security of the image is still properly evaluated downstream via `engineutils.IsImageVerified()`.

Signed-off-by: om7057 <om7057@users.noreply.github.com>

title: fix: close file descriptor in printOutput to prevent handle leak
author: D-source1602
head: D-source1602:fix/file-descriptor-leak-15400
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
This PR fixes a file descriptor leak in the printOutput method in cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go.
When os.OpenFile is called but a subsequent file.Write fails, the file descriptor was never closed, causing a resource leak.
Changes:

Added defer file.Close() immediately after os.OpenFile — ensures the file is always closed on any early return from a write error
Kept an explicit file.Close() error check at the end of the success path — defer discards return values, so without this, flush errors (e.g. disk full, NFS failure) would be silently ignored
Removed commented-out dead code from the previous implementation

Calling Close() twice is safe — the second call from defer returns os.ErrClosed which is intentionally discarded.
Closes #15400

/kind bug

title: fix(engine): make Equals/NotEquals symmetric for string vs numeric operands
author: risjai
head: risjai:fix/equals-notequals-type-symmetry-16358
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

The `Equals` / `NotEquals` condition operators evaluated logically-equivalent values inconsistently depending on operand order. Comparing a numeric key against a string value (e.g. `Equals(5, "5")`) returned `true`, but the reverse — a string key against a numeric value (e.g. `Equals("5", 5)`) — returned `false` (and `NotEquals("5", 5)` returned `true`). This is a **bug fix** for incorrect policy evaluation: a policy comparing a string literal against a numeric variable could have a precondition or deny rule evaluated incorrectly.

## Related issue

Closes #16358

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

The operator handlers dispatch on the **key's** type. The numeric handlers (`validateValueWithIntPattern` / `validateValueWithFloatPattern`) already contain a `case string:` that parses a string value, so `Equals(5, "5")` works. However, `validateValueWithStringPattern` only handled duration, resource-quantity, and string (wildcard) values — when the value was numeric it fell through to `return false` (`Equals`) / `return true` (`NotEquals`).

This change makes `validateValueWithStringPattern` (in both `equal.go` and `notequal.go`) handle a numeric value by delegating to the existing numeric handlers with the operands flipped. This reuses already-tested parsing logic and makes the comparison **symmetric by construction** — the previously-broken direction now runs the exact same code path as the working direction.

The numeric check is placed **after** the existing duration and resource-quantity checks, so those behaviors are unchanged (e.g. `Equals("100Mi", 100)` correctly remains `false`; `Equals("100", 100)` is `true`).

Behavior before/after:

| Comparison | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Equals("5", 5)` | `false` ❌ | `true` ✅ |
| `Equals(5, "5")` | `true` | `true` |
| `NotEquals("5", 5)` | `true` ❌ | `false` ✅ |
| `Equals("5.5", 5.5)` | `false` ❌ | `true` ✅ |
| `Equals("100Mi", 100)` | `false` | `false` (unchanged) |

### Proof Manifests

A Kyverno CLI test is included at `test/cli/test/test-string-numeric-equals/` that exercises the previously-broken operand order (string literal key vs numeric value) end-to-end. It is auto-discovered by `make test-cli-local-validate`.

I verified the test **fails against the pre-fix binary** (`Want fail, got pass` — the 5-replica Deployment was wrongly allowed because `Equals("5", 5)` returned `false`) and **passes after the fix**.

# Kyverno policy

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-five-replicas
spec:
  admission: true
  background: false
  rules:
  - match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Deployment
    name: deny-when-replicas-equals-five
    validate:
      failureAction: Enforce
      message: Deployments with exactly 5 replicas are not allowed.
      deny:
        conditions:
          all:
          - key: "5"
            operator: Equals
            value: "{{ request.object.spec.replicas }}"
```

# Kyverno CLI test manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: test-string-numeric-equals
policies:
- policy.yaml
resources:
- resources.yaml
results:
# replicas == 5 -> Equals("5", 5) is true -> deny fires -> fail
- kind: Deployment
  policy: deny-five-replicas
  rule: deny-when-replicas-equals-five
  resources:
  - deployment-five-replicas
  result: fail
# replicas == 3 -> Equals("5", 3) is false -> deny does not fire -> pass
- kind: Deployment
  policy: deny-five-replicas
  rule: deny-when-replicas-equals-five
  resources:
  - deployment-three-replicas
  result: pass
```

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).
- [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.

## Further Comments

The fix delegates to the existing numeric handlers rather than duplicating parse logic, so `Equals`/`NotEquals` remain mutual negations across both operand orders. Coverage:
- Unit tests in `equal_test.go` / `notequal_test.go` cover the string-vs-numeric direction, plus a dedicated `TestEqualNotEqual_TypeSymmetry` asserting order-independence and `NotEquals == !Equals`.
- A Kyverno CLI test (`test/cli/test/test-string-numeric-equals/`) proves the fix end-to-end and was confirmed to fail before the fix and pass after.

title: Fix ImageValidatingPolicy bypass for ephemeral containers
author: LoveChauhan-18
head: LoveChauhan-18:main
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR addresses an issue where `ImageValidatingPolicy` checks are silently bypassed when creating or modifying subresources like ephemeral containers. 

Prior to this PR, `HandleValidating` inside the IVPol engine relied on looking up policy outcomes injected as annotations on the object by `HandleMutating`. Because the Kubernetes API server silently drops annotation changes during subresource operations, validation was bypassed entirely. This PR routes subresource verification directly to `handleMutation` (the evaluator) inside the validation admission phase so policies evaluate correctly without relying on persistent annotations.

This represents a fix of existing behavior for subresources.

## Related issue

Closes #16275

## Milestone of this PR

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. 
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is: 

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

1. **Before this PR:** If an `ImageValidatingPolicy` (IVPol) existed on `Pod` resources, adding an ephemeral container would silently skip image validation. This occurred because `HandleValidating` relied on `ImageVerificationOutcome` annotations, which the Kubernetes API server strips on subresource update requests.
2. **This PR does:** Checks if `request.Request.SubResource` is populated. If it is, `HandleValidating` directly invokes `handleMutation` to dynamically compile and evaluate the image policy, instead of looking up annotations.
3. **After this PR:** Image validation correctly triggers for ephemeral container additions/modifications and rejects unauthorized images.

title: contain policy name when writing pulled oci policies
author: sage-mode-hunter
head: sage-mode-hunter:oci-pull-path-traversal
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

`kyverno oci pull` saves every policy found in an OCI image to disk. The on-disk filename is built from the policy's own `metadata.name`, which comes from the image content and is not validated. A crafted image whose policy name contains `../` segments writes the policy file outside the chosen output directory, so pulling an untrusted image can overwrite arbitrary files the user can write to. This is a fix.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- `oci pull` builds the output path as `filepath.Join(dir, policy.GetName()+".yaml")`; the name is image-controlled and unchecked
- a name like `../../../../tmp/x` resolves outside `dir`, turning a pull into an arbitrary file write
- resolve the path with `securejoin.SecureJoin(dir, ...)` so it stays contained in `dir`, matching how `dir` itself is already resolved a few lines above

### Proof Manifests

N/A — this is a CLI file-write path fix, not a policy behavior change. Trigger trace: image layer bytes -> `yamlutils.GetPolicy` -> `policy.GetName()` -> path join -> `os.WriteFile`. With name `../../tmp/pwned`, `filepath.Join("/out", name+".yaml")` yields `/tmp/pwned.yaml`; with `SecureJoin` it yields `/out/tmp/pwned.yaml`.

title: fix: always re-arm background scan and TTL controllers after transient errors (#16109)
author: ANAMASGARD
head: ANAMASGARD:fix/16109-background-ttl-rearm
action: Keep on main
body: ## Summary Fixes #16109 — background scan and TTL controllers no longer silently stop reconciling resources after transient errors exhaust the workqueue retry budget. ## Explanation Both controllers rely on explicit `queue.AddAfter` for periodic work (background scan interval / TTL deadline). Before this fix, `AddAfter` was only reachable on some success paths. When `reconcile()` returned an error, `handleErr` rate-limited up to `maxRetries` (10) and then called `Forget()`, dropping the key. Without a parallel `AddAfter`, periodic scanning or TTL deletion stopped until a pod restart or an informer event re-enqueued the resource. **Background scan:** `PolicyReport` / `ClusterPolicyReport` entries could go stale with no visible error. **TTL:** Resources past their TTL could survive indefinitely if delete or lister calls failed transiently. **Type:** bug fix (existing behavior correction) ## Related issue Fixes #16109 ## Milestone of this PR ## Documentation (required for features) My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. - [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is: Not needed — internal controller reliability fix; no user-facing API or flag changes. ## What type of PR is this /kind bug ## Proposed Changes ### Background scan controller (`pkg/controllers/report/background/controller.go`) - Move `defer c.queue.AddAfter(key, c.forceDelay)` to immediately after the `!exists` block (when resource is still in metadata cache) - Flatten `needsReconcile` from nested `if/else` + inner defer to flat `if err` / `if needsReconcile` (avoids double `AddAfter`) - Add comment explaining `handleErr` handles short-term retries; `forceDelay` is long-term recovery ### TTL controller (`pkg/controllers/ttl/controller.go`) - Add `minRequeueDelay = 1 * time.Second` (matches cleanup/deleting controllers) - Conditional `defer` on delete failure path to re-arm with `minRequeueDelay` - Inline `AddAfter(itemKey, minRequeueDelay)` on transient lister/accessor errors ### Tests - `TestReconcile_NoReconcileNeeded_StillRearmed` — background happy-path re-arm via `captureQueue` - `TestReconcile_DeleteError_StillRearmed` — TTL delete failure still schedules `minRequeueDelay` ### Proof Manifests No conformance/chainsaw fixture — bug is timing-dependent (transient lister/API errors). Proof is unit tests + structural fix (defer placement guarantees re-arm on all error paths where resource exists). **Screenshot 1 — tests pass :** **Screenshot 2 — key fix in background controller :** **Background test:** `TestReconcile_NoReconcileNeeded_StillRearmed` -> `lastDelay == forceDelay` **TTL test:** `TestReconcile_DeleteError_StillRearmed` -> `lastDelay == minRequeueDelay`, reconcile returns error ## Checklist - [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR. - [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective. - [ ] This is a feature and I have added CLI tests that are applicable. - [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is . - [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
# Add a loggingFormat value that emits human-readable text logs without ANSI escape codes, making output easier to read in log aggregation tools without switching to JSON

## Explanation

When Kyverno runs with `--loggingFormat=text` (the default), log output includes ANSI escape codes that colorize timestamps, log levels, and messages. This is helpful in a terminal but makes raw logs harder to read in log aggregation tools such as Datadog, Loki, and CloudWatch.

This PR adds a new `text-nocolor` logging format option that keeps the same human-readable text layout while stripping ANSI color codes. Operators can use it to get clean, readable logs without switching to JSON and incurring higher log storage volume.

This PR represents an **addition** to existing behavior. The default `text` format is unchanged.

## Related issue

Fixes #16283

title: feat: add standalone attestation CEL library for ValidatingPolicy
author: JimBugwadia
head: JimBugwadia:worktree-attestation-cel-lib
action: Keep on main
body:
## Summary

- Introduces `pkg/cel/libs/attestation`, a new policy-neutral CEL library exposing `verifyAttestationSignatures`, `verifyImageSignatures`, `getImageData`, and `extractPayload` in `ValidatingPolicy` (VPOL) rules.
- Previously these functions were only available in `ImageValidatingPolicy` (IVPol), which resolves OCI references from pod image fields and cannot target arbitrary OCI artifacts.
- The new library enables **CI/CD pipeline gate** patterns: a policy verifies an attestation on an OCI artifact referenced in a custom resource field, with `PolicyException` providing per-gate bypasses.
- `imageverify` lib is **unchanged**; full backward compatibility preserved.

## Motivation

`ImageValidatingPolicy` is image-centric — it fires on pod admission and resolves OCI references from pod spec image fields. There is no way to use it to verify attestations on:
- Pipeline artifacts referenced in custom resources (e.g. `PipelineGate`, `ArtifactBundle`)
- Non-image OCI artifacts (SBOMs, signatures, configs stored in OCI registries)
- Arbitrary fields in any Kubernetes resource

This PR makes attestation verification a first-class capability in `ValidatingPolicy`, enabling Kubernetes-native supply chain gates without requiring a separate image-centric policy type.

## Design

| | `imageverify` (existing) | `attestation` (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Used by | IVPol compiler | VPOL compiler |
| Constructor dep | `ImageValidatingPolicyLike` | `imgCtx` + `lister` (both optional) |
| Image-match guard | Yes (`matchImageReferences`) | No — all OCI refs accepted |
| Attestation lookup | By name from policy spec | Inline from type string |
| CEL function names | Same | Same (different `cel.Env`) |

`NewCompiler` gains optional `imgCtx imagedataloader.ImageContext` and `lister k8scorev1.SecretInterface` params. Pass `nil, nil` where registry access is not needed (validate, CLI, scanner); `cmd/kyverno/main.go` passes the real secret lister for authenticated registry access.

## Example: CI/CD pipeline gate

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-slsa-provenance
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: ["ci.example.com"]
      resources: ["pipelinegates"]
      operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  validations:
  - expression: >
      verifyAttestationSignatures(
        object.spec.ociRef,
        "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1",
        [{"cosign": {"keyless": {"issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"}}}]
      ) > 0
    message: "SLSA provenance attestation is required"
```

## Example: inspect the payload after verification

```yaml
spec:
  variables:
  - name: payload
    expression: >
      verifyAttestationSignatures(object.spec.ociRef, "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1",
        [{"cosign": {"keyless": {"issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"}}}]) > 0
      ? extractPayload(object.spec.ociRef, "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1")
      : null
  validations:
  - expression: "variables.payload != null"
    message: "verified SLSA provenance is required"
```

## Test plan

- [x] `pkg/cel/libs/attestation/impl_test.go` — 8 unit tests: CEL compilation for all 4 functions, nil-constructor fallback, no-image-guard property, library name uniqueness, inline attestation struct construction
- [x] `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/engine_test.go` — `TestVPOL_AttestationFunctionsAvailable`: all 4 functions compile in VPOL context; `TestVPOL_AttestationPipelineGatePattern`: full compiler→engine→handle path for a CI/CD gate policy
- [x] All existing `pkg/cel/...` tests pass with no regressions
- [x] `go build ./...` clean

## Files changed

- `pkg/cel/libs/attestation/` — new package (`lib.go`, `impl.go`, `impl_test.go`)
- `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/compiler/compiler.go` — register `attestation.Lib`, update `NewCompiler` signature
- `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/engine_test.go` — new VPOL attestation integration tests
- `cmd/kyverno/main.go` — pass secret lister to `NewCompiler`
- `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go`, `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/validate.go`, `pkg/controllers/report/utils/scanner.go`, `test/integration/framework/vpol.go` — update `NewCompiler(nil, nil)` call sites
- `docs/dev/cel-attestation-lib.md` — architecture, function reference, and usage examples
