title: improve handling of empty/comments-only files
author: Moglum
head: Moglum:empty-documents
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

Running `kyverno apply --resource` against a YAML file that contains only document separators and comments failed with `Object 'Kind' is missing.`  Such files can be quite frequently generated by Helm when a specific template nin a file renders to nothing and only keeps the `—` separator.

This is a simple fix: such files are now silently skipped, matching the behavior for fully empty files.

## Related issue

Closes #13219
Closes #16416

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`IsEmptyDocument` in `ext/yaml/empty.go` only recognized blank lines and # comments as non-content. It did not recognize `---` (the YAML document-start marker), so a document like:
```yaml
---
# Source: aws-load-balancer-controller/crds/gateway-crds.yaml
---
```
was passed to the YAML parser, which returned a null document with no kind and errored. The fix adds `---` to the set of lines that count as empty. Plus tests.

Policy authors can now develop and validate attestation-based policies offline or in air-gapped environments. This is an **addition** of new CLI-only functionality and does not change admission-time behavior.

Closes #2866

## Proposed Changes

Adds support for declaring local attestations in a `kyverno test` manifest so that `verifyImages.attestations` rules can be evaluated without registry access:

- **CLI test schema** (`cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/apis/v1alpha1/test.go`): new `attestations` list with `image`, `predicateType`, and `predicateFile`, plus `ValidateAttestations` (required fields + duplicate `image|predicateType` detection). CRD and CLI API docs regenerated.

title: fix(registry): preserve global keychain for image verification
author: lucchmielowski
head: lucchmielowski:preserve-global-registry-keychain
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Description

Fixes a regression where image verification stopped using the admission controller's global registry credentials (IRSA, ECR credential helper, `--registryCredentialHelpers`) once the admitted workload declared `imagePullSecrets`.

Following #15112, any resource with `imagePullSecrets` causes `RegistryClientFactory.GetClient` to build a secrets-only client and skip the global keychain entirely. That leads to 401s on clusters that use IRSA for Kyverno while app pods use separate static ECR pull secrets for kubelet.

## Problem

`GetClient` returns the global client only when both `imageRegistryCredentials` and resource `imagePullSecrets` are absent. Otherwise it builds a brand-new client from policy secrets and/or workload `imagePullSecrets` only, silently dropping the credential chain configured at startup in `cmd/internal/registry.go` (credential helpers, deployment pull secrets, etc.). Workloads with `imagePullSecrets` (e.g. `ecr-credentials` for image pulls) end up forcing verification through those secrets instead of IRSA.

## Related PRs

Made changes to `kyverno/sdk` to use the `WithKeychain` method: kyverno/sdk#126

⚠️ We need to bump SDK before merging this

## Related discussion

- [Thread on K8s Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1780578844241979)

## Solution

- Use `registryclient.WithKeychain()` to compose the existing global keychain into any per-request client built by `GetClient`.
- When building a per-request client, prepend the **global** keychain via `WithKeychain`, then layer policy/resource credentials on top via `WithImagePullSecrets` and `WithCredentialHelpers`.

Credential resolution order (first non-anonymous auth wins):

1. Global admission-controller keychain (IRSA / helpers / Kyverno deployment secrets)
2. Policy `imageRegistryCredentials.secrets` + resource `imagePullSecrets`
3. Policy `imageRegistryCredentials.providers`
4. `authn.DefaultKeychain` — only used when neither (2) nor (3) apply

The fast path is unchanged: no policy creds and no resource pull secrets → return `globalClient` directly.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./pkg/engine/factories/...` (kyverno) — includes new `TestGetClient_PreservesGlobalKeychain` and `TestGetClient_FallsBackWhenGlobalKeychainIsAnonymous`
- [ ] Manual: Kyverno with `registryCredentialHelpers` including `amazon` + IRSA; verify-images on a Pod with unrelated `imagePullSecrets`; confirm verification succeeds without using workload static creds
- [ ] Regression: workload-only private registry (no cluster creds) still works when global auth is anonymous and pull secrets are valid

title: Fix: stop policy cache invalidation storm and support plural resource kinds
author: CygnusMaximillian
head: CygnusMaximillian:Bug/kind-with-s
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
This commit addresses a severe admission review latency bug described
in #16146, which was caused by repeated unconditional invalidations of
the discovery cache when evaluating policies with unrecognized or
plural resource kinds (e.g. "Secrets").
Changes:
* dclient: Removed the forceful cache invalidation in `FindResources`
  when `len(resources) == 0`. Cache invalidation now strictly relies on
  the CRD watcher or staleness checks (`!c.cachedClient.Fresh()`).
* dclient: Enhanced `findResources` and `getMatchingServerResources` to
  case-insensitively match user-provided kinds against the plural resource
  name (`APIResource.Name`) and `SingularName`.
This ensures policies containing plural kinds (e.g. `kinds: ["Secrets"]`)
gracefully map to the correct GVK instead of causing a discovery cache
rebuild storm, significantly improving overall cluster performance.
Fixes #16146

title: fix(verify-images): bind image verification cache to verified digest
author: lucchmielowski
head: lucchmielowski:fix-kyverno-caching-exploit
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Summary

Fixes a critical verify-images cache integrity issue where a cache hit on a **tag reference** could skip verification and allow `mutateDigest` to pin a different digest if the tag had moved.

This was a verify-A / run-B chain:
1. verify a signed digest for `repo:tag` once (cache warm),
2. move `repo:tag` to a different digest,
3. hit cache and pass without re-verification,
4. patch the **current** tag digest into the admitted resource.

Fixes GHSA-2r43-6962-xcw5.

## Root cause

The image verification cache key included policy/rule/imageRef, but cache entries did not store or validate a verified digest binding.  
On cache hit, verification was short-circuited with `verified from cache`, and `mutateDigest` could still resolve and patch the current digest from the registry.

## Fix

- **Cache now stores the verified digest** on successful verification.
- **Cache hit is accepted only when digest binding matches**:
  - resolve current digest (from input digest or registry lookup for tag),
  - compare with cached verified digest,
  - on mismatch, treat as cache miss and re-verify.
- **MutateDigest uses the verified bound digest** from cache-hit path, preventing pinning an unverified moved-tag digest.
- Do not cache entries when no verified digest is available.

title: fix: handle multi-cert PEM bundle in decodeTLSSecret
author: lmasaya
head: lmasaya:fix/decode-tls-secret-multi-cert
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Problem

When using cert-manager with an external Issuer or ClusterIssuer (e.g. a Vault-backed intermediate CA), cert-manager writes the leaf certificate **and** intermediate CA cert into `tls.crt` as a PEM bundle. `decodeTLSSecret` in `pkg/tls/renewer.go` has three branches for the number of parsed certs:

- 0 certs: returns `nil` cert (correct)
- 1 cert: returns `certs[0]` (correct)
- 2+ certs: returns `nil, nil, nil, err` — but `err` is guaranteed to be `nil` at this point, so callers receive no cert and no error

This causes silent failures in TLS renewal and validation when Kyverno is configured to use an external CA.

## Fix

Scan the PEM bundle for the first non-CA certificate (the leaf) and return it. Falls back to `certs[0]` if all certs are CAs. This handles bundles regardless of cert ordering.

## Tests

Added `renewer_test.go` with eight test cases:
- Single cert (existing behavior, still works)
- Multi-cert chain — leaf first (cert-manager default ordering)
- Multi-cert chain — reversed order (CA first, leaf second)
- Multi-cert chain — ECDSA P-256, leaf first
- Multi-cert chain — ECDSA P-256, reversed order
- All CAs — fallback to `certs[0]` when no leaf is present
- Empty cert field
- Secret not found

All multi-cert tests include key-pair validation (`assertKeyMatchesCert`) to verify the returned certificate's public key matches the private key from the secret.

Fixes #15469

Related: #15595 (converts the silent nil to an explicit error but still rejects multi-cert bundles)

title: Feat/deleting policy reports
author: amine-zaiem
head: amine-zaiem:feat/deleting-policy-reports
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
```markdown
## Explanation

Kyverno's `DeletingPolicy` / `NamespacedDeletingPolicy` and `CleanupPolicy` / `ClusterCleanupPolicy` had no structured, durable, per-resource audit trail of deletion operations. Platform teams running these policies for orphaned resource cleanup had no way to answer "which exact resources did this policy delete, in which namespace, and did any deletions fail?" without falling back to raw Kubernetes audit logs.

This PR adds two complementary observability signals for both policy families:

1. **PolicyReport / ClusterPolicyReport entries** — after each execution cycle, the cleanup controller creates or replaces a `(Cluster)PolicyReport` with one result entry per resource that was targeted for deletion, recording the resource identity, outcome (`pass` / `error`), timestamp, and error detail. This is an addition that brings `DeletingPolicy` and `CleanupPolicy` to parity with the report generation already in place for `ValidatingPolicy`, `MutatingPolicy`, etc.

2. **Per-resource Prometheus counters** — four new counters (`kyverno_deleting_controller_deleted_resources_total`, `kyverno_deleting_controller_deleted_resource_failures_total`, `kyverno_cleanup_controller_deleted_resources_total`, `kyverno_cleanup_controller_deleted_resource_failures_total`) carrying `resource_kind`, `resource_namespace`, and `resource_name` labels, enabling Prometheus alerting and dashboards at individual resource granularity.

## Related issue

Closes #1493

@JimBugwadia — following your guidance from the Kyverno Slack: _"all policy types should support the same events, metrics, logs, and reports. PRs are always welcome."_

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.15.0

## Proposed Changes

### Summary of changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pkg/utils/report/source.go` | Add `SourceDeletingPolicy` and `SourceCleanupPolicy` string constants |
| `pkg/utils/report/results.go` | Add `DeletingPolicyToReportResult()` and `CleanupPolicyToReportResult()` helpers that convert a deleted resource + outcome into an `openreportsv1alpha1.ReportResult` |
| `pkg/controllers/deleting/report.go` | New `reportWriter` — creates or replaces a `ClusterPolicyReport` (DeletingPolicy) or `PolicyReport` (NamespacedDeletingPolicy) after each execution cycle |
| `pkg/controllers/deleting/controller.go` | Wire `reportWriter`; collect per-resource `deletionRecord`s during the deletion loop; call new per-resource metrics |
| `pkg/controllers/deleting/report_test.go` | 7 unit tests: cluster-scoped create, update idempotency, error result, empty run, namespaced create, helper pass/error |
| `pkg/controllers/cleanup/report.go` | New `cleanupReportWriter` — same pattern for `CleanupPolicy` / `ClusterCleanupPolicy` |
| `pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller.go` | Wire `cleanupReportWriter`; call new per-resource metrics |
| `pkg/metrics/deleting.go` | Extend `DeletingMetrics` interface; implement 2 new per-resource counters |
| `pkg/metrics/cleanup.go` | Extend `CleanupMetrics` interface; implement 2 new per-resource counters |

### Design decisions

- Each execution run **replaces** the previous `(Cluster)PolicyReport` results rather than appending, so the report always reflects the latest run without unbounded growth.
- Per-resource Prometheus labels (`resource_name`) are scoped to deletion events only — cardinality is bounded because only resources that matched the policy and were attempted for deletion are recorded.
- No new CRDs — uses the existing `wgpolicyk8s.io/v1alpha2` `PolicyReport` / `ClusterPolicyReport` CRDs already required by Kyverno.
- All new metric interface methods have nil-guards; existing aggregate metrics (`kyverno_deleting_controller_deletedobjects`, etc.) are unchanged — fully backwards compatible.

title: feat(webhook): minimize webhook registration scope with ValidatingAdmissionPolicy autogen
author: jasdeepbhalla
head: jasdeepbhalla:feat/minimize-webhook-scope-with-vap-autogen
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

Fixes #15761.

When a `ValidatingPolicy` sets `spec.autogen.validatingAdmissionPolicy.enabled=true`, Kyverno now also generates native `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` resources for each autogenerated pod-controller variant (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, ReplicaSet, Job, CronJob). Admission webhook registration for those kinds is then skipped, since the API server's in-process VAP handles them instead of Kyverno's external webhook.

**Before:** Enabling `spec.autogen.validatingAdmissionPolicy` on a `ValidatingPolicy` that also had pod-controller autogen active was silently blocked (`"pod controllers autogen is enabled"`). Kyverno always registered webhooks for all autogenerated controller kinds, making itself a single point of failure for those resources.

**After:**
- Base pod policy → native VAP (`vpol-<name>`)
- Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/ReplicaSet/Job group → native VAP (`vpol-<name>-autogen-defaults`)
- CronJob → native VAP (`vpol-<name>-autogen-cronjobs`)
- Kyverno webhook only covers resource kinds whose policies cannot be expressed as VAP

title: feat: allow HTTP headers and caBundle in ServiceCall to reference Secret/ConfigMap values
author: jakharmonika364
head: jakharmonika364:feat/globalcontextentry-valuefrom
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

`ServiceCall` HTTP headers and `caBundle` currently require values to be written inline in the policy spec, which means credentials and certificates end up hardcoded in plain text. This PR adds `valueFrom`/`caBundleFrom` fields that let you source those values from a Kubernetes Secret or ConfigMap instead - similar to how pod env vars work. This is an addition to existing behavior; nothing breaks if you keep using inline values.

## Related issue

Closes #14776 

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.14.0

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. 
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:
  <!-- Uncomment to link to the PR -->
  <!-- https://github.com/kyverno/website/pull/123 -->

## What type of PR is this

/kind api-change
/kind feature

## Proposed Changes

Adds `valueFrom` to `HTTPHeader` and `caBundleFrom` to `ServiceCall`, both accepting a `secretKeyRef` or `configMapKeyRef` selector (same shape as pod env var sources, but with an explicit `namespace field` since GlobalContextEntry is cluster-scoped).
- Namespaced policies: `namespace` defaults to the policy's own namespace; cross-namespace refs are rejected
- Cluster-scoped contexts (GlobalContextEntry, ClusterPolicy): `namespace` must be set explicitly
- Secret values are base64-decoded automatically (Kubernetes stores Secret data as base64); ConfigMap values are used as-is
- Inline `value`/`caBundle` still work - the new fields are opt-in

### Proof Manifests

# Secret holding an API token:

```apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
  namespace: kyverno
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: "Bearer my-secret-token"
```

# GlobalContextEntry using valueFrom in a header:

```apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2beta1
kind: GlobalContextEntry
metadata:
  name: external-data
spec:
  apiCall:
    refreshInterval: 5m
    service:
      url: https://internal-api.example.com/data
      headers:
        - key: Authorization
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-creds
              namespace: kyverno
              key: token
```

# ClusterPolicy using caBundleFrom:

```apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: check-with-tls
spec:
  rules:
    - name: fetch-data
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: [Pod]
      context:
        - name: result
          apiCall:
            service:
              url: https://secure-api.example.com/check
              caBundleFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: ca-bundle
                  namespace: kyverno
                  key: ca.crt
```

title: fix(webhooks): propagate request context for toggle resolution in mpol handler
author: krrishverma1805-web
head: krrishverma1805-web:fix/webhook-context-propagation
action: Keep on main
body:
## Description

The `admissionResponse` method in the MutatingPolicy webhook handler used `context.TODO()` when resolving feature flags via `toggle.FromContext()`. This meant toggle resolution always fell back to default values instead of honoring any request-scoped toggle overrides that may have been set in the admission context.

This change threads the parent `context.Context` from `mutate()` through `admissionResponse()` so that `toggle.FromContext` receives the actual request context.

## Changes

- Added `ctx context.Context` as the first parameter to `admissionResponse()`
- Updated the call site in `mutate()` to pass the existing `ctx`
- Replaced `toggle.FromContext(context.TODO())` with `toggle.FromContext(ctx)`

title: feat: add admission warning for wildcard policies
author: CygnusMaximillian
head: CygnusMaximillian:feature/warn-wildcard-policies
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
I’m submitting this PR to help protect cluster performance. Right now, a user can create a policy that matches every single resource in a cluster using a wildcard (*) without being aware of how much load that puts on the system. This PR adds a friendly "heads-up" warning in the terminal when a user applies such a policy. It’s a non-breaking change—the policy will still work—but the user gets a clear signal that they might want to specify exact resource kinds to keep their cluster running smoothly.

Related issue
Closes #15488

Proposed Changes
I’ve focused on making this warning integrated and lightweight:

New Helper: I created a simple hasWildcard function in pkg/validation/policy/validate.go that scans both the match and exclude blocks for that * character.

Integrated Warning: I added a check in the main validation loop. If a wildcard is found, it appends a message to the admission response warnings. This ensures the message reaches the user's terminal during kubectl apply.

Testing: I’ve added a set of unit tests in validate_test.go to make sure we’re catching wildcards in different parts of the rule (both matching and excluding) and to confirm that the policy itself still validates correctly.

Challenges Faced
Since this is my very first time contributing to Kyverno, I had a bit of a learning curve:

Validation Layers: It took me a moment to figure out where the strict "error" logic ends and where a "warning" should live. I wanted to make sure I didn't accidentally block valid policies.

The Background Gotcha: My first round of tests failed because I didn't realize Kyverno assumes background processing is on by default. I learned that wildcards and background mode have a strict relationship, so I had to adjust my test manifests to account for that.

The CLI Side: I noticed the Kyverno CLI doesn't show these warnings yet. I decided to keep this PR focused on the core engine logic to get the foundation right first, and I’ll be happy to help with a CLI-specific fix in a follow-up.

Proof Manifests
Example Policy that Triggers the Warning
YAML
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: wildcard-check-example
spec:
  background: false
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: match-all-resources
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - "*"
    validate:
      message: "This is a wildcard policy."
      cel:
        expressions:
          - expression: "object.metadata.name != ''"

This PR fixes that gap by adding verbose logging throughout the `ImageValidatingPolicy` evaluation path — covering policy matching, image extraction, CEL expression results, and final outcomes.

The `ImageValidatingPolicy` CEL evaluation path had no logging instrumentation at any verbosity level.

Two files are changed:

  - Adds `V(4)` logs to `handleMutation()` and `handleValidation()`
  - Covers:

- whether CEL expressions were evaluated

title: fix(ivpol): verify sigstore bundles via sigstore-go to honour user-provided TSA chains
author: jimgus
head: jimgus:ivpol-bundle-via-sigstore-go-v2
action: Keep on main
body:
Closes #16084.

## Summary

When IVPOL verifies a sigstore bundle (`signatureFormat: bundle` / v3-bundle), it currently delegates to `cosign.VerifyImageAttestations`. For the keyless path that builds a `cosign.CheckOpts` carrying *both* `TrustedMaterial` (TUF root) and the legacy `TSACertificate / TSAIntermediateCertificates / TSARootCertificates` fields (populated from the policy's `tsaCertChain`), cosign v3 silently drops the legacy fields when `TrustedMaterial` is set ([sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847)). For users whose TSA isn't in any TUF root — GitHub `actions/attest-build-provenance` on private repos uses GitHub's per-tenant TSA — signed-timestamp verification fails with no indication the configured chain was ignored.

Per [@steiza's redirect on sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847#issuecomment-3500670921):

> cosign is intended to be used as a CLI, **not** a library […] If you want to verify a Sigstore bundle using Go code, my first recommendation would be to use sigstore-go.

This PR migrates IVPOL's bundle path off cosign-as-library, mirroring the sigstore-go-direct shape that CPOL's `pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go` already uses for the same purpose.

## What changed

### Routing — `verifier.go`

`VerifyImageSignature` and `VerifyAttestationSignature` route through `dispatchVerify` / `dispatchVerifyAttestations` (in `sigstore.go`):

| CheckOpts shape | IVPOL dispatches to | Underlying verifier |
|---|---|---|
| bundle + keyless (`co.NewBundleFormat && co.SigVerifier == nil && co.TrustedMaterial != nil`) | `verifyImageBundleAttestations` (new) | sigstore-go directly — with our composed `TrustedMaterial` |
| bundle + static-key (`co.SigVerifier != nil`) | `cosign.VerifyImageAttestations` | sigstore-go via cosign's `verifyImageAttestationsSigstoreBundle` — cosign handles this case correctly, no TSA chain to drop |
| non-bundle | `cosign.VerifyImageSignatures` / `cosign.VerifyImageAttestations` (unchanged) | cosign's traditional (non-bundle) verification — unaffected by the TSA-drop bug |

In other words: sigstore-go does the cryptographic work on **both** bundle paths; the bundle + keyless path is the only one where IVPOL needs to drive sigstore-go itself, because that's the only configuration where cosign drops the caller's TSA chain.

Dispatch is keyed on `co.SigVerifier == nil` rather than asserting `co.TrustedMaterial`'s concrete type. opts.go is the single producer of `TrustedMaterial` and may legitimately wrap it (this code also wraps it via `composeTrustedMaterial` → `TrustedMaterialCollection`), so a concrete-type assertion would silently route around the bug-fix path the first time `TrustedMaterial` isn't a bare `*root.TrustedRoot`.

### Bug-fixing primitive — `composeTrustedMaterial`

```go
func composeTrustedMaterial(
    publicRoot root.TrustedMaterial,
    customTSALeaf *x509.Certificate,
    customTSAIntermediates, customTSARoots []*x509.Certificate,
) (root.TrustedMaterial, error)
```

When a custom chain is provided, returns a `TrustedMaterialCollection` combining `publicRoot` with one `tsaOnlyTrustedMaterial` per root; otherwise returns `publicRoot` unchanged.

- **Roots-only chains** (no caller leaf) are honoured — sigstore-go's `SigstoreTimestampingAuthority.Verify` delegates to `tsaverification.VerifyTimestampResponse`, which documents `TSACertificate` as "Optional if the TSR contains the TSA certificate" and errors clearly when neither is available. This matches cpol/cosign's non-bundle path, which preserves leaf-less chains via `opts.go`.
- **Multi-root chains** produce one `SigstoreTimestampingAuthority` per root (all sharing the caller's leaf and intermediates), mirroring cpol/cosign's non-bundle handling that accepts a timestamp anchored at any of the caller's roots.

`tsaOnlyTrustedMaterial` is a thin wrapper around `root.SigstoreTimestampingAuthority` that only exposes `TimestampingAuthorities()`; everything else (Fulcio CAs, Rekor logs, CT logs) inherits empty defaults from `BaseTrustedMaterial`. The collection's other member (`publicRoot`) contributes those.

`TrustedMaterialCollection.TimestampingAuthorities()` aggregates from members → sigstore-go's verifier sees TSAs from both sources → bundles whose timestamp is signed by the caller's TSA verify successfully.

### Multi-identity (cosign-OR semantics)

`certificateIdentityOptions` returns one `WithCertificateIdentity` per `co.Identities` entry. sigstore-go's `CertificateIdentities.Verify` documents the OR contract — verification succeeds when the signing certificate matches *any* configured identity — so cosign's keyless-with-multiple-identities behaviour is preserved on the bundle path.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Half-specified identities are rejected, not silently skipped.** An `Identity` entry must configure both an issuer matcher (`issuer` or `issuerRegExp`) and a SAN matcher (`subject` or `subjectRegExp`); a half-specified entry returns a wrapped error naming every configured matcher. CPOL's bundle path and the non-bundle cosign path both silently fall back to a no-identity policy in the same case.
>
> Silent fallback is a quiet weakening: a misconfigured entry that the operator believes is constraining verification collapses the policy to digest-only with no signal back to admission. The hard-fail surfaces the misconfiguration at policy-build time as a clear *"fix your config"* error rather than at runtime as *"your verification is silently lax"*. The wrapped error names every configured matcher (`issuer`, `issuerRegExp`, `subject`, `subjectRegExp`), making typo'd field names trivial to spot in admission logs.
>
> Aligning CPOL and the non-bundle path the same way is a worthwhile follow-up.

## Test coverage

35 new unit tests across `composeTrustedMaterial`, `buildBundlePolicy`, `buildBundleVerifyOptions`, `certificateIdentityOptions`, `rejectAnnotationsOnBundlePath`, `bundleToOCISignature`, and the `tsaOnlyTrustedMaterial` wrapper. The bug-catching one is `TestComposeTrustedMaterial_AggregatesTSAsFromBothSources` — it asserts that a custom TSA chain reaches sigstore-go's verifier via the `TrustedMaterialCollection`, which is the configuration cosign-as-library silently breaks.

The full existing IVPOL test suite passes unchanged: `Test_GitHubAttestationVerification`, `TestConcurrentVerification` across v2-traditional / v3-traditional / v3-bundle, `TestVerifyImageSignature_ErrorCases`, etc.

## Scope

- **Bundle + keyless only**, by design. The bundle + static-key path and both non-bundle paths still go through `cosign.VerifyImageSignatures` / `cosign.VerifyImageAttestations`. They are not bug-affected (cosign doesn't drop TSA chains on those configurations) and re-implementing them here would balloon the review surface for paths that currently work. The end state @steiza describes — *all* sigstore-bundle verification driven by sigstore-go, with cosign confined to the CLI — would migrate those remaining paths off cosign-as-library too. That's the right direction; it's just bigger than this PR and would risk regressing paths that aren't broken.
- Only one IVPOL bundle path is rebuilt. CPOL already uses sigstore-go directly for the same purpose; a shared `internal/sigstore` package between them is the natural extraction point if the broader migration above is taken on.

title: fix: replace brittle strings.Contains with errors.As in anchor error matching
author: AftAb-25
head: AftAb-25:fix/anchor-error-propagation
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
Fixes #16068

## Description

This PR fixes a technical debt/bug in `pkg/engine/anchor/error.go` where the `isError` helper relied on string matching (`strings.Contains`) as a fallback when type assertions failed. 

The fallback was added because the `validateAnchorError` type was being lost when errors were wrapped upstream (like in `PatternError` or `multierr`). Relying on string matching is brittle and can lead to false positives if the error message happens to contain the anchor error substring (e.g., "conditional anchor mismatch").

**Changes included:**
- Removed the `strings.Contains` fallback in `anchor.isError` and replaced it with `errors.As` for proper Go 1.13+ error chain traversal.
- Added an `Unwrap()` method to `PatternError` in `validate.go` so `errors.As` can successfully traverse through it to find the underlying `validateAnchorError`.
- Removed the unused `msg` parameter and `strings` import in `error.go`.
- Updated `error_test.go` to use `fmt.Errorf("... %w", ...)` for testing wrapped errors and added explicit test cases to ensure plain strings no longer trigger false positives.

## Testing Done

- Ran `go test ./pkg/engine/anchor/... ./pkg/engine/validate/...` (all passed)
- Checked for any regressions with `go vet` and ensured formatting with `gofmt`

title: fix(ivpol): merge user-provided TSA chain into TrustedMaterial for bundle verification
author: jimgus
head: jimgus:ivpol-merge-tsa-into-trusted-material
action: Keep on main
body:
Refs #16054 (proposed primary fix is #16084; this PR is the alternative).

## Summary

Minimal-scope fix for a silent verification failure on the IVPOL bundle path: when the keyless attestor configures a `tsaCertChain`, the TSA cert ends up on `cosign.CheckOpts` as `TSACertificate / TSAIntermediateCertificates / TSARootCertificates` *and* `cosign.CheckOpts.TrustedMaterial` is set from the TUF-fetched root. cosign's `pkg/cosign.verificationOptions` (called from `verifyImageAttestationsSigstoreBundle` → `VerifyNewBundle`) wraps `co.TrustedMaterial` directly without folding in the legacy TSA fields, so sigstore-go's verifier never sees the caller-provided TSA. Bundles whose timestamp is signed by a TSA outside any TUF root (GitHub `actions/attest-build-provenance` on private repos uses GitHub's per-tenant TSA) fail to verify with no indication the configured chain was ignored.

This PR composes the public TrustedRoot and the parsed TSA chain into a `TrustedMaterialCollection` *before* assigning to `opts.TrustedMaterial`, in `checkOptions`. `TrustedMaterialCollection.TimestampingAuthorities()` aggregates from all its members, so cosign's wrapping passes the merged set through to sigstore-go and the bundle path verifies successfully.

> [!NOTE]
> **Held as alternative.** #16084 is the proposed primary fix — it migrates IVPOL's bundle path off cosign-as-library entirely, mirroring the sigstore-go-direct shape that CPOL already uses and matching [@steiza's recommendation on sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847#issuecomment-3500670921) ("cosign is intended to be used as a CLI, not a library"). This PR is the smaller, defensive option that stays on cosign-as-library and only fixes the trust-material composition gap at the call site. Available if the project would rather not take the larger architectural change now. Both produce the same end-user outcome on the affected case.

## Diff shape

| File | Δ |
|---|---|
| `pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/opts.go` | 4-line change at the `opts.TrustedMaterial = trustedRoot` assignment (calls the helper + propagates errors) |
| `pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/tsa_trusted_material.go` | new — tiny `tsaOnlyTrustedMaterial` wrapper and the `mergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial` helper |
| `pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/tsa_trusted_material_test.go` | new — 8 unit tests |

The legacy `CheckOpts.TSA*` fields are still populated; the non-bundle code path (`cosign.VerifyImageSignatures` / `VerifyImageAttestations` with `NewBundleFormat=false`) continues to read them directly and is unchanged.

## How `mergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial` works

```go
func mergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial(publicRoot *root.TrustedRoot, leaf *x509.Certificate, intermediates, roots []*x509.Certificate) (root.TrustedMaterial, error) {
    if publicRoot == nil {
        return nil, errors.New("public trusted root must not be nil")
    }
    if leaf == nil {
        return publicRoot, nil
    }
    if len(roots) == 0 {
        return nil, errors.New("custom TSA chain requires at least one root certificate")
    }
    customTSA := &root.SigstoreTimestampingAuthority{
        Root: roots[0], Intermediates: intermediates, Leaf: leaf,
    }
    return root.TrustedMaterialCollection{
        publicRoot,
        &tsaOnlyTrustedMaterial{tsa: customTSA},
    }, nil
}
```

`tsaOnlyTrustedMaterial` is a 5-line wrapper around `root.SigstoreTimestampingAuthority` that exposes only `TimestampingAuthorities()`; everything else (Fulcio CAs, Rekor logs, CT logs) inherits empty defaults from `BaseTrustedMaterial`. The collection's other member (`publicRoot`) contributes those.

## Test coverage (8 unit tests, all passing)

```
TestTSAOnlyTrustedMaterial_ExposesConfiguredTSA
TestTSAOnlyTrustedMaterial_OtherMethodsReturnDefaults

TestMergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial_NilPublicRootIsRejected
TestMergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial_NilLeafReturnsPublicRootUnchanged
TestMergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial_LeafWithoutRootIsRejected
TestMergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial_AggregatesTSAsFromBothSources
TestMergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial_ReturnsCollectionType
TestMergeTSAIntoTrustedMaterial_OnlyFirstRootIsUsed
```

The test surface deliberately mirrors `composeTrustedMaterial`'s in #16084 so reviewers can compare the two PRs without translating between API shapes. title: fix(apicall): add SSRF blocklist/allowlist enforcement for service calls
author: jakharmonika364
head: jakharmonika364:fix/15994-ssrf-apicall-url-validation-clean
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

Kyverno's APICall service calls had no URL validation. Any user with Policy creation permissions could point a policy at internal endpoints like 169.254.169.254 and have Kyverno fetch them using its own elevated ServiceAccount, leaking credentials or internal data in multi-tenant clusters.

This fix applies the same blocklist/allowlist enforcement that CEL http.Get/http.Post already uses to service calls as well. The existing --httpBlocklist, --httpAllowlist, and --allowHTTPInNamespacedPolicies flags now cover both paths.

## Related issue

Closes #15994

## Milestone of this PR


## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno. 
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:
  <!-- Uncomment to link to the PR -->
  <!-- https://github.com/kyverno/website/pull/123 -->

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

Two functions added to `pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go`:

- **`validateServiceURL`**  pre-flight check run before every service call. Validates the target hostname against hostname-based blocklist entries and enforces the allowlist if configured.

- **`secureDialContext`**   plugged into the HTTP transport's `DialContext`. Resolves the hostname once, validates every resolved IP against CIDR blocklist entries (e.g. `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1/128`), then connects directly to the already-resolved IP. Pinning to the resolved IP closes the DNS-rebinding window that would otherwise exist between validation and the actual `connect`
  syscall.

`buildHTTPClient` now always uses the secure dial context regardless of whether a CA bundle is provided.

In `pkg/engine/apicall/apiCall.go`, `Fetch` now explicitly checks the `AllowHTTPInNamespacedPolicies` toggle for service calls in namespaced policies, replacing a confusing `"path . does not contain a namespace segment"` error with a clear actionable message.

### Proof Manifests
Policy that would previously reach the AWS/GCP metadata service and is now blocked:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ssrf-demo
spec:
  rules:
    - name: fetch-metadata
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: [Pod]
      context:
        - name: meta
          apiCall:
            method: GET
            service:
              url: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/
      validate:
        message: "should never reach here"
        deny: {}
```

title: fix(ivpol): don't require rekor URL when InsecureIgnoreTlog is true
author: jimgus
head: jimgus:fix-ivpol-rekor-url-not-required-when-ignore-tlog
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

Bug fix. `ImageValidatingPolicy` (IVPOL) currently rejects a valid configuration where the user has explicitly opted out of Rekor verification (`ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog: true`) but has not set `ctlog.url`, with the error `getting Rekor public keys: rekor URL must be provided`. The same configuration on `ClusterPolicy verifyImages` is accepted today and works correctly. This PR brings IVPOL behaviour in line with CPOL — when the user has opted out of Rekor, the URL is not required.

The configuration is needed for verifying images attested by an out-of-tree TSA — for example, GitHub Actions Artifact Attestations on private repositories use GitHub's private TSA and have no Rekor entry by design, so there is no real `rekor.url` to provide.

## Related issue

Closes #16012

## Milestone of this PR

<!-- Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.2.3`. -->

## Documentation (required for features)

This is a bug fix; no documentation change is needed.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

`pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/opts.go` `checkOptions` calls `getRekor()` unconditionally before reading `att.CTLog.InsecureIgnoreTlog`, demanding a Rekor URL that will never be contacted. CPOL handles this correctly by gating Rekor setup behind `!opts.IgnoreTlog` ([pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/cosign.go:148-159](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/cosign.go#L148-L159)); this PR brings IVPOL to parity.

The fix short-circuits `getRekor()` when `ctlog.InsecureIgnoreTlog` is true, returning a nil Rekor client and no pub keys. Cosign downstream honours the `IgnoreTlog` flag and skips Rekor verification regardless of whether `RekorClient` is populated, so no client is needed in this case.

**Test changes:**

- New `TestCheckOptions_NoRekorURLNeededWhenIgnoreTlog` asserts the corrected behaviour. It fails on `main` (with the exact error from the linked issue) and passes with the fix.
- Existing `TestCheckOptions_MissingRekorURL` was codifying the bug — it set `InsecureIgnoreTlog: true` and asserted the URL-required error. Reworked to test the legitimate "missing URL when not ignoring tlog" case, preserving regression coverage of the real validation path.
- `TestCheckOptions_KeyBased` previously asserted a non-nil `RekorClient` even when `InsecureIgnoreTlog: true`. That assertion was leaning on the buggy behaviour. Updated to assert nil `RekorClient` in that case, matching CPOL semantics.

### Proof Manifests

The bug is in IVPOL's CheckOpts construction — purely an admission-time validation problem, with no Kubernetes resource semantics changed. The repro is a unit test in this PR (`TestCheckOptions_NoRekorURLNeededWhenIgnoreTlog`); the equivalent end-user manifest reproduction is documented in linked issue #16012 and is replicated below for reference.

```yaml
# Failing IVPOL on main; accepted with this PR applied.
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-keyless-no-rekor
spec:
  validationActions: [Audit]
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: [v1]
        operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
        resources: [pods]
  attestors:
    - name: gh
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
              subjectRegExp: https://github.com/example-org/.*/\.github/workflows/.*
        ctlog:
          insecureIgnoreSCT: true
          insecureIgnoreTlog: true
          # No url — the user has explicitly opted out of Rekor.
  attestations:
    - name: provenance
      intoto:
        type: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
```

The same use case is also blocked by [sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847) (cosign v3 silently dropping user-provided TSA chain when `TrustedMaterial` is set) and [sigstore/cosign#4846](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4846) (panic on empty `verifiedTimestamps`); PRs against cosign are filed for both. When a mutate policy test fails due to a resource mismatch, `kyverno test` previously only showed `Fail | Resource diff` with no details. The diff computed internally during mutate test evaluation was never printed unless `--detailed-results` was passed. This change calls `printDiffs()` after the results table in both the standard and `--fail-only` paths, showing the actual resource diff automatically on failure.

title: fix: enable Pod Security Standards relaxation for user namespace pods (hostUsers=false)
author: jakharmonika364
head: jakharmonika364:fix/15979-user-namespaces-pss
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

Kubernetes user namespaces (spec.hostUsers: false) reached general availability in Kubernetes 1.30. When a pod opts into user namespaces, root inside the container is mapped to a non-privileged user on the host, making certain Pod Security Standards (PSS) restrictions unnecessary. This PR fixes Kyverno's PSS evaluation so that pods with spec.hostUsers: false correctly skip the runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, and procMount checks matching the behavior defined by the Kubernetes PSS documentation. Previously, these checks were always enforced even for user namespace pods, causing false violations.

## Related issue

Closes https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15981


## Milestone of this PR

title: feat(gpol): add reconciler-backed compiled-policy cache
author: atharrva01
head: atharrva01:feat/gpol-compiled-policy-cache
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
While working on the background controller, I noticed something odd: **GeneratingPolicy** was the only CEL-based policy that still recompiled everything on every request. Each time an `UpdateRequest` ran, it would call `compiler.Compile()` from scratch rebuilding the CEL environment, loading 14 extension libraries, and recompiling every `matchCondition`, variable, and generation expression.

Meanwhile, **ValidatingPolicy** and **MutatingPolicy** had already solved this years ago with compiled-policy caches. GeneratingPolicy had simply never been brought up to the same standard.

So I fixed that.

I added a reconciler that watches both **GeneratingPolicy** and **NamespacedGeneratingPolicy** objects using controller-runtime. On create or update, it compiles the policy once and stores the result in a `sync.RWMutex`-protected cache. That means `Get()` calls now do a quick cache lookup instead of a full CEL recompile every time.

I also made sure **PolicyException** changes stay in sync. If an exception referencing a generating policy is updated, the reconciler requeues that policy so it gets recompiled with the latest exception state.

On the integration side, I wired `NewKubeProvider` into `cmd/background-controller/main.go`, replacing `NewFetchProvider`. The existing `ctrl.Manager` was already in place (used by mpol), so the swap was clean and didn’t require extra plumbing.

There was one subtle issue along the way: in this repo’s version of `k8s.io/apimachinery`, `types.NamespacedName{Name: "x"}.String()` returns `"/x"` instead of `"x"`. Since the background controller expects policy keys in `"name"` or `"namespace/name"` format, I added a small `policyKey()` helper instead of relying on `.String()`.

I kept the old `NewFetchProvider` as well, since it’s still useful in contexts without a manager, like the CLI and unit tests.

### What changed

* CEL expressions for **GeneratingPolicy** are now compiled once per policy change, not once per `UpdateRequest`
* Background controller CPU usage during generate-existing sweeps no longer scales with trigger-resource count
* PolicyException updates still trigger recompilation of affected policies

### Testing

I added **7 unit tests** covering:

* cache miss behavior
* storing compiled policies after reconcile
* cache removal on delete
* overwriting on update
* namespaced policy key formatting
* coexistence of cluster-scoped and namespaced policies
* concurrent reads protected by `sync.RWMutex`

title: [fix]: always re-arm cron schedule in cleanup and deleting controllers
author: Ady0333
head: Ady0333:fix/cleanup-deleting-cron-rearming
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

CleanupPolicy and DeletingPolicy controllers permanently stop executing after 10 cleanup errors, causing silent loss of policy enforcement. This occurs because the cron re-scheduling mechanism (`queue.AddAfter`) is only called on the success path - any transient error (finalizer-blocked deletion, flaky webhook, RBAC change, namespace cache miss) causes the policy to stop firing until pod restart or spec change. This PR fixes the issue by ensuring the cron schedule is always re-armed regardless of cleanup failures, while preserving the workqueue retry behavior for error handling.

---

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.13.0

---

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

---

## Proposed Changes

**Root Cause:**
Both `cleanup` and `deleting` controllers' `reconcile()` functions use early `return err` for cleanup and status-update failures inside the `if time.Now().After(*executionTime)` block. Since `queue.AddAfter` - the only mechanism that schedules the next cron tick - sits below that block, it becomes unreachable on any error path. After `maxRetries` (10), the workqueue calls `Forget()`, permanently removing the key.

**The Fix:**
- Capture cleanup/status errors in `execErr` instead of immediate return
- `queue.AddAfter` is now always reached (as long as the policy exists and has a parseable schedule)
- `execErr` is returned at the end, so the workqueue still rate-limits and retries partial failures
- Only behavioral change: policies with persistently failing cleanup passes continue firing on schedule instead of dying silently

**Impact:**
- **Before:** A policy with one sticky resource (finalizer, webhook issue) died after 10 retries. `LastExecutionTime` froze. No events, no visibility.
- **After:** Policy keeps firing on schedule, retrying the full cleanup pass each tick, until the underlying issue resolves.

**Files Changed:**
- `pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller.go` - Applied fix to CleanupPolicy reconcile
- `pkg/controllers/deleting/controller.go` - Applied identical fix to DeletingPolicy reconcile  
- `pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller_test.go` - Added regression test proving the bug and verifying fix

---

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have read the [AI Usage Policy](https://github.com/kyverno/community/blob/main/AI_USAGE_POLICY.md). If I used AI assistance, I have disclosed it in my commit(s) (e.g., via `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailer).
- [x] I have read the [PR documentation guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/pr_documentation.md) and followed the process including adding proof manifests to this PR.
- [x] This is a bug fix and I have added unit tests that prove my fix is effective.
- [ ] This is a feature and I have added CLI tests that are applicable.
- [ ] My PR needs to be cherry picked to a specific release branch which is <replace>.
- [ ] My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno and
  - [ ] CLI support should be added and my PR doesn't contain that functionality.

---

## Further Comments

This fix follows the principle that cron scheduling must be unconditional - it's a timer, not a retry mechanism. The workqueue already handles transient error retries via rate-limiting; the cron's job is to keep the policy firing on schedule. By separating these two concerns, we eliminate a class of silent failures where policies appear healthy (`kubectl get` shows no issues) but have stopped working.

The regression test proves both aspects: (1) cleanup errors are still propagated for workqueue retry logic, and (2) `queue.AddAfter` is called despite errors, ensuring the cron survives.

title: feat: add wildcard support for policyName in PolicyException
author: pierluigilenoci
head: pierluigilenoci:feat/wildcard-policyname-exception
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Problem

The `ruleNames` field in `PolicyException` supports wildcard matching (added in #6773), but `policyName` uses exact string comparison (`==`). This inconsistency forces users who need to exempt a resource from all policies to enumerate every policy name explicitly, which is verbose and brittle (breaks when new policies are added).

**Use case**: CRDs that share a `kind` name with native Kubernetes resources (e.g., Knative's `serving.knative.dev/v1 Service` vs core `v1 Service`) trigger Kyverno autogen rules intended for the native resource. Users need to exempt these resources from *all* policies, but currently must list every policy name individually.

## Solution

Two coordinated changes so that wildcard `policyName` works end-to-end:

1. **Match logic** (`api/kyverno/v2/policy_exception_types.go`) — replace the exact `==` comparison with `wildcard.Match()` in `Exception.Contains()`, consistent with how `ruleNames` are already matched. The `PolicyName` godoc is updated to document the supported pattern syntax.

2. **Index invalidation** (`pkg/controllers/exceptions/controller.go`) — when a `PolicyException` is added/updated/deleted, the exceptions controller re-indexes the policies it references. The previous code enqueued only the literal `PolicyName` string, so wildcard patterns never reached any policy until that policy was re-reconciled for some other reason. The new `enqueuePoliciesForExceptions` helper expands wildcard patterns by listing existing cluster and namespaced policies via the controller's listers and enqueuing every key that matches.

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward compatible. Existing PolicyExceptions with literal policy names continue to work identically — `wildcard.Match("exact-name", "exact-name")` returns `true`, same as `==`. The new helper short-circuits literals (`!wildcard.ContainsWildcard(...)`) so non-wildcard exceptions take exactly the same path as before.

## Changes

- `api/kyverno/v2/policy_exception_types.go` — switch `Exception.Contains()` to `wildcard.Match()`; document wildcard syntax on `PolicyName`.
- `api/kyverno/v2/policy_exception_types_test.go` — new table-driven tests covering exact match, `*`, `disallow-*`, `?`, `default/*`, and negative cases.
- `pkg/controllers/exceptions/controller.go` — extract a shared `enqueuePoliciesForExceptions` helper that resolves wildcard patterns to concrete policy keys via the cluster/namespaced policy listers; the existing `addPolex`/`updatePolex`/`deletePolex` handlers delegate to it.
- `pkg/controllers/exceptions/controller_test.go` — new tests using the fake clientset and a started informer factory: literal-only, `*` (match-all), `disallow-*` (cpol prefix), `default/*` (namespace-scoped only), mixed literal + wildcard.

## Test Results

```

--- PASS: TestExceptionContains (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/exact_policy_and_rule_match (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/exact_policy_match_with_wildcard_rule (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/wildcard_policy_match_with_exact_rule (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/wildcard_policy_and_wildcard_rule (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/policy_glob_pattern (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/policy_glob_pattern_no_match (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/policy_name_mismatch (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/rule_name_mismatch (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/namespaced_policy_with_wildcard (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/question_mark_wildcard_in_policy_name (0.00s)
    --- PASS: TestExceptionContains/question_mark_wildcard_no_match (0.00s)
PASS

=== RUN   TestEnqueuePoliciesForExceptions_Literal
--- PASS: TestEnqueuePoliciesForExceptions_Literal (0.10s)
=== RUN   TestEnqueuePoliciesForExceptions_WildcardMatchAll
--- PASS: TestEnqueuePoliciesForExceptions_WildcardMatchAll (0.10s)

title: fix(engine): checkpoint JSON context in validateOldObject to prevent false pre-existing violation skips
author: aabhinavvvvvvv
head: aabhinavvvvvvv:fix/cli-panic-image-registry-credentials
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

When a `ClusterPolicy` with `allowExistingViolations: true` evaluated an UPDATE request, Kyverno incorrectly skipped enforcement even when the *old* (pre-update) resource was valid. This is a bug fix: rule-level context variables (e.g. `jmesPath` bindings) were being reused from the new-object evaluation pass when validating the old object, causing the old object to falsely appear as a violation. Since both old and new appeared to fail, Kyverno concluded a pre-existing violation existed and skipped the rule — allowing an invalid UPDATE through.

## Related issue

Closes #15763

## Milestone of this PR


## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

Two fixes:

**1. Engine (`validate_resource.go`):** `validateOldObject` now checkpoints the JSON context before reloading rule-level context entries against the old resource, and restores it afterward via `defer`. This prevents stale variable bindings from the new-object pass from leaking into the old-object evaluation.

**2. CLI test framework (`policy_processor.go`):** `request.object` and `request.oldObject` values from `values.yaml` are now applied with replace semantics (`AddResource`/`AddOldResource`) instead of merge semantics (`AddVariable`). Previously the old object data was merged on top of the new resource data, contaminating `request.oldObject` with fields from the new resource.

### Proof Manifests

See `test/cli/test/allow-existing-violations-context-vars/` — a CLI test that reproduces the bug: an UPDATE that introduces an invalid label into a previously-valid resource should `fail`, but without this fix it `skip`s.

## Explanation

This PR addresses a potential runtime panic in the `buildStatementMap` function within the image verification logic. Specifically, it replaces an unsafe type assertion on the "type" field of an attestation statement with a safe, two-value type assertion. This prevents the admission controller from crashing if the "type" field is missing, `nil`, or not of type string.

- Updated `buildStatementMap` to return an `error` if the type assertion fails.
- Updated the caller `verifyAttestation` in `pkg/engine/internal/imageverifier.go` to handle and propagate the error.

title: fix(cli): prevent panic on webhook matchConditions in mock mode
author: Kunalbehbud
head: Kunalbehbud:fix/cli-webhook-matchconditions-panic
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
Fixes #15833

When `kyverno test` validates a `ClusterPolicy` that sets `spec.webhookConfiguration.matchConditions`, the CLI runs policy validation in mock mode with a nil Kubernetes client. The existing validation path still attempted to dereference the client for the Kubernetes version check, which caused a nil pointer dereference panic.

This change keeps the `matchConditions` validation path safe in mock mode by skipping the Kubernetes version check when `mock == true`, while still returning an explicit validation error if custom webhook configuration is validated outside mock mode without a client.

The change also adds regression coverage in `pkg/validation/policy` and a CLI fixture plus command test to verify that `kyverno test` handles this policy shape without panicking.

title: chore: migrate cert manager to shared kyverno/pkg/certmanager
author: alliasgher
head: alliasgher:refactor-migrate-certmanager-to-shared-pkg
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Summary

Remove the duplicated cert manager controller from `pkg/controllers/certmanager/` and use the shared implementation from `github.com/kyverno/pkg/certmanager` instead.

## Motivation

As noted in #15244, we have a duplicated cert manager controller — one in `kyverno/pkg` (shared) and one inside this repo (`pkg/controllers/certmanager/`). Both were functionally identical, so the internal copy can be removed.

## Changes

### Removed
- `pkg/controllers/certmanager/controller.go` (148 lines)
- `pkg/controllers/certmanager/log.go` (5 lines)

### Updated callers to import the shared package
- `cmd/kyverno/main.go`
- `cmd/cleanup-controller/main.go`
- `cmd/internal/metrics.go`

The shared package exports the same `ControllerName`, `Workers`, and a `NewController()` whose return value implements `Run(ctx, workers)` — fully compatible with the existing `internal.NewController()` wrapper.

### `NewController()` signature change
The shared package takes a `logr.Logger` and a `*tlsmgr.Config{ServiceName, Namespace}` instead of separate `caSecretName`, `tlsSecretName`, and `namespace` strings. The shared package derives secret names internally via `GenerateTLSPairSecretName` / `GenerateRootCASecretName`.

### Type compatibility
The existing internal `tls.NewCertRenewer` return value structurally satisfies the shared `CertRenewer` interface (identical methods: `RenewCA(ctx) error` and `RenewTLS(ctx) error`), so no changes to the cert renewer implementation are needed.

### Net code change: **-148, +27** lines

## Verification

- `go build ./...` passes
- `go vet ./...` passes
- `pkg/tls` tests pass
- `go.mod` updated with `github.com/kyverno/pkg/certmanager v0.0.10` and `github.com/kyverno/pkg/tls v0.0.9`

Fixes #15244

Fixes several issues with the Argo CD platform-specific notes:
- Add config.preserve=false to Complete Application Example
- Update Argo CD v3 tracking info (annotation-based by default since v3)
- Clarify 'appropriate annotations' with concrete example
- Fix webhookLabels -> config.webhookLabels (correct Helm nesting)

## Explanation

The Argo CD platform notes page had several inaccuracies and missing details
that could confuse users trying to deploy Kyverno via Argo CD. This PR is a
fix to bring the documentation up to date and fill in the gaps:

- The "Complete Application Example" was missing `config.preserve=false` even
  though the section above it explicitly recommends setting it — that
  inconsistency is now fixed.
- The page stated that Argo CD "automatically sets the app.kubernetes.io/instance
  label" for tracking, but this is no longer the default since Argo CD v3
  (released May 2025), which switched to annotation-based tracking by default.
  The docs now clearly cover both Argo CD v2 and v3 behavior.
- The phrase "Add appropriate annotations to your Application manifest" gave
  users no idea what annotations to actually add. Concrete YAML examples are
  now provided.
- The Complete Application Example used a top-level `webhookLabels:` Helm key,
  but the correct path in the Kyverno Helm chart is `config.webhookLabels`.
  The top-level key silently does nothing — this is now corrected with a
  callout note.
- It was never explained *why* the webhook labels are set or what each one
  does. A new "Webhook Labels" best practice item now covers this clearly for
  both Argo CD v2 and v3 users.

title: Fix event broadcasting log verbosity (#9581)
author: Rama542
head: Rama542:fix-9581-event-logging-verbosity
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
### Explanation
This PR bumps up the log level for the event broadcaster to stop console spam. Right now, if you run Kyverno with --v=1, the console still gets flooded with info logs saying "Event occurred" every time a mutation happens. This change just quiets that down so those event logs only show up when you actually want them (like at --v=3).

### Related issue
Closes #9581

### Milestone of this PR
### Documentation (required for features)
- [ ]  I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

### What type of PR is this
/kind cleanup
### Proposed Changes
Updated `eventBroadcaster.StartStructuredLogging()` parameter from `0` to `3` in the policy controller initialization. This ensures event mutations only appear in standard out at verbosity level 3 or higher, instead of spamming default `--v=1` levels.

### Proof Manifests
Here is a ConfigMap and mutate policy you can use to prove this works. When you run Kyverno with `--v=1` with this code, you will no longer see the "Event occurred" spam.
Kubernetes resource

`apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: test-cm
  namespace: default`
Kyverno Mutation Policy
`apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: mutate-cm
spec:
  rules:
  - name: mutate-test-configmap
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - ConfigMap
          names:
          - test-cm
    mutate:
      patchStrategicMerge:
        metadata:
          labels:
            mutated: "true"`

title: fix(logging): reduce klog Event occurred noise at -v 0–1
author: vikash232
head: vikash232:fix/logging-klog-event-noise-9581
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

When the admission controller runs with `--v=1`, Kubernetes client-go still emits a high volume of structured klog lines with the fixed message `Event occurred` for **Normal** events (for example policy applied / resource mutated). Those calls use `klog.InfoS` at logr verbosity 0, so they are not gated by the numeric `-v` threshold in the same way as Kyverno’s own `logging.V(n)` messages. This change wraps the logr sink passed to `klog.SetLogger` so that **Normal** `Event occurred` lines are dropped when `-v` is **0 or 1**, while **Warning** events and all klog output at `-v>=2` stay available for debugging. This is a behavior fix for noisy logging at low verbosity.

## Related issue

Closes #9581

- Add `klogVerbosityFilterSink` in `pkg/logging` implementing `logr.LogSink` and `logr.CallDepthLogSink`, delegating to the existing zerologr sink.
- In `logging.Setup`, pass the klog logger through this wrapper using the same `-v` value as `zerologr.SetMaxV`.
- Unit tests cover Normal vs Warning events and maxV 1 vs 2.

title: feat: add catchError support to imageRegistry context variable
author: jakharmonika364
head: jakharmonika364:feature/image-registry-graceful-fail-14302
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

When using imageRegistry as a context variable, if the image doesn't exist (e.g. deleted from the registry), the entire policy fails with an error. This makes it impossible to use preconditions to gracefully handle missing images, the error fires before preconditions are even evaluated.

This PR adds a catchError field to the ImageRegistry spec. When set to true, fetch errors are captured into the context variable as failed: true and errorMessage: "<error>" instead of failing the rule. This lets users write preconditions to check for failures and skip rules accordingly, without breaking existing behavior (default is false).

## Related issue

Closes #14302

- On successful fetch, the returned map now also includes failed: false and errorMessage: "" for consistency.

title: fix: resolve mutate.targets core resources correctly in load_target
author: MatiasRoje
head: MatiasRoje:fix/mutate-target-gvr-resolution
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

This fixes a bug in the legacy `ClusterPolicy` mutate path.

When a target uses `apiVersion: v1`, Kyverno should resolve it as a core resource. In this case it was parsed too loosely, so a target like `Service` could be resolved against a different API group that has the same kind name. As an example, with Knative installed, Kyverno would try to look up `services.serving.knative.dev` instead of core `v1/Service`.

This PR fixes that by parsing `target.APIVersion` as a real group/version and keeping the target kind handling separate.

The new `MutatingPolicy` API is not affected by this issue.

## Related issue

#12455 (closed due to staleness)
Closes kyverno/policies#1263, currently open downstream although the fix needed to be done here

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- In `pkg/engine/handlers/mutation/load_targets.go`, stop using `ParseKindSelector` for `target.APIVersion` and parse `target.APIVersion` with `schema.ParseGroupVersion` instead.
- Keep subresource parsing based on `target.Kind`.
- Add focused unit tests for:
  - core API group targets like `v1/Service`
  - grouped targets like `serving.knative.dev/v1`
  - kind/subresource values like `Deployment/status`

This keeps core resources mapped to the empty API group (`""`) instead of treating them like a wildcard.

## Proof Manifests

**Policy**
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: remove-zone-label-when-no-endpoints
spec:
  background: false
  rules:
    - name: remove-zone-selector-on-empty-endpoints
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Endpoints"]
              namespaces: ["default"]
              names: ["demo-frontend"]
              operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE", "DELETE"]
      preconditions:
        all:
          - key: "{{ request.object.subsets || `[]` | length(@) }}"
            operator: Equals
            value: 0
      mutate:
        targets:
          - apiVersion: v1
            kind: Service
            name: "demo-frontend"
            namespace: "default"
        patchesJson6902: |-
          - op: remove
            path: /spec/selector/zone-dedicated-service-name
```

**Service**
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: demo-frontend
  namespace: default
spec:
  selector:
    app: demo-frontend
    zone-dedicated-service-name: hello
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
```

**Deployment (for triggering the policy you would need to scale it down to 0)**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: demo-frontend
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: demo-frontend
      zone-dedicated-service-name: demo-frontend
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: demo-frontend
        zone-dedicated-service-name: demo-frontend
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:1.27
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
```

**RBAC**
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: kyverno:bg-controller:services
  labels:
    rbac.kyverno.io/aggregate-to-background-controller: "true"
rules:
  - apiGroups:
      - ""
    resources:
      - services
    verbs:
      - get
      - update
      - patch
```

title: fix(cleanup-controller): implement real TLS health probes
author: atharrva01
head: atharrva01:feature/cleanup-controller-probes
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
**Problem**

`IsReady` was a stub that always returned `true`, so the pod showed `1/1 READY` even before TLS certs were provisioned. Webhook traffic would come in, the handshake would fail, and the error showed up as a cryptic admission failure on `CleanupPolicy` ops, nowhere near the actual cause.

**What I changed**

Added a `tls.CertValidator` and a `logr.Logger` to the `probes` struct. `IsReady` now calls `ValidateCert(ctx)` and logs any error before returning `false`, so operators can actually tell why the pod is stuck not ready. `IsLive` is unchanged.

Instead of creating a separate renewer just for the probe, I moved the single `*certRenewer` to the outer scope and reuse it for both the readiness probe (`CertValidator`) and the cert rotation controller (`CertRenewer`), no duplicated constructor args.

Added 4 unit tests for `IsReady` and `IsLive` using a mock validator and `logr.Discard()`.

title: Honor stderrthreshold when logtostderr is enabled
author: pierluigilenoci
head: pierluigilenoci:fix/honor-stderrthreshold
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Summary

- Opt into the new klog behavior by setting `-legacy_stderr_threshold_behavior=false` so that `-stderrthreshold` is honored even when `-logtostderr=true` (the klog default).
- Set `stderrthreshold=INFO` to preserve backward-compatible behavior (all logs still appear on stderr by default). Users can now override `-stderrthreshold` to `WARNING` or `ERROR` to reduce stderr noise.

This project already uses klog v2.140.0 which includes the fix. This PR just enables it.

## Background

When `-logtostderr=true` (klog's default), the `-stderrthreshold` flag was completely ignored — all log levels were written to stderr. Log aggregation systems that infer severity from the output stream (stdout=INFO, stderr=ERROR) would misclassify every log message as an error.

klog v2.140.0 (kubernetes/klog#432) introduced a fix behind the `-legacy_stderr_threshold_behavior` flag. Setting it to `false` enables proper severity-based filtering.

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing tests pass
- [ ] Deploy with default configuration — all logs appear on stderr (backward compatible)
- [ ] Deploy with `-stderrthreshold=WARNING` — only WARNING and above appear on stderr

Ref: kubernetes/klog#212, kubernetes/klog#432

title: fix(cli): correctly report test failures for excluded resources
author: jakharmonika364
head: jakharmonika364:fix-issue-12198
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation
Currently, the Kyverno CLI unconditionally reports excluded resources as a successful `Pass`, completely ignoring whatever the user configured in `test.Result`. This fix ensures that if a resource gets skipped/excluded, but the test specifically expected it to fail, the CLI correctly logs it as a test failure.

title: fix: handle wildcard `match.resource` selectors in background policy processing
author: omad
head: omad:fix-wildcard-resource-selectors
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
## Explanation

Policies with `generateExisting` or mutate-existing rules can fail during policy reconciliation when `match.resources.selector.matchLabels` contains Kyverno wildcard patterns such as `*` or `?`. 

When processing these policies, Kyverno lists existing resources from the K8s API server. However, it doesn't map the wildcards to the form K8s will accept like happens elsewhere, and K8s rejects them. This causes trigger discovery to fail and existing matching resources are skipped.

This change fixes wildcard selector handling in those cases, so policies using wildcard label matches will reconcile existing resources correctly.

title: feat(cli): add mock APICall and GlobalContextEntry support for kyverno test
author: Rohanraj123
head: Rohanraj123:fix/update-context-loader
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation
### Offline Mock Support for `kyverno test`: APICall and GlobalContextEntry

---

## Problem

Policies that depend on **external HTTP services** (`context.apiCall.service` in v1, `http.Get()`/`http.Post()` in CEL) or **GlobalContextEntry** resources (`context.globalReference` in v1, `globalContext.Get()` in CEL) cannot be tested offline with `kyverno test`. The CLI has no cluster, no live services, and no global context store -- so these policies either fail or must be tested only in a live cluster.

This blocks a significant class of policies from being validated in CI/CD, local development, and PR workflows.

---

## Solution

Extend the `kyverno-test.yaml` spec with two new **optional** fields that let users declare static mock data inline:

```yaml
# Mock an external HTTP service response
mockAPICallResponses:
  - urlPath: "https://external-service.example.com/api/check"
    response:
      statusCode: 200
      body:
        allowed: true

# Mock a GlobalContextEntry
mockGlobalContextEntries:
  - name: gctxentry-deployments
    data:
      items:
        - name: existing-deployment-1
```

Both fields are optional and additive. Existing tests are completely unaffected.

---

## Architecture: Two Engines, Two Mock Injection Points

Kyverno has two separate policy evaluation paths. Each needs its own mock injection because they use different internal APIs:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph testYAML [kyverno-test.yaml]
    mockAPI["mockAPICallResponses"]
    mockGCE["mockGlobalContextEntries"]
  end

  subgraph v1Engine [v1 Engine - ClusterPolicy/Policy]
    ctxLoader["store/contextloader.go wrapper.Load()"]
    gctxStore["store/mock.go mockGCtxStore"]
  end

  subgraph celEngine [CEL Engine - ValidatingPolicy/MutatingPolicy/etc.]
    httpMock["libs/http_mock.go mockHTTPContext"]
    fakeCtx["libs/fake_context.go FakeContextProvider"]
  end

  mockAPI -->|"v1: intercept context entries by URL"| ctxLoader
  mockAPI -->|"CEL: SetHTTPMockResponses"| httpMock
  mockGCE -->|"v1: WithGlobalContextStore"| gctxStore
  mockGCE -->|"CEL: AddGlobalReference"| fakeCtx
```



**Why two paths, not one?**

- The **v1 engine** loads context via `pkg/engine/apicall` (real `http.Client` and `client.Do(req)`) and `pkg/engine/context/loaders/globalcontext.go` (reads from a `Store` interface). Neither touches CEL libs.
- The **CEL engine** evaluates `http.Get()` via the SDK's `http.ContextInterface` and `globalContext.Get()` via the `libs.Context` interface. Neither touches the v1 context loader.

A unified mock layer would require refactoring the core engine, which is out of scope. Instead, the test command reads mock data once and injects it into both paths.

---

## Key Design Decisions

**1. `runtime.RawExtension` for arbitrary JSON**
Mock body/data can be any JSON shape. Using `runtime.RawExtension` (instead of `interface{}`) makes the types compatible with `controller-gen` CRD generation. A helper `RawExtensionToObject()` decodes at use sites.

**2. Scoped lifecycle for CEL HTTP mocks**
The global `httpMockResponses` is set at the start of `runTest()` and cleared with `defer`. A `sync.RWMutex` guards concurrent reads. Tests run sequentially, so no cross-test leakage.

**3. v1 APICall mock via context entry interception**
In `wrapper.Load()`, mock URL entries are matched against `entry.APICall.Service.URL`. Matched entries are resolved from mock data and removed from the list before passing to the inner loader. Unmatched entries proceed normally (e.g. K8s API path calls still work with `clusterResources`).

**4. v1 GlobalContext mock via factory option**
`WithGlobalContextStore(NewMockGCtxStore(...))` plugs a mock store into the standard `DefaultContextLoaderFactory`. The mock store implements `loaders.Store` and `store.Entry` -- the same interfaces the real global context store uses.

---

## Backward Compatibility


| Scenario                          | Behavior                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Test YAML without mock fields     | Zero-value slices; no mock logic runs; identical to before                                                                              |
| `kyverno apply` (no test context) | `MockGlobalContextEntries` field is zero; `NewContextProvider` variadic is empty; CEL `GetHTTPContext()` returns default `NewHTTP(nil)` |
| Existing `clusterResources` tests | `AllowApiCall` still works; mock URL interception only activates when `mockAPICallResponses` is non-empty                               |


No engine code (`pkg/engine/`) is modified. All changes are in CLI-only paths (`cmd/cli/`) and the CEL libs fake/mock layer (`pkg/cel/libs/`).

---

## Files Changed


| Area              | Files                                                                                 | Purpose                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Test API**      | `cmd/cli/.../apis/v1alpha1/test.go`                                                   | New types + `RawExtensionToObject` helper                  |
| **CRD**           | `cmd/cli/.../config/crds/cli.kyverno.io_tests.yaml`                                   | Generated CRD with new fields                              |
| **Test command**  | `cmd/cli/.../commands/test/test.go`                                                   | Wire mocks into both engines                               |
| **Store**         | `cmd/cli/.../store/store.go`, `contextloader.go`, `mock.go`                           | v1 engine mock injection                                   |
| **Processor**     | `cmd/cli/.../processor/policy_processor.go`, `utils.go`                               | Pass mock global context to CEL `NewContextProvider`       |
| **CEL libs**      | `pkg/cel/libs/fake_context.go`, `http_mock.go`                                        | `FakeContextProvider.AddGlobalReference` + HTTP mock       |
| **CEL compilers** | `pkg/cel/policies/{vpol,mpol,gpol,dpol}/compiler/compiler.go`                         | Use `libs.GetHTTPContext()` instead of `http.NewHTTP(nil)` |
| **Test fixtures** | `test/cli/test/mock-global-context/`, `mock-apicall-responses/`, `cel-http-get-mock/` | End-to-end CLI test cases                                  |
| **Unit tests**    | `fake_context_test.go`, `http_mock_test.go`, `mock_test.go`                           | Unit coverage for all new code                             |


---

## Test Coverage

- **3 new CLI test suites** covering: v1 APICall mock, v1+CEL GlobalContext mock, CEL `http.Get()` mock
- **Unit tests** for `FakeContextProvider`, `mockHTTPContext`, `mockGCtxStore`, `buildMockAPICallURLIndex`
- All **222 existing CLI tests** continue to pass (verified locally)

---

## Bonus: golangci-lint Fixes

This branch also fixes all **37 pre-existing golangci-lint issues** (3 `gosec` G118 goroutine context + 34 `prealloc`) across 25+ files. These are independent quality improvements included for a clean lint pass.


## Related issue

Closes #15427
