title: use NamespaceLister for CEL validation namespace lookups
author: nishanthreddydd
head: nishanthreddydd:feat/cel-namespace-lister-main
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
Use a cached NamespaceLister in the CEL validation handler instead of making direct API calls to fetch namespace objects, improving performance and reducing API server load during policy evaluation.


## Explanation

Currently, the CEL validation handler fetches namespace objects by making direct API calls to the Kubernetes API server (client.GetNamespace()) for every policy evaluation that needs namespace context. In high-throughput admission webhook scenarios, this creates unnecessary load on the API server. This PR adds support for using a cached NamespaceLister (backed by a shared informer) for namespace lookups in the CEL validation handler, falling back to the existing API call behavior when the lister is not available. This is a performance improvement for existing CEL validation behavior.

## Related issue

I haven't created an issue for it but the same kind of optimization is done for VPOL performance : https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pull/13572 

This PR addresses performance concerns observed when running CEL validation policies at scale, where repeated API server calls to fetch namespace objects during policy evaluation caused increased latency and API server load.

## Milestone of this PR
/milestone 1.15.x

## Proposed Changes

> - Added a nsLister (corev1listers.NamespaceLister) field to the engine struct and threaded it through NewEngine() and cmd/internal.NewEngine().
> - Updated NewValidateCELHandler to accept and store a NamespaceLister.
> - In the CEL validation handler's Process method, namespace lookups now prefer the cached NamespaceLister when available, falling back to the existing client.GetNamespace() API call when it is not.
> - The main kyverno admission controller (cmd/kyverno) passes the namespace lister from the kube shared informer factory. Background controller, reports controller, and CLI pass nil (retaining existing behavior).

title: Add wildcard detection and emit policy warning events
author: rishabh998186
head: rishabh998186:fix/wildcard-policy-warnings-events
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation ##
This PR implements warnings and events for Kyverno policies that use wildcard (*) matching or exclusion logic. Wildcard policies can impose a high load on the API server and potentially degrade cluster performance. This change ensures users are warned during policy creation/update and that a  `PolicyWarning`                   event is emitted for visibility.


## Related issue ##
Closes #15488

## What type of PR is this ##
/kind feature

## Changes ##

Created a new  utility file `wildcard.go` which  providing the  `HasWildcard` function. It comprehensively scans match and exclude blocks in Kyverno rules, and `MatchConstraints` in CEL-based or Admission policies. It also defines the global WildcardWarning constant. 
In `event.go` I  Implemented a func `NewPolicyWarningEvent` which handles metadata extraction for all policy types (v1, v1beta1, etc.) to ensure the event's Regarding field is accurately populated 

and in `handlers.go`  I integrated the `event.Generator` into the policy admission webhook which emits a `PolicyWarning` event immediately when a wildcard policy is created or updated.

other changes like in `controller.go` Updated the `PolicyStatusController` to check for wildcards during status reconciliation. This provides persistent coverage, ensuring events are emitted for existing policies whenever their status is updated.

In `main.go` Updated the instantiation of the `PolicyStatusController` to pass the  `eventGenerator` , fulfilling the new structural dependency.

Modified the apply command in `command.go` to capture and display validation warnings returned by Kyverno's engine or the CLI's internal validation, providing immediate feedback to users during local development.

`test.go` Mirrored the warning display logic in the test command for a consistent user experience.

 Added `Test_NewPolicyWarningEvent` in `events_test.go` to verify that events are correctly constructed with the right policy coordinates.

## test ##

Kyverno Policy (Wildcard)
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: warn-all-kinds
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: false
  rules:
  - name: check-all
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - "*"
    validate:
      message: "Testing wildcard warning"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          name: "*"
```

```
$ kyverno apply wildcard-policy.yaml --resource dummy-ns.yaml
Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...
Policy Warning: wildcard policy adds high load to the API server and can bring down a cluster
pass: 1, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0
```

```
$ kubectl get events -A --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | grep PolicyWarning
default   5s   Warning   PolicyWarning   clusterpolicy/warn-all-kinds   wildcard policy adds high load to the API server and can bring down a cluster
```

title: feat(ivpol): add CEL expression support for keyless identity fields
author: jzeng4
head: jzeng4:juzeng/cel
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR adds CEL expression support to the `issuer`, `subject`, `issuerRegExp`, and `subjectRegExp` fields of the `Identity` type in `ImageValidatingPolicy`'s keyless (Fulcio/Sigstore) configuration. Previously these fields only accepted static strings, which forced users to write one policy per image when they needed per-image signing identity pinning. With this change, each field accepts either a plain string (unchanged) or a `{expression: "..."}` CEL expression that is evaluated at admission time with full access to the request context — enabling a single policy to enforce precise per-image signing identities across an entire organization.

This is a backward-compatible addition: all existing policies using plain string values continue to work without modification.

## Related issue

Fixes https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15398
Depend on https://github.com/kyverno/api/pull/64

## Milestone of this PR

<!--
Add the milestone label by commenting `/milestone 1.2.3`.
-->

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno.
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

## What type of PR is this

/kind api-change
/kind feature

## Proposed Changes

The `Identity` struct fields (`issuer`, `subject`, `issuerRegExp`, `subjectRegExp`) are changed from plain `string` to `*StringOrExpression` — the same union type already used for `cert`, `certChain`, and Notary `certs` fields. A custom `UnmarshalJSON` on `StringOrExpression` ensures that a plain YAML string (e.g. `issuer: "https://..."`) is transparently decoded into `StringOrExpression{Value: "..."}`, so no existing policies need to be updated.

At policy compile time, any `{expression: "..."}` values are compiled into CEL programs. At admission time, those programs are evaluated against the full request context (including `object`, `images`, `request`, and `variables`) and their string results are substituted as the identity values passed to cosign's `CheckOpts.Identities`. This means `subject` and `subjectRegExp` are matched against the Fulcio certificate's SAN URI, and `issuer`/`issuerRegExp` against the OIDC issuer OID extension, exactly as before — the only difference is the values can now be computed rather than hardcoded.

Changes:
- `api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/imagevalidating_policy.go` — change `Identity`
  fields to `*StringOrExpression`; add backward-compatible `UnmarshalJSON` on
  `StringOrExpression`
- `api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/zz_generated.deepcopy.go` — update
  `Identity.DeepCopyInto` and `Keyless.DeepCopyInto` for the new pointer fields
- `pkg/imageverification/variables/attestors.go` — compile and evaluate CEL expressions
  for identity fields
- `pkg/imageverification/imageverifiers/cosign/opts.go` — read `.Value` from pointer
  fields when building `cosign.CheckOpts`

### Proof Manifests

#### Example 1: Backward-compatible plain string (no change needed)

Existing policies continue to work unchanged:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-keyless-static
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  attestors:
    - name: sigstore
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subject: "https://github.com/my-org/my-repo/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main"
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.sigstore])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: Image signature verification failed.
```

#### Example 2: Derive subject from a pod label (per-repo identity, one policy for all services)

The expected signer workflow is derived from the `github-repo` pod label at admission
time. `subject` and `subjectRegExp` match against the Fulcio certificate's SAN URI;
`issuer`/`issuerRegExp` match against the OIDC issuer OID extension on the certificate.

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-keyless-cel-identity
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  attestors:
    - name: sigstore
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer:
                value: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subject:
                expression: >-
                  "https://github.com/" + object.metadata.labels["github-repo"] +
                  "/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main"
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.sigstore])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: >-
        Image signature verification failed. The image must be signed by the
        GitHub Actions workflow for the repository specified in the 'github-repo' label.
```

Pod that is admitted (label matches the signing identity):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: my-app
  labels:
    github-repo: "my-org/my-app"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: ghcr.io/my-org/my-app:v1.2.3
```

Pod that is denied (label does not match the actual signing identity):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: untrusted-app
  labels:
    github-repo: "my-org/other-repo"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: ghcr.io/my-org/my-app:v1.2.3
```

#### Example 3: Derive subject from the namespace

Enforce a per-team signing convention where each namespace maps to a GitHub org team:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-keyless-by-namespace
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  attestors:
    - name: sigstore
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer:
                value: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subjectRegExp:
                expression: >-
                  "^https://github\\.com/my-org/" + object.metadata.namespace + "/.*"
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.sigstore])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: >-
        Image must be signed by a workflow belonging to the GitHub repository
        matching this pod's namespace.
```

#### Example 4: Derive subject from the image reference (single-container pods)

Use `images.containers[0]` to extract the org and repo from the image reference itself.
Note: this approach works reliably for single-container pods; for multi-container pods,
use a pod label (Example 2) or policy variable instead.

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-keyless-from-image-ref
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  attestors:
    - name: sigstore
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer:
                value: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subjectRegExp:
                expression: >-
                  "^https://github\\.com/" +
                  images.containers[0].split("/")[1] + "/" +
                  images.containers[0].split("/")[2].split(":")[0] + "/.*"
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.sigstore])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: >-
        Image must be signed by a workflow from the same GitHub repository as the image.
```

### Available CEL variables in identity expressions

Identity expressions are evaluated once per admission request with the same context
available to `validations` expressions:

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | dynamic | The K8s resource being admitted |
| `images` | `map<string, list<string>>` | e.g. `images.containers`, `images.initContainers` |
| `request` | object | Admission request (`.namespace`, `.name`, `.userInfo`) |
| `namespaceObject` | object | The namespace object |
| `variables` | object | Policy-defined variables |

## Further Comments

The design deliberately mirrors the existing `StringOrExpression` pattern used for
`cert`, `certChain`, and Notary `certs` fields, keeping the API consistent. The

title: fix: failurePolicy not working for image verification.
author: lucchmielowski
head: lucchmielowski:fix-cpol-registry-error
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
## Explanation

Given the `failurePolicy` feature :

>    FailurePolicy defines how unrecognized errors from the admission endpoint
     are handled. Rules within the same policy share the same failure behavior

when runing a CPOL with image verification, we expect it to ignore underlying transient errors that could create deadlines and cancelations errors, but that's not actually the case because we're only checking for network errors.

This PR allows the `failurePolicy` to work correctly for this kind of uses cases. It also add useful debug logs to understand if underlying errors are being caused by the shared context of a given policy (all containers should validate in the span of the webhook timeout, but in case of network latencies, etc that could be an issue)


## Related issue

## Proposed Changes

Check for `Canceled` and `DeadlineExceeded` errors when handling images (instead of just network errors). If it happens, sends a `RuleError` (same behaviour than network errors)

title: Expose Standard Workqueue Metrics for Kyverno Controllers
author: atharrva01
head: atharrva01:feat/workqueue-metrics
action: Retarget -> release-1.19 (rebase onto release-1.19)
body:
While debugging controller behavior, I noticed Kyverno wasn’t exposing standard Kubernetes workqueue metrics like other operators do. That made it difficult to tell whether queues were backing up or if processing was simply slow.

This PR adds metrics such as `workqueue_depth`, `workqueue_adds_total`, `workqueue_queue_duration_seconds`, and `workqueue_retries_total` to the `/metrics` endpoint for all four controller binaries.

### What changed

1. **Enabled workqueue metrics registration**
   Added blank imports in each controller entrypoint so the workqueue collectors register at startup.

2. **Updated `/metrics` handler**
   Switched from `promhttp.Handler()` to `legacyregistry.Handler()`. Workqueue metrics were registering in the component-base registry, but Kyverno’s endpoint only exposed the default Prometheus registry, so they never appeared in scrapes. This change exposes both through one endpoint.

3. **Handled re-registration during config refresh**
   Kyverno can recreate its Prometheus exporter during live config refreshes. Since old collectors weren’t unregistered, repeated setup caused duplicate registration errors. `swappableRegisterer` safely replaces the old collector so refreshes continue to work.

4. **Dependency update**
   Promoted `k8s.io/component-base` to a direct dependency since it’s now explicitly imported.

### Testing

* Added unit tests for `swappableRegisterer`
* Added test for calling `NewPrometheusConfig()` twice (refresh simulation)
* `go vet` and `go test ./pkg/metrics/...` pass

### Notes

No changes to policy evaluation, admission, or generate behavior. Only the metrics endpoint is affected.

title: fix(cli/apply): use namespace from flag for manifests without namespace
author: sysedwinistrator
head: sysedwinistrator:cli-apply-use-namespace
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

<!--
In a couple sentences, explain why this PR is needed and what it addresses. This should be an explanation a non-developer user can understand and covers the "why" question. It should also clearly indicate whether this PR represents an addition, a change, or a fix of existing behavior. This explanation will be used to assist in the release note drafting process.

THIS IS MANDATORY.
-->

While it is considered best practice to always explicitly include .metadata.namespace in the manifests for namespaced resources - for example, by using "{{ .Release.Namespace }}" in Helm charts - it isn't always done, because it isn't strictly necessary to deploy to the correct namespace.

When a manifest for a namespaced resource doesn't include the namespace, kubectl (and other tools using it, like Helm and ArgoCD) first tries the namespace passed to the CLI (-n/--namespace), then the namespace configured on the context, and only then falls back to "default".

Therefore, kyverno apply should follow the same behavior, and use the -n/--namespace flag to inject the namespace into manifests that don't set one (until this commit, the flag was only used when applying kyverno policies against live resources on a cluster).

To keep the impact minimal, the fallback namespace parameter falls back to "default" when set to an empty string, and only the ResourceFetcher used by the apply and test CLI commands sets it to a non-empty string - if a namespace was passed as a command line flag.

The test verifies exactly this behavior: for a Pod manifest that doesn't specify a namespace, and a ClusterPolicy that disallows the usage of the "default" namespace (at least for some resources including Pods), the policy will pass when running kyverno apply with the namespace flag set, and fail if running it without it (because the "default" namespace is used in that case).

## Proposed Changes

<!--

***NOTE***: If this PR results in new or altered behavior which is user facing, you **MUST** read and follow the steps outlined in the [PR documentation guide](pr_documentation.md) and add Proof Manifests as defined below.
-->

1. Prior to this PR, when running `kyverno apply` against a (or multiple) manifest for a namespaced resource that doesn't include `.metadata.namespace`, kyverno would **always** inject `default` as the namespace

For example, this Pod manifest:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myapp-pod
  labels:
    app: myapp
spec: 
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.12
```

Would be patched to look like this before the policies are applied:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myapp-pod
  namespace: default
  labels:
    app: myapp
spec: 
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.12
```

2. This PR changes the behavior to use the namespace from the `-n`/`--namespace` CLI flag instead of `default` if the CLI flag is set. When running `kyverno apply -n myapp-namespace <path to policies> <path to pod manifest>`, the resulting manifest would be this one:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myapp-pod
  namespace: myapp-namespace
  labels:
    app: myapp
spec: 
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.12
```

This helps in scenarios where the manifests don't (always) include a namespace, but are applied (via kubectl or tools based on it) against a specific namespace (other than default) - by aligning the behavior of `kyverno apply -n <namespace>` with `kubectl apply -n <namespace>`.

title: feat(reports): respect webhook namespace/object selectors in background scan
author: atharrva01
head: atharrva01:feat/webhook-selector-background-scan
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body: ## Summary I worked on **#9356** to make the background scan respect the webhook `namespaceSelector` and `objectSelector`. Right now the reports controller scans everything, even namespaces/resources that the admission webhook never touches. That felt inconsistent. So I added an opt-in flag to align background scans with the webhook scope. --- ## What I added ### New flag ``` --backgroundScanRespectsWebhookSelector (default: false) ``` When enabled, the reports controller checks the webhook selectors from `data.webhooks` and skips resources that wouldn’t be processed by the webhook. --- ### Controller changes I added two small helpers: * `isNamespaceExcludedByWebhookSelector` * `isObjectExcludedByWebhookSelector` They evaluate labels against the webhook’s `NamespaceSelector` / `ObjectSelector`. In `reconcile()`, I added guards before policy loading: * If a namespace or object is excluded, I delete any stale EphemeralReport and return early. * This avoids unnecessary policy evaluation. --- ## Tests I added unit tests covering: * Nil selectors * Matching and non-matching labels * NotIn matchExpressions * Missing namespaces * Empty selectors / empty labels All tests pass. --- Let me know if you'd like me to adjust the flag naming or placement of the guards.

title: Fix mapping of CRDs from ClusterResource in CLI tests

body:
## Explanation

When writing tests for a CEL-based policy that acts on CRs and providing the CRD through a ClusterResource, the CRD is not correctly mapped, which causes the test to fail with the following error:

```
Error: failed to run test (failed to apply policies on resource <resource> (failed to map gvk to gvr <group>/<version>, Kind=<Kind> (no matches for kind "<Kind>" in version "<group>/<version>")
```

It appears to be due to the following:
1. We build a RESTMapper at [cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go#L200]( https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/b986dc8cf62edfd4712ee3980705f547c72fe196/cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go#L200) but don't do anything with it.
2. PolicyProcessor build gets its own RESTMapper at [cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go#L251](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/b986dc8cf62edfd4712ee3980705f547c72fe196/cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go#L251), thus obtaining the default built-in RESTMapper which doesn't contain the CRD.
3. The policy fails because the CRD is considered unknown when looked up through the RESTMapper..

## Related issue

Closes #15384

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.17.2

## Documentation (required for features)

N/A

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go`: Add an optional `RESTMapper meta.RESTMapper` field to `PolicyProcessor`.
  - When set, it is used directly.
  - When nil, the RESTMapper is obtained through `utils.GetRESTMapper` as it was before, preserving the existing logic.
- `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go`: Accumulate the loaded CRDs, build the RESTMapper and pass it to `PolicyProcessor`. Also pass it down to `applyDeletingPolicies` and `applyImageValidatingPolicies`.

title: feat: add fine-grained CEL exceptions (Images/AllowedValues) for MutatingPolicy
author: JagjeevanAK
head: JagjeevanAK:jagjeevan/issue-13654
action: Keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR adds support for fine-grained CEL-based PolicyExceptions (`Images` and `AllowedValues` fields) for MutatingPolicy (mpol). Previously, mpol exceptions only supported full-skip behavior. With this change, exception data is injected into CEL variable expressions via `exceptions.allowedImages` and `exceptions.allowedValues`, allowing policies to make conditional mutation decisions based on exception-permitted images and values.

Key implementation details:
- Uses `cel.DynType` with `map[string]any` to inject exception data through the `compositionContext` variables, working around the incompatibility between `ext.NativeTypes` and the upstream `CompositedCompiler`
- Fixes logic bugs in `matchExceptions` (inverted `DeepEqual` check, incorrect append placement inside inner loop, struct-to-pointer conversion for request)
- Updates `BuildMutatingAdmissionPolicy` to generate MAP variables for fine-grained exceptions

## Related issue

Closes #13654


## Proposed Changes

1. **`pkg/cel/policies/mpol/compiler/compiler.go`** — Declare `exceptions` as `cel.DynType` variable in the mpol CEL environment
2. **`pkg/cel/policies/mpol/compiler/policy.go`** — Inject `exceptions` data (`allowedImages`/`allowedValues`) as `map[string]any` through `compositionContext`; fix `matchExceptions` logic bugs
3. **`pkg/cel/policies/mpol/compiler/policy_test.go`** — Fix and add unit tests for `matchExceptions` (empty match conditions, false-breaks-loop)
4. **`pkg/admissionpolicy/builder.go`** — Handle fine-grained exceptions in MAP generation (create `allowedImages`/`allowedValues` variables, replace `exceptions.*` references with `variables.*`)
5. **CLI tests** — `exceptions-exclude-images` and `exceptions-allow-specific-values` test directories
6. **Chainsaw conformance tests** — `exclude-images` and `allow-specific-values` test directories

### Proof Manifests

CLI tests can be run with:
```bash
kubectl-kyverno test test/cli/test-mutating-policy/exceptions-exclude-images
kubectl-kyverno test test/cli/test-mutating-policy/exceptions-allow-specific-values
```

All 9 mpol CLI tests pass (including the 2 new fine-grained + 3 existing tests).

body:
Fixes: #14332

## Explanation

Attestation data fetched in `verifyImages` was lost after the rule finished because the engine restores the context checkpoint immediately. This PR adds a [Persist](cci:1://file:///e:/opensource/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/context.go:115:1-116:21) mechanism to [JSONContext](cci:1://file:///e:/opensource/kyverno/pkg/engine/api/policycontext.go:29:1-29:38) so named variables can survive context restoration and be used in later rules.

## Related issue

Closes #14332

## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.14.0

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

- Introduced [Persist](cci:1://file:///e:/opensource/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/context.go:115:1-116:21) in [JSONContext](cci:1://file:///e:/opensource/kyverno/pkg/engine/api/policycontext.go:29:1-29:38) to mark keys that should survive restoration.
- Updated the image verifier to mark attestation results as persistent.
- Added [pkg/engine/attestation_context_test.go](cci:7://file:///e:/opensource/kyverno/pkg/engine/attestation_context_test.go:0:0-0:0) to cover cross-rule variable persistence.

### Proof Manifests

# Kubernetes resource
```yaml

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: main
      image: ghcr.io/kyverno/test-verify-image:signed
```

# Kyverno Policy
```yaml

kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: attestation-persistence
spec:
  rules:
    - name: verify-image
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: ["Pod"]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences: ["ghcr.io/kyverno/test-verify-image:*"]
          attestations:
            - name: myAttestation
              type: [https://example.com/CodeReview/v1](https://example.com/CodeReview/v1)
              attestors:
                - entries:
                    - keys:
                        publicKeys: |-
                          -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
                          MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAE8nXRh950IZbRj8Ra/N9sbqOPZrfM
                          5/KAQN0/KjHcorm/J5yctVd7iEcnessRQjU917hmKO6JWVGHpDguIyakZA==
                          -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
    - name: validate-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: ["Pod"]
      validate:
        message: "Attestation data was successfully persisted."
        deny:
          conditions:
            - key: "{{ myAttestation.author }}"
```

body:
### Summary
This PR fixes a bug in the background generate controller where generated resources from **earlier rules** in a multi-rule generate policy were **overwritten** instead of accumulated. As a result, only the resources generated by the **last rule** were recorded in the UpdateRequest status.

---

### Problem
In `ProcessUR`, the slice used to track generated resources (`genResources`) was reassigned on each iteration of the rule-processing loop:

```
go
genResources, err = c.applyGenerate(...)

```
Because of this:
	•	Each rule overwrote the results from the previous rule
	•	Only the last rule’s generated resources were persisted in ur.Status.GeneratedResources

Earlier rules still created resources successfully, but those resources were not tracked.

---

### Impact

This caused several serious issues:
	1.	Orphaned resources
Cleanup logic relies on ur.Status.GeneratedResources.
Resources generated by earlier rules were never deleted and remained permanently orphaned.
	2.	Security risk
Stale Secrets, ConfigMaps, NetworkPolicies, etc. could persist indefinitely after a policy or trigger was removed.
	3.	Silent failure
The UpdateRequest completed successfully with no warnings or errors, giving false confidence that all generated resources were managed correctly.
	4.	Affects all multi-rule generate policies
Any generate policy with two or more rules was impacted.

---

### Fix

The fix changes the logic to accumulate generated resources instead of overwriting them.

A temporary slice is used for each rule, and the results are appended to the accumulator:

ruleResources, err := c.applyGenerate(...)
genResources = append(genResources, ruleResources...)

This ensures that all resources generated by all rules are tracked.

---

### Result After Fix
	•	All generated resources from every rule are recorded in ur.Status.GeneratedResources
	•	Cleanup correctly deletes all generated resources
	•	No orphaned resources remain
	•	Generate behavior now matches user expectations

---

### Scope & Compatibility
	•	✅ No API changes
	•	✅ No behavior change beyond correcting the bug
	•	✅ Backward compatible
	•	✅ Minimal, low-risk fix

---

### Files Changed
	•	pkg/background/generate/controller.go
	•	Function: ProcessUR

---

### Notes

This issue was caused by a simple overwrite vs. accumulation mistake when collecting results in a loop. The fix follows idiomatic Go patterns and preserves existing controller behavior while correcting resource tracking.

title: fix: add subPath support to global.caCertificates.volume
author: hiirrxnn
head: hiirrxnn:fix/helm-cacert-subpath
action: Keep on main (verify after legacy removal lands)
body:
### Explanation

This PR fixes a bug where users could not mount a specific file from a Secret for the CA certificate bundle when using `global.caCertificates.volume`. Previously, the entire Secret was mounted as a directory, causing applications expecting a single file to fail.

This fix introduces a new `subPath` configuration option in the Helm chart `values.yaml`, allowing the volume mount to point to a specific file (for example, `ca.crt`) while correctly preserving the volume source definition.

---

### Related Issue

Closes #14615

---

### Milestone of this PR

Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior to Kyverno.

* [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update the documentation at [https://github.com/kyverno/website](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:

---

### What type of PR is this?

```
/kind bug
```

---

### Proposed Changes

**values.yaml**

* Added `global.caCertificates.volume.subPath` (defaults to empty string).

**Templates**

* Updated:

  * `admission-controller`
  * `background-controller`
  * `reports-controller` deployment templates.

**Logic**

* Added conditional logic to include `subPath` in the container `volumeMounts` only when it is defined in values.
* Used `omit . "subPath"` when rendering the volume source to ensure the `subPath` key is excluded from the volume definition (preventing Kubernetes validation errors).

---

### Proof Manifests

Verified using `helm template`.

#### 1. Default Behavior (No Regression)

**Command**

```bash
helm template kyverno charts/kyverno -n kyverno | grep -C 5 "ca-store"
```

**Result (Volume mounts without subPath)**

```yaml
volumeMounts:
  - mountPath: /.sigstore
    name: sigstore
  - name: ca-store
    mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
```

---

#### 2. With subPath Enabled

**Command**

```bash
helm template kyverno charts/kyverno -n kyverno \
  --set global.caCertificates.volume.subPath="my-ca.crt" | grep -C 5 "ca-store"
```

**Result (Correctly adds subPath)**

```yaml
volumeMounts:
  - mountPath: /.sigstore
    name: sigstore
  - name: ca-store
    mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
    subPath: my-ca.crt
```

---

  [https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: fix: wildcard-policy-new-cr-match
author: roandudel
head: roandudel:fix/wildcard-policy-new-cr-match
action: Manual review: split into 2 PRs or keep on main
body:
## Explanation

This PR fixes a bug where policies with wildcard resource matching `(*/*/*)` do not apply to custom resources when the CRD is created after the policy.

The problem: When Kyverno creates a policy before the CRD exists, it caches the policy without knowing about that resource type. When the CRD is later created, the policy cache is not updated, so the policy never matches resources of that CRD - until Kyverno is restarted.

The fix: When a CRD is added, updated, or deleted, the policy cache controller now re-evaluates all policies with the updated discovery information.

## Related issue

Closes #14325

## Milestone of this PR

## Documentation (required for features)

This is a bug fix, no documentation changes required.

## What type of PR is this

/kind bug

## Proposed Changes

The policy cache controller now subscribes to CRD change events via the existing `OnChanged` callback mechanism in the discovery client. When a `CRD` is added, updated, or deleted, all policies are re-queued and re-processed with the updated discovery cache. This ensures that policies using wildcard matching correctly apply to custom resources even when the `CRD` is created after the policy.

Changes:

* Added `requeueAllPolicies()` method to the policy cache controller
* Registered callback `client.Discovery().OnChanged(c.requeueAllPolicies)` in `NewController()`
* Added conformance e2e test to verify the fix

### Proof Manifests

Chainsaw end2end test is added

## Explanation

Add validation for condition types.

## Related issue

Fixes https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/13546

## Milestone of this PR

1.15

## Documentation (required for features)

  <!-- Uncomment to link to the PR -->
  <!-- https://github.com/kyverno/website/pull/123 -->

## What type of PR is this

 /kind bug

## Proposed Changes

Return parse / validation errors when a condition:
1. Has invalid (extra) fields
2. Is missing a key
3. Is missing a value
4. Is missing the operator

### Proof Manifests

This policy was allowed prior to changes:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: check-configmaps
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Check ConfigMaps Exist
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Best Practices
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Check for existence of referenced ConfigMaps
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: validate-configmap-exists
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Deployment
            - StatefulSet
            - Job
      validate:
        message: "Referenced ConfigMap must exist"
        foreach:
        - list: "request.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[*].configMap.name"
          deny:
            conditions:
              - key: "configMap"
                operator: Equals
                value: null
                apiCall:
                  apiVersion: v1
                  kind: ConfigMap
                  name: "{{ element }}"
```

Now it is blocked:

```sh
k apply -f /tmp/policy.yaml
Error from server: error when creating "/tmp/policy.yaml": admission webhook "validate-policy.kyverno.svc" denied the request: json: unknown field "apiCall"
```

Here is a unit test case added:

https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/compare/main...JimBugwadia:kyverno:improve_cpol_condition_validation?expand=1#diff-4811dd610286bf5874e97e728413d7e29cbaf91e6ca13c0eb64f33f913561b3eR3479
